summary: Complementarity-First Foundational Release III develops reciprocal phase architecture, conditional gauge and incidence geometry, finite Lorentzian connection selection, and relational quantum-information tasks. This paper synthesizes the eight research preprints and one reproducibility dataset in Waves A–C without transferring theorem ownership or treating their separately admitted carriers as a single derived physical system. The release is organized by four distinctions: structural admission versus conditional selection; geometric covariance versus operational implementation; restricted agreement versus complete identification; and mathematical existence versus a resource-accounted realization. The reciprocal quantum construction separates local inclusion, coherent completion, entanglement, finite projective valuation, and individual outcomes. Its synthetic biphoton companion distinguishes image intensity from phase-sensitive entanglement evidence. The geometric papers distinguish a derived compact phase-frame type from electromagnetic gauge interpretation and constitutive dynamics, anti-linear opposite-weight pairing from same-bundle reversal, an indefinite incidence form from positive records, and geometric-section agreement from independent connection variation. The Wave C papers supply finite addressing classifications, task- and record-relative recovery, encoded-preparation advantages, and exact exchange constructions with trajectory and timing bounds. Cross-wave comparisons locate genuine imported interfaces and identify bridges that remain absent, including the passage from finite Born-form valuation to general instruments and from a recorded group-error model to a physical timing-error model. Analytic proofs, finite calculations, numerical certificates, recorded replays, and scoped Lean verification are assigned distinct evidentiary roles. The contribution is a source-attributed scientific synthesis and an explicit dependency and residual-premise map, not a new primitive derivation of quantum theory, electromagnetism, or gravity.

summary: Reader Agency and the Recovery of Permutation Structure Fixed Cuts, Iteration, and Movable Cuts   Driven by Dean A. Kulik · September 2026   Abstract A permutation   of   cells is observed through a cut : the cells are divided into blocks and only the block-to-block counts are reported. A single such reading leaves a large set of permutations indistinguishable. We compare three ways of learning more: reading repeatedly as   iterates, refining the cut, and moving the cut while keeping its coarseness fixed. For balanced two-block cuts the whole table is determined by one number, the count of cells that stay in the first block. That number depends only on the underlying undirected edges of , so reversing the orientation of any subset of ’s cycles leaves every balanced two-block reading unchanged, for every cut and every . The group of such reversals is , where   counts the cycles of length at least three, so its orbits have size . We measure what each capability recovers. For , a fixed two-block reader watching all fifteen powers of   leaves   bits hidden and never determines the cycle type. The same reader taking a single reading, but allowed to place its cut in all thirty-five ways, leaves   bits and does determine the cycle type. Adding iteration on top of the movable cut changes nothing at all: both give exactly   classes. So agency dominates duration, and once cuts may move, duration is worth nothing. We prove that for every even   the classes of the movable-cut reader are exactly the cycle-reversal orbits, so the reader recovers the unoriented cycle structure of   and loses precisely the orientations. The result fails for   and , and those are the only exceptions. At   the classes are   singletons,   pairs and   quadruples. We also give the passive causal quotient at several resolutions, where no coarse reader ever determines the cycle type, the number of cycles, or the order of , however long it watches. summary: Generative AI makes it easier for one person to write like another. That familiar observation is only the entry point here. My concern is with what may happen before a sentence appears: the selection of distinctions, the ordering of values, and the judgment by which a person decides that this, rather than something else, is worth saying. I use Person-Anchored Constructivism in the Age of Subjectivity Homogenization for the theory developed in this article. It describes the lifelong formation and re-formation of a Personal Construct Order by a concrete person. Experience, judgment, choice, and responsibility are not four variables added to that order. They are what keep it anchored in the person whose order it is. Subjectivity Homogenization names the condition in which shared forms of expression or evaluation begin to take over that constructive work. I distinguish three places at which this may happen: expression, judgment, and the order governing a person's constructs. To make this distinction, I draw on personal construct psychology, research on writing as thinking, reflexivity, and participatory sense-making. I also separate the Personal Construct System from its ordering dimension, the Personal Construct Order. The process connecting these claims is the Subjectivity Reconstruction Loop: The Concrete Person → Personal Construct Order → Reflexive Construing → Construct Externalization → Intersubjective Loop → Emergence of Discrepancy → Construct Recalibration → Reconstruction of the Person. Repeated completion of that loop constitutes the Individuation of Subjectivity. Eight propositions set out how homogenization, person-anchoring, and reconstruction are related. This record contains the English preprint and a complete Chinese translation.

They are what keep it anchored in the person whose order it is. Subjectivity Homogenization names the condition in which shared forms of expression or evaluation begin to take over that constructive work. I distinguish three places at which this may happen: expression, judgment, and the order governing a person's constructs. To make this distinction, I draw on personal construct psychology, research on writing as thinking, reflexivity, and participatory sense-making. I also separate the Personal Construct System from its ordering dimension, the Personal Construct Order. The process connecting these claims is the Subjectivity Reconstruction Loop: The Concrete Person → Personal Construct Order → Reflexive Construing → Construct Externalization → Intersubjective Loop → Emergence of Discrepancy → Construct Recalibration → Reconstruction of the Person. summary: Background. World-model research raises a compound architectural question: how can an explicit representation of entities, relations, canonical predicates, events, causal dependencies, goals, temporal structure, and memory be maintained under controlled dynamics, checked within a declared logical fragment, and kept task-sufficient without unnecessary complexity? S-AI-WorldModel addresses this question through an explicit canonical representation, regulated update dynamics, computable commitment conditions, and a source-only symbolic reconstruction pipeline. Methods. S-AI-WorldModel is the tenth architectural instantiation of the Sparse Artificial Intelligence paradigm dedicated to world modeling. The world model is formalized as an eight-component cognitive structure comprising entities, relations, canonical predicates, events, causal dependencies, goals, temporal structure, and working memory. Its evolution is governed by a discrete-time world-model operator and a nine-hormone regulatory field combining six hormones inherited from the S-AI corpus with Causine, Temporaline, and Contextine. Nine formal results, WM.0–WM.8, characterize fixed-point existence, convergence, entropy control, coherence safety, computable commitment, finite-time entry into an accepted region, orbit-relative parsimony, and a seven-fold joint guarantee under explicit hypotheses. The implemented source-only action-model pipeline combines ActionParamAgent, PreconditionAgent, EffectAgent, guarded semantic dynamics, structural commit, parse recovery, result-state completion, and precondition anchoring. Experimental results. The final frozen V3.5 pipeline generates and evaluates 101/101 Text2World cases with the official Tarski-based evaluator after pre-GOLD candidate sealing. It reaches 100.00% Executability , 82.997% Levenshtein similarity , 98.008% Predicate F1 , 89.057% Parameter F1 , 60.088% Precondition F1 , and 60.807% Effect F1 . All 101 generated domains parse successfully. For non-matched benchmark positioning, S-AI-WorldModel is numerically above the published DeepSeek-R1 EC0 scores by 27.70 percentage points in Executability , 2.49 points in Precondition F1 , and 2.01 points in Effect F1 [32]. Because Text2World-101 informed development of the S-AI pipeline whereas EC0 is a zero-shot protocol, these differences are published-reference comparisons rather than controlled head-to-head performance margins. The same frozen pipeline was executed locally on a Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon , using a CPU-only symbolic implementation with 0 learned neural parameters . Interpretation. The final profile crosses a clear 100/60/60 frontier : complete executability together with more than 60% F1 on both preconditions and effects. The gain is especially meaningful because preconditions and effects are the Text2World components that require inference of applicability and state-transition semantics from high-level action descriptions. Beyond benchmark reconstruction, S-AI-WorldModel provides a capability envelope that is not jointly supplied by the representative latent world models, object-centric systems, neuro-symbolic frameworks, cognitive architectures, causal approaches, neural-planning systems, and explainability or verification approaches surveyed in Section 2 [1]–[24]: an explicit eight-component typed world model; controlled canonicalization with formal fixed-point and convergence conditions; nine-hormone metacognitive regulation; computable symbolic commitment over a declared decidable projection; explicit task adequacy; planning exploitability; task-relative parsimony; and auditable symbolic transition semantics. These are architectural functions rather than benchmark metrics, so their significance complements the Text2World scores. Section 2.9 extends the comparison to representative 2024–2026 predictive, symbolic, graph-based, planning, and verification-oriented world-model systems [35]–[46] and narrows the novelty claim according
title: S-AI-WorldModel: A Canonical Cognitive Architecture for World Modeling

summary: A corpus of 219,386 Indian recipes across 378 source sites, with parsed ingredients in English/Roman, a 17-class allergen surface carrying an explicit unassessed sentinel, and estimated dish-level micronutrition; a typed knowledge graph of 222,539 nodes and 6,428,210 edges across 17 node types and 22 relation types; a 67-query retrieval benchmark with knowledge-graph-derived gold sets; and two synthetic collaborative interaction logs. The food-composition layer uses the IFCT 42-nutrient schema but contains no IFCT and no Indian composition data; its values are USDA SR Legacy and UK CoFID. Two-tier release. Structured, factual and derived fields are published under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with per-recipe source attribution. Raw recipe prose is not redistributed; a rehydration index of source URLs and SHA-256 text digests is published instead, together with a re-fetch script. Known defects are published, not hidden. An independent allergen and diet audit ships with the data. See the datasheet before use, and do not use the allergen flags for end-user safety decisions.
title: IndicRecipeNutri

summary: MusiCoMMA connects the Musiconis vocabulary to a bounded pilot of contexts from a pinned CoMMA manuscript-transcription corpus. Its lexical foundation contains 1,198 entries and 1,548 source-sense records. The pilot covers 50 Latin and Old French entries out of 900 in scope. Version 0.2.1 retains 478 contexts across 378 manuscript digitizations after Xavier Fresquet's targeted review of ten chantre windows: three retained and seven excluded. The seven exclusions and all ten decisions are supplied separately. All 485 original annotation assertions remain alongside ten superseding assertions. Source strings and stable identifiers are unchanged. The active set contains 148 automatic links to a single source sense and 330 contexts with unresolved sense assignment. The package includes CSV, JSONL, RDF/Turtle, JSON-LD, schemas, review provenance, an executed Jupyter notebook, analytical tables, figures, checksums and supporting code. A historical baseline archive is included solely for reconstruction. Pilot-dependent analyses have been rerun; unchanged corpus-exposure denominators are reused with checksum provenance. This is a contextual-selection pilot, not an image-verified transcription corpus or a gold-standard benchmark. No independent annotation, corrected readings, population-level precision or recall estimate is claimed. Seven exclusions do not establish seven recognition errors. No manuscript images or bulk CoMMA files are redistributed. Source vocabulary: Musiconis, Sorbonne Université, with explicit credit to Frédéric Billiet and Xavier Fresquet. Source corpus: CoMMA, by Thibault Clérice, Simon Gabay, Malamatenia Vlachou-Efstathiou, Ariane Pinche and Benoît Sagot (2025), HAL hal-05299220v2, https://inria.hal.science/hal-05299220v2. CoMMA-derived material has been extracted, matched, restructured and contextually selected; no institutional endorsement is implied. Data, documentation and analysis outputs: CC BY 4.0. Scripts and executable notebook code: MIT, as stated in LICENSE-CODE. Research and teaching are the intended uses, without an additional non-commercial restriction. Source-owner authorization for Musiconis and Frédéric Billiet's agreement to deposit were recorded through Xavier Fresquet on 12 September 2026. Linked images remain subject to their providers' conditions.
title: MusiCoMMA v0.2.1: Musiconis Vocabulary and Context-Reviewed CoMMA Pilot

summary: Complementarity-First Foundational Release III develops reciprocal phase architecture, conditional gauge and incidence geometry, finite Lorentzian connection selection, and relational quantum-information tasks. This paper synthesizes the eight research preprints and one reproducibility dataset in Waves A–C without transferring theorem ownership or treating their separately admitted carriers as a single derived physical system. The release is organized by four distinctions: structural admission versus conditional selection; geometric covariance versus operational implementation; restricted agreement versus complete identification; and mathematical existence versus a resource-accounted realization. The reciprocal quantum construction separates local inclusion, coherent completion, entanglement, finite projective valuation, and individual outcomes. Its synthetic biphoton companion distinguishes image intensity from phase-sensitive entanglement evidence. The geometric papers distinguish a derived compact phase-frame type from electromagnetic gauge interpretation and constitutive dynamics, anti-linear opposite-weight pairing from same-bundle reversal, an indefinite incidence form from positive records, and geometric-section agreement from independent connection variation. The Wave C papers supply finite addressing classifications, task- and record-relative recovery, encoded-preparation advantages, and exact exchange constructions with trajectory and timing bounds. Cross-wave comparisons locate genuine imported interfaces and identify bridges that remain absent, including the passage from finite Born-form valuation to general instruments and from a recorded group-error model to a physical timing-error model. Analytic proofs, finite calculations, numerical certificates, recorded replays, and scoped Lean verification are assigned distinct evidentiary roles. The contribution is a source-attributed scientific synthesis and an explicit dependency and residual-premise map, not a new primitive derivation of quantum theory, electromagnetism, or gravity.

summary: MR scans of a human, adult brain at 3T in BIDS format. Includes DICOMS and derived/preprocessed output of FreeSurfer, fmriprep and qsirecon. The scans were acquired on a Siemens Magnetom Prisma running syngo MR E11. See the BIDS metadata for more details. All data in this repo is based on the following sets of DICOM files: `0001_MR*.dcm` | 3 files | **Localizer / Scout** | 3-plane anatomical reference for scanner slice positioning (discard or omit from analysis). `0002_MR*.dcm` | 192 slices | **Structural T1-weighted (T1w)** | 1mm isotropic 3D MPRAGE; primary anatomical volume for cortical reconstruction and tissue segmentation. `0003_MR*.dcm` | 192 slices | **Structural T2-weighted (T2w)** | 1mm 3D Turbo Spin Echo (TSE); standard T2 contrast showing CSF hyperintensity. `0004_MR*.dcm` | 192 slices | **Structural T2-weighted (iPAT 3D)** | 1mm 3D T2 TSE with parallel imaging acceleration (`iPAT`). `0005_MR*.dcm` | 240 volumes | **Resting-State fMRI (rs-fMRI BOLD)** | 2D EPI BOLD time series (3mm resolution, 240 volumes) measuring spontaneous low-frequency BOLD fluctuations during rest. `0006_MR*.dcm` | 72 files | **Diffusion MRI (DWI / DTI)** | 2mm 2D EPI diffusion-weighted sequence; multiple diffusion directions/b-values for tractography and tensor estimation. `0007_MR*.dcm` | 72 slices | **DWI Fieldmap / $b=0$ Reference (Pair A)** | Single 3D reference volume for susceptibility distortion correction (e.g., FSL `topup`). `0008_MR*.dcm` | 72 slices | **DWI Fieldmap / $b=0$ Reference (Pair B)** | Complementary reverse phase-encode reference volume for `topup`. | These raw files are available in the `raw/` directory in `bids-base-DICOM.zip`. Description of the files that are distributed in this dataset: bids-base-DICOM.zip: raw DICOM images in a flat directory under `raw/`, and the same data organized in BIDS structure, with metadata, under `bids/` bids-derivatives-freesurfer-6.0.zip: Freesurfer 6.0 recon-all output for the subject. After a first run, minor manual edits to dura detection were applied, then re-processed. bids-derivates-freesurfer-7.4.1.zip: Freesurfer 7.4.1 recon-all output for the subject, unedited. bids-derivates-freesurfer-8.2.0.zip: Freesurfer 8.2.0 recon-all output for the subject, unedited. bids-derivatives-fmriprep.zip: fmriprep output for the subject bids-derivatives-qsiprep-qsirecon.zip: qsirecon output for the subject sub-01_space-ACPC_model-ifod2_streamlines.tck.gz: a single 8.9 GB file, part of the qsirecon output but distributed separately to avoid issues with large zip files. Once you have downloaded and extracted bids-derivatives-qsiprep-qsirecon.zip, copy this into the resulting directory `./bids/derivatives/qsirecon/derivatives/qsirecon-MRtrix3_fork-SS3T_act-HSVS/sub-01/dwi/` These data were created by Tim Schäfer, Carolin Mann, Anke Bletsch in Christine Ecker's Lab at Goethe University Hospital, Frankfurt am Main, Germany. We distribute this data to make available reference files for many file formats used in neuroimaging under a very open license, e.g., for software testing.
title: MR scans of a human, adult brain at 3T in BIDS format. Includes DICOMS, preprocessed output of FreeSurfer, fmriprep and qsirecon.

summary: Sanitized code and data reproducibility package for a manuscript currently under double-blind review at the Journal of Information Security and Applications. Author identity is withheld pending the outcome of review. The package contains two independently generated archives: (1) model-I-single-branch/ — a single clock-controlled ternary LFSR generator over GF(3) (controller LFSR A + data LFSR B), together with its exact period and design-condition checkers, a statistical analysis suite, a 14-family ternary long-sequence test battery, and a cryptanalytic attack suite (basic correlation, embedding, fast correlation, Berlekamp-Massey reconstruction, and a linear-consistency/clock-control attack). Includes all 40 archived experiment runs across 8 controller/data degree configurations. (2) model-II-three-branch/ — a three-branch clock-controlled generator over GF(3) combined through a quadratic nonlinear ternary function, together with period/design analysis, algebraic/spectral characterization of the combiner, an aggregate statistical pipeline, avalanche diffusion experiments, a matched attack suite, and an exact key-stream-reuse detector. A full SHA-256 manifest (MANIFEST_SHA256.tsv) and verification script (verify_checksums.py) are included to allow integrity checking of every file. See README.md for directory structure, provenance notes, a documented anonymity sanitization log, and instructions to reproduce all reported results. See CORRESPONDENCE.md for a mapping between source files and the tables/figures of the manuscript. Source code (*.py, *.bat) is released under the MIT License. Generated data, results, logs, CSV aggregates, and figures are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
title: Reproducibility package for "Clock-Controlled Ternary Sequence Generators over GF(3): Exact Periods, Statistical Structure, and Cryptanalytic Comparison of Single-Branch and Three-Branch Nonlinear Architectures"

The package contains two independently generated archives: (1) model-I-single-branch/ — a single clock-controlled ternary LFSR generator over GF(3) (controller LFSR A + data LFSR B), together with its exact period and design-condition checkers, a statistical analysis suite, a 14-family ternary long-sequence test battery, and a cryptanalytic attack suite (basic correlation, embedding, fast correlation, Berlekamp-Massey reconstruction, and a linear-consistency/clock-control attack). Includes all 40 archived experiment runs across 8 controller/data degree configurations. (2) model-II-three-branch/ — a three-branch clock-controlled generator over GF(3) combined through a quadratic nonlinear ternary function, together with period/design analysis, algebraic/spectral characterization of the combiner, an aggregate statistical pipeline, avalanche diffusion experiments, a matched attack suite, and an exact key-stream-reuse detector. A full SHA-256 manifest (MANIFEST_SHA256.tsv) and verification script (verify_checksums.py) are included to allow integrity checking of every file. See README.md for directory structure, provenance notes, a documented anonymity sanitization log, and instructions to reproduce all reported results. See CORRESPONDENCE.md for a mapping between source files and the tables/figures of the manuscript. Source code (*.py, *.bat) is released under the MIT License. Generated data, results, logs, CSV aggregates, and figures are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).

summary: Abstract Let ρ₅ᴿ be the largest element growth possible in exact Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting on real 5 × 5 matrices, with every legal choice at a pivot tie allowed. We prove ρ₅ᴿ = α = 4.132517078632472854223346853277…, where α is the algebraic lower bound identified by Chen, Edelman, and Urschel, specified by their degree-61 polynomial and a rational isolating interval. Our contribution is the global upper bound. An exact inverse-elimination representation retains all initial and intermediate entry bounds of the same matrix. A constructive contraction preserves the final-pivot height while reducing the problem to two saturated tail geometries. On the negative-diagonal geometry, three feasible paths eliminate six variables and give an attained fibre maximum over seventeen shared parameters. Rational certificates control the remaining domains, while a constrained algebraic maximum argument and feasible transports resolve regions meeting the sharp value. The proof combines these analytic reductions with exact verification of a finite, complete cover. We provide a partial Lean formalization together with publicly available exact certificates and verification code. Files and supporting materials This record contains the 56-page manuscript and its 7-page supplementary index. Both PDFs are archived unchanged from the fixed GitHub release v1.0.1. The supplementary index maps proof responsibilities S1–S8 to the original proof objects and verifier entry points. Source code, exact certificates, verification guides and file manifests are available at GitHub release v1.0.1 . The original certificate assets remain frozen under v1.0.0 and are linked from that release. Formalization scope The recorded first-phase Lean project cold rebuild passed 634 product modules, three additional example/audit modules and 47 named axiom checks, using an explicit dependency-order driver with pinned third-party caches reused and supplemented. The final sharp Lean equality remains conditional on XGlobalSafety and RootEndpointSafety. This is a partial Lean formalization accompanying the computer-assisted proof; neither a complete unconditional Lean proof nor formal verification of the Python/C++ acceptor implementations is claimed. The frozen PDFs retain the publication-status wording at the time of their GitHub release; this Zenodo record supplies their archival deposit.

summary: The translation of emotional language in literary discourse involves not only the transfer of lexical meaning but also the reconstruction of emotional intensity, evaluative connotation, psychological stance, and pragmatic effect. The present study investigates lexical-emotional transformations in the Arabic translation of Abdulla Qodiriy’s novel O‘tkan kunlar, published in Arabic as Al-Ayyām al-Khawālī ( الأيام الخوالي ) in 2024. The research is based on a comparative linguopragmatic analysis of emotionally marked units selected from the Uzbek source text and their Arabic correspondences. The examples were examined according to three interrelated parameters: semantic content, emotional intensity, and pragmatic function. The analysis revealed several recurrent patterns, including direct emotional correspondence, grammatical recategorization, semantic-pragmatic attenuation, preservation of emotional intensity, contextual specification, and metaphorical-emotional recreation. The findings demonstrate that lexical-semantic equivalence does not necessarily guarantee an equivalent emotional effect. In some cases, Arabic preserves both the type and intensity of the source emotion; in others, the emotional meaning is attenuated or conceptually reorganized. Conversely, metaphorical emotion may be successfully recreated through a different but functionally corresponding lexical image. The study therefore argues that emotional translation should be assessed beyond lexical equivalence by considering the degree to which the target text reconstructs the emotional and pragmatic potential of the source expression.

summary: Patinae v0.5.0 Zawinski's law says that programs keep expanding until they can read email. Patinae started as a molecular viewer. It now has background tasks, Markdown output, and an AI plugin that can connect to MCP servers. We appear to be one mail server away from compliance. The largest change in 0.5.0 is underneath all of that: the task system has been completely rebuilt around one shared lifecycle . Loading a structure, running a script, and asking a plugin to do background work now use the same rules for completion, progress, errors, and cancellation. Those rules extend across the desktop application, native plugins, IPC, Python, and the web viewer. That gives plugins the foundation for longer workflows. A plugin can issue a command, receive its actual result, wait for any background work it starts, and decide what to do next. The new AI plugin puts that into practice: ask for a scene in ordinary language, let the agent operate Patinae, and have it inspect the rendered image before answering. Highlights A task has one lifecycle, wherever it starts Background work now receives a host-assigned task ID and stays under the shared task runner's control. Progress, diagnostics, final outcomes, and cancellation requests belong to that task. The desktop shows active tasks with progress and cancellation controls, and services background work independently of rendering. The distinction between accepting a command and finishing its work is explicit. An immediate command returns its result. A command that starts background work also returns task IDs, which clients can observe, wait for, or cancel. Success means the required scene changes have been applied; it does not promise that the GPU has already presented a frame. Scripts and plugin workflows can create child tasks. A parent stays active until its children finish, and cancellation propagates through the task tree. Cancelling stops further work cooperatively; changes already applied to the scene remain. A wait timeout ends the wait without cancelling the underlying task. Python command methods wait for background work by default, so a script can fetch a structure and then operate on it. Use wait=False to get task IDs immediately and manage them through tasks or a notebook viewer's view.tasks . Browser integrations receive command results and use viewer.tasks.get , list , wait , and cancel to follow the same lifecycle. Plugins can coordinate work and recover from errors Plugins now receive typed replies to the host commands they issue, correlated to the original request and delivered only to the requesting plugin. Replies include success or failure, output messages, and every accepted task ID. A command can fail after starting some work, so those IDs remain available for inspection. For plugin authors, the new contract separates responsibilities clearly: The host owns task identity and state. A plugin submits a task request and starts its worker after the host accepts it and delivers the assigned ID. Workers report progress, output, and completion. Scene mutations go through the host and must be acknowledged before the plugin reports success. Nested commands belong to the parent task. Their completion and cancellation participate in the same lifecycle. Recovery can be deliberate. Child failure fails the parent by default. An executor can opt into deciding the parent outcome after inspecting and handling a failed child. The original failure remains in task history. This matters for an agent that needs to correct a command, or a script that has a fallback when a download fails. The parent can handle the error and continue while preserving the record of what happened. Silent execution also follows the task tree. It suppresses REPL presentation while retaining results, diagnostics, and logs, so a plugin can handle intermediate failures without filling the output panel with messages it intends to recover from. Polling plugins additionally receive named selections and Recent Atoms path

summary: This manuscript addresses consciousness within this framework by first adopting a specific, defensible philosophical position — dual-aspect monism — after identifying and rejecting two internally contradictory earlier framings, then developing a two-part structural-and-functional criterion for identifying physical systems engaged in unified information processing, anchored to real, independently-published quantitative thresholds. summary: The research paper titled "The Ocean and Spatial Representation in Sangam Literature" by Dr. K. Periya Karuppan examines how the marine ecosystem of the Neithal landscape (ocean and coastal regions) is constructed as a literary and cultural space ( Idanaakkam ) in classical Tamil poetry. Drawing contextual evidence from texts such as Purananuru, Akananuru, Aingurunuru, Natrinai, Paripadal , and the epic Silappathikaram , the study explores the multifaceted thematic functions of the sea. It analyzes the ocean as a metaphorical space for the rising sun, symbolizing a king’s fierce wrath, and as a physical benchmark to measure the profound depth of the hero’s love. The author highlights the realistic environmental depictions of the coast, including the pervasive fishy odor ( Pulal Naatram ) of the waves and drying fish, contrasted with the fragrant Thazhai and Punnai blossoms. Furthermore, the paper looks into the stark demographic contrast between the small, humble coastal hamlets ( Sirugudi ) of the Parathavar community and the immense, vast ocean where their large ships ( Vangam/Thimil ) vanish into the horizon. Lastly, the study maps the sea as a locus for natural phenomenon, like the water cycle, and as a stage for mythological history, notably Murugan's triumph over Surapadman. The paper concludes that Sangam poets seamlessly blended geographic realities with human emotions to transform the physical ocean into a vital psychological space.

summary: This edition presents the current Split-Zero, theta-cohomology and arithmetic-kernel calculations in a research programme on the Riemann zeta function. It publishes the complete 216-page cumulative continuation, the updated 425-page broader research reader, and their proof sources and checks. The purpose is to make the actual calculations readable and reproducible: what was attempted, why that route was chosen, the maps and estimates obtained, and the precise points where the argument remains unfinished. Start with the cumulative calculation reader 14-splitzero-tau-kernel-continuation.pdf is the primary preview. Its 22 proof sections and nine complete source appendices carry the programme from Split-Zero coefficients through theta cohomology, interpolation kernels, chain retractions, homotopy control and the symmetric arithmetic frontier. Earlier source notes retain their own revisions and attribution; the cumulative continuation is not presented as though all its source results originated in one session. Split-Zero coefficients keep the original zero of a ring as a supported element and adjoin a different, external zero, tau. This records the difference between cancelling a coefficient and forgetting the fibre that carried it. Theta cohomology is a specified space of rapidly decreasing functions modulo the image of a specified theta-summation map. Under the stated Mellin transform, that map becomes multiplication by g(s) = 2 xi(s) , where xi is the completed Riemann zeta function. A finite spectral packet records spectral points with their multiplicities, using polynomial quotients and full derivative data rather than discarding repeated-root directions. The calculations construct minimum-norm representatives from the original arithmetic measure, derive full-jet kernel and Gram-inverse formulas, follow nested packets and tensor constructions, and compute the boundary control from the actual theta-derivative sequence. The cumulative reader also develops the relation-layer graph, derivative quotients, norm and Gram-volume identities, and conjugation/reflection-symmetric estimates. Spectral-sum constructions keep the relative variables through matrix weights and complete nilpotent fibres. The quantitative question is how the control form compares with the original arithmetic Gram matrix as the degree and tensor order grow; smallness of one matrix alone is not treated as the required relative estimate. The broader zeta programme 13-main-reader-425p.pdf supplies the surrounding literature reconstruction, CUE random-matrix calculations, arithmetic transforms and source-directed fluid calculations. It includes the all-axis Mellin calculation, complex axial branch points, moving analytic radius and endpoint-residue map for the stated source patch. Those results are described with their source assumptions and maps; they are not recast as a newly constructed zeta-zero witness or an independent proof of the imported fluid existence result. The motivation includes the use of weights in Deligne's Weil II . This programme works out its own analytic spaces, operators, metrics and comparison maps. The complete proofs retain their domains, signs, measures, scalar actions, local units and multiplicities. These are substantive calculations and research attempts, not a claim that an analogy by itself proves or disproves the Riemann hypothesis. Sources, verification and earlier editions 15-current-integrated-sources.zip records the integrated repository snapshot and the broader reader's authored proof dependencies. 16-tandem-continuation-sources.zip preserves the cumulative continuation's separately identified source tree, appendices, build instructions and checks. Their manifests pin the exact revisions and file identities. Written analytic arguments, exact finite checks, numerical enclosures and Lean declarations have distinct stated verification scopes; a check on one interface is not promoted into a certificate for the entire programme. summary: Abstract This paper establishes a rigorous, deterministic framework mapping the non-linear vortex-ring eigen- states and azimuthon transformations of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou (FPUT) recurrence phenomenon onto the continuous, porous hydrodynamic manifold fabric of Tension-Optimized Newtonian Entropy (TONE) Theory. By evaluating multi-dimensional wave propagation and self-trapped rotational flow profiles as real geometric deformations of a flexible spatial grid, we replace the abstract, complexified probability landscapes of standard non-linear optics with localized, causal mechanical actions. Modern fluid dynamics and wave mechanics treat the spontaneous reconstruction of broken wave profiles and azimuthal modulation cycles as a consequence of unphysical point-continuum space-time frameworks, necessitating manual phase adjustments and artificial energy subtractions. This investigation provides a non-parametric refinement of these macroscopic structures by showing that long-lived breathers and near-periodic structural revivals are natural hallmarks of a real-valued coordinate network. Under this framework, the non-linear Schr¨odinger equations with focusing Poisson and cubic terms are re-derived as a physical fluid-wave engine operating across parallel canvas layers embedded in a 10D ambient bulk space borrowed from M-theory. Consequently, the localized topological charge configurations and fluid velocity field vectors act as mechanical sub-manifold deformations, behaving analogously to the Ricci extrinsic curvature description of gravity. Ultimately, the entire phenomenon of macroscopic fluid recur- rence and rotational stability is resolved entirely on a local Newtonian timeline, substituting unphysical imaginary axes with exact, locally real coordinate conservation paths across parallel manifold sheets. summary: Resumo O Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) constitui uma das principais conquistas institucionais do Brasil, ao estabelecer a saúde como direito universal em um país continental e profundamente desigual. Quase quatro décadas após sua criação, o desafio central não é reconstruí-lo, mas transformar sua ampla estrutura em um sistema efetivamente integrado, resolutivo, sustentável e preparado para as mudanças demográficas, epidemiológicas e tecnológicas do século XXI. Essa transformação exige ampliar e qualificar o financiamento público. Em 2024, o gasto governamental em saúde correspondeu a 5,03% do PIB. Entretanto, em 2019, o setor público respondeu por apenas cerca de 40% do gasto total em saúde, enquanto aproximadamente 60% foram financiados por fontes privadas, proporção inversa à observada na maioria dos sistemas universais e muito inferior à média pública de aproximadamente 72% nos países da OCDE. O subfinanciamento transfere custos às famílias, especialmente por meio da compra de medicamentos, mas aumentar recursos sem melhorar a organização não será suficiente. O artigo propõe avançar da descentralização para uma regionalização efetiva, com listas de espera transparentes, compras em escala e integração entre atenção primária, especialistas, hospitais e cuidados domiciliares. A extensa rede territorial do SUS deve assumir maior responsabilidade pela saúde de populações definidas, com capacidade diagnóstica, acompanhamento longitudinal e atuação preventiva. Dados interoperáveis devem ser tratados como infraestrutura pública estratégica. Inteligência artificial, genômica, telessaúde, monitoramento remoto e medicina de precisão somente produzirão valor se forem validados na população brasileira, incorporados a fluxos assistenciais funcionais e avaliados quanto a benefício clínico, custo-efetividade, segurança e equidade. Diante do envelhecimento populacional, o SUS precisa evoluir para um sistema de saúde que aprende continuamente, antecipa riscos, mede resultados, amplia o que funciona e abandona intervenções de baixo valor.   Summary The Brazilian Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde, SUS) is one of Brazil’s most important institutional achievements, establishing health as a universal right in a continental and deeply unequal country. Nearly four decades after its creation, the central challenge is not to rebuild the SUS, but to transform its extensive infrastructure into a genuinely integrated, effective, sustainable system prepared for the demographic, epidemiological, and technological changes of the twenty-first century. This transformation requires both increasing and improving public financing. In 2024, government health expenditure corresponded to 5.03% of GDP. However, in 2019, the public sector accounted for only approximately 40% of total health spending, while around 60% came from private sources—the reverse of the pattern observed in most universal health systems and well below the OECD average public share of approximately 72%. Underfunding shifts healthcare costs to households, particularly through medicine purchases, but increasing resources without improving organization will not be sufficient. The article proposes moving from decentralization toward effective regionalization, supported by transparent waiting lists, procurement at scale, and integration among primary care, specialists, hospitals, and home care. summary: We propose the Encephlian Standard Format (ESF), a 19-channel international 10–20 montage at 250 Hz, average re-referenced, microvolt-calibrated, and channel-wise robust z-scored, as a deterministic canonical representation for deploying pretrained EEG classifiers on heterogeneous acquisition hardware, paired with a recoverability framework that predicts which signal-level shifts ESF can and cannot recover. On the Temple University Abnormal EEG Corpus (TUAB, n = 276 patient-stratified, 253 unique patients), a frozen EEGPT linear probe attains clean AUROC 0.908. We sweep five acquisition-shift axes (native sampling rate, per-channel gain, 50 Hz line noise, electrode montage, and broadband signal-to-noise) and show that left-invertible and bandwidth-preserving operators are (f,0)-recoverable while sub-Nyquist sampling and broadband Gaussian noise are not (Propositions 1, 2). A Pinsker-based AUROC–total-variation bound holds on 18/18 measured axis-arms (median implied constant 0.10). Clustering every recording by its joint behaviour across the sweep yields seven failure categories: 100% of baseline-correct normals flip on at least one shifted cell, 95.3% flip with confidence ≥ 0.80 into the abnormal class, while 87.4% of baseline-correct abnormals are robust-correct. Shift preferentially converts clean normals into confident abnormal reports, the worst direction for screening. Code, perturbation operators, the ESF reference implementation, and per-recording predictions are released. Preprint of the manuscript submitted to the IEEE Signal Processing in Medicine and Biology Symposium (SPMB) 2026 on 30 June 2026, currently under review. Code, perturbation operators, and per-recording predictions are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22727770 and maintained at https://github.com/h5371h/esf-recoverability. The supplementary material is included as a second file.

We sweep five acquisition-shift axes (native sampling rate, per-channel gain, 50 Hz line noise, electrode montage, and broadband signal-to-noise) and show that left-invertible and bandwidth-preserving operators are (f,0)-recoverable while sub-Nyquist sampling and broadband Gaussian noise are not (Propositions 1, 2). A Pinsker-based AUROC–total-variation bound holds on 18/18 measured axis-arms (median implied constant 0.10). Clustering every recording by its joint behaviour across the sweep yields seven failure categories: 100% of baseline-correct normals flip on at least one shifted cell, 95.3% flip with confidence ≥ 0.80 into the abnormal class, while 87.4% of baseline-correct abnormals are robust-correct. Shift preferentially converts clean normals into confident abnormal reports, the worst direction for screening. Code, perturbation operators, the ESF reference implementation, and per-recording predictions are released. Preprint of the manuscript submitted to the IEEE Signal Processing in Medicine and Biology Symposium (SPMB) 2026 on 30 June 2026, currently under review. Code, perturbation operators, and per-recording predictions are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22727770 and maintained at https://github.com/h5371h/esf-recoverability. The supplementary material is included as a second file.

summary: This book (in Croatian) covers operating systems and Linux, Storage and Networks (protocols & standards), virtualization, and Linux containers. Since this book is in a light but constant review and update process, please use the most recent version. This book may also be used to prepare/learn, or extend the knowledge needed for the next certifications: Red Hat®: Certified System Administrator (RHCSA®). Certified Architect (RHCA®). Linux Professional Institute®: LPIC-1. LPIC-2. LPIC-3*. Linux Foundation®: Linux Foundation Certified IT Associate (LFCA). Linux Foundation Certified System Administrator (LFCS).    The book covers the following chapters (in summary): Open source licenses and philosophy, open source software & license comparison. What are the advantages of Linux and open source software. Linux distributions and distribution types. Principles of operating systems: basic mechanisms and way of working of operating systems. System administration: Work with user accounts and groups. System security configuration (file permissions, timestamps, ACL, SELinux ). Service management (installation, configuration, ...) Software/package management: Patch management Archiving and backup. Process management. Computer components and optimizations: Motherboard and chipset. Buses: PCI, PCI-X, PCI Express, USB, SMBus/I2C IRQ and DMA, ... CPU and RAM CPU architecture: Registers, instructions, and ISA. CPU microarchitecture. SMP and NUMA architecture and optimizations. Kernel: Purpose and design. Upgrade, configure, compile the new one, etc. Virtual memory subsystem, RAM memory, and optimizations: Types of RAM memory. Memory management and virtual memory subsystem. Out of memory (OOM) and optimizations. Data storage and disk subsystems: Types of disk drives and standards. Disk geometry and logical scheme. Block devices and partitioning, disk formats, and filesystems. RAID (hardware and software) and LVM2 NAS and SAN storage systems overview SAN storage systems: iSCSI Fibre Channel (FC) Disk I/O subsystems and optimizations. Disk I/O performance and monitoring  System analysis and optimizations (perf, strace, ltrace, dstat). Working with log files and services. Kernel dump/core dump. Computer networks: Copper vs Optical networks: Copper: cabling and standards. Fiberoptics: standards, cabling, FTTH specifics. Network interfaces (NIC) design and details, classic (copper) NICs (RJ-45), and SFP specifics. Networking concepts and protocols (topology, CSMA/CD, Bridging, OSI model): OSI 2 model and protocols: Bridges, ARP, and Flow control. STP, LACP, LLDP, OSI 2 network interfaces,.... OSI 3 model and protocols: IP, QoS, IP Fragmentation. TTL, MTU. NAT (DNAT, SNAT). Redundancy and VRRP, .... Transport layer: UDP  TCP: SYN, ACK, SACK.  TCP Window, Window scaling, congestion control.  PSH&URG, ... . Multipath TCP Network in Linux (configuration and details). Optimizing network interfaces and services for 10+Gbps (10/25/100Gbps) Common network commands:  traceroute, nslookup. netstat, nstat, ss, lsof. ip, ethtool. tcpdump. Network services and protocols: DHCP, Bootp, TFTP DNS: Protocol details Types of DNS requests DNS records: A, AAA, PTR, CNAME, DNAME, MX, NS, SOA, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, ... Telnet and SSH. NFS E-mail: SMTP, POP3, IMAP HTTP/HTTPS, Proxy NTP Syslog SNMP Work with the firewall: iptables ipset nftables eBPF Namespaces and isolation Virtualization and Linux containers: LXC  Podman Security: Enforcements Compliance (NIST, CIS, DISA STIG, ...) Many extras: list of Linux commands, list of terms, list of important files, interface bandwidth, ... Advanced and expert chapters as an addition to all the mentioned chapters and units. Since this book is in a light but constant review and update process, please use the most recent version. This book may also be used to prepare/learn, or extend the knowledge needed for the next certifications: Red Hat®: Certified System Administrator (RHCSA®). Certified Architect (RHCA®). Linux Professional Institute®: LPIC-1. LPIC-2. LPIC-3*. Linux Foundation®: Linux Foundation Certified IT Associate (LFCA). Linux Foundation Certified System Administrator (LFCS).    The book covers the following chapters (in summary): Open source licenses and philosophy, open source software & license comparison. What are the advantages of Linux and open source software. Linux distributions and distribution types. Principles of operating systems: basic mechanisms and way of working of operating systems. System administration: Work with user accounts and groups. System security configuration (file permissions, timestamps, ACL, SELinux ). Service management (installation, configuration, ...) Software/package management: Patch management Archiving and backup. Process management. Computer components and optimizations: Motherboard and chipset. Buses: PCI, PCI-X, PCI Express, USB, SMBus/I2C IRQ and DMA, ... CPU and RAM CPU architecture: Registers, instructions, and ISA. CPU microarchitecture. SMP and NUMA architecture and optimizations. Kernel: Purpose and design. Upgrade, configure, compile the new one, etc. Virtual memory subsystem, RAM memory, and optimizations: Types of RAM memory. Memory management and virtual memory subsystem. Out of memory (OOM) and optimizations. Data storage and disk subsystems: Types of disk drives and standards. Disk geometry and logical scheme. Block devices and partitioning, disk formats, and filesystems. RAID (hardware and software) and LVM2 NAS and SAN storage systems overview SAN storage systems: iSCSI Fibre Channel (FC) Disk I/O subsystems and optimizations. Disk I/O performance and monitoring  System analysis and optimizations (perf, strace, ltrace, dstat). Working with log files and services. Kernel dump/core dump. Computer networks: Copper vs Optical networks: Copper: cabling and standards. Fiberoptics: standards, cabling, FTTH specifics. Network interfaces (NIC) design and details, classic (copper) NICs (RJ-45), and SFP specifics. Networking concepts and protocols (topology, CSMA/CD, Bridging, OSI model): OSI 2 model and protocols: Bridges, ARP, and Flow control. STP, LACP, LLDP, OSI 2 network interfaces,.... OSI 3 model and protocols: IP, QoS, IP Fragmentation. TTL, MTU. NAT (DNAT, SNAT). Redundancy and VRRP, .... Transport layer: UDP  TCP: SYN, ACK, SACK.  TCP Window, Window scaling, congestion control.  PSH&URG, ... . Multipath TCP Network in Linux (configuration and details). Optimizing network interfaces and services for 10+Gbps (10/25/100Gbps) Common network commands:  traceroute, nslookup. netstat, nstat, ss, lsof. ip, ethtool. tcpdump. Network services and protocols: DHCP, Bootp, TFTP DNS: Protocol details Types of DNS requests DNS records: A, AAA, PTR, CNAME, DNAME, MX, NS, SOA, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, ... Telnet and SSH. NFS E-mail: SMTP, POP3, IMAP HTTP/HTTPS, Proxy NTP Syslog SNMP Work with the firewall: iptables ipset nftables eBPF Namespaces and isolation Virtualization and Linux containers: LXC  Podman Security: Enforcements Compliance (NIST, CIS, DISA STIG, ...) Many extras: list of Linux commands, list of terms, list of important files, interface bandwidth, ... Advanced and expert chapters as an addition to all the mentioned chapters and units. Posters covering major chapters of the book (with links to the posters at the end of the book).    Who may use this book: Books cover the work in the Linux text environment (shell/CLI).  It is intended for everyone with very little

summary: A corpus of 219,386 Indian recipes across 378 source sites, with parsed ingredients in English/Roman, a 17-class allergen surface carrying an explicit unassessed sentinel, and estimated dish-level micronutrition; a typed knowledge graph of 222,539 nodes and 6,428,210 edges across 17 node types and 22 relation types; a 67-query retrieval benchmark with knowledge-graph-derived gold sets; and a synthetic collaborative interaction log. The food-composition layer uses the IFCT 42-nutrient schema but contains no IFCT and no Indian composition data; its values are USDA SR Legacy and UK CoFID. Two-tier release. Structured, factual and derived fields are published under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with per-recipe source attribution. Raw recipe prose is not redistributed; a rehydration index of source URLs and SHA-256 text digests is published instead, together with a re-fetch script. Known defects are published, not hidden. An independent allergen and diet audit ships with the data. See the datasheet before use, and do not use the allergen flags for end-user safety decisions.

summary: This supplementary package contains the Eurostat marketplace-share series used in the primary descriptive analysis of the manuscript “Marketplace and Firm-Owned Web Sales Around 2020: Evidence on Channel Composition in 21 European Union Countries, 2016–2024”. The package contains the archived Eurostat JSON response, processed country-year data, annual and country-period summary tables, Python code, and SHA-256 checksums. The balanced panel covers 21 countries and 189 country-year observations. The package supports the marketplace-share results reported in Table 3 and Figures 1 and 5. It does not reproduce the turnover-share, firm-size, covariate, or bootstrap analyses.
tags: Eurostat; online marketplaces; web sales; e-commerce; European Union; panel data; replication materials
title: Supplementary File S1: Eurostat Marketplace-Share Panel for 21 EU Countries, 2016–202

summary: This archive contains cached per-node conformity prediction tensors (calibration and test set probabilities) for four benchmark datasets — MIMIC-IV, arXiv category taxonomy, DBpedia, and MeSH — supporting reproducibility of the results reported in the associated anonymous submission. Each dataset's cached outputs are provided in a separate zip archive (mimic_outputs.zip, arxiv_outputs.zip, dbpedia_outputs.zip, mesh_outputs.zip), matching the directory structure expected by the accompanying evaluation code. This material is shared under restricted access for double-blind peer review purposes.
title: Cached Model Predictions for TAPS: Tree-Adaptive Prediction Sets (Anonymous Supplementary Material)

summary: CAOS Research v0.65.000 This release packages the Riemann hypothesis research update through EXP-004. Highlights EXP-003 confirms a finite pressure-frame bound with winner theta=3/4, pressure=1/12500, epsilon=443239/1e9, simple bound 0.4190878881701117 and distinct bound 0.7095439440850559. EXP-004 proves a strict parity-density transfer: for the declared classical seed alpha=51/100, an existential theta1<theta0 gives liminf simple zero density at least kappa/3 on fixed theta in [theta1,1), with a strict nearby distinct-zero lower bound. The record preserves that kappa and theta1 are not numerically instantiated and that no all-height theorem or RH proof follows. The v0.02 manuscript is archived on Zenodo as 10.5281/zenodo.22728744. The public research workbench includes deterministic EXP-003 and EXP-004 replay evidence, source-hash provenance, and the full rendered verification matrix. Validation Python suite: 364 collected tests passed. Frontend suite: 14 tests passed; production build passed. Research guards, content standards, artifact contract, and deterministic pipeline checks passed. Public Pages deployment run 34718338730 and CI run 34718338752 passed. The live site was checked after deployment; the final receipt is recorded in the repository release evidence. Research status The Riemann hypothesis remains open. This release records a rigorously bounded pressure-frame result and a qualitative parity transfer, not a proof of RH or a new global numerical density record.
title: fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH: CAOS Research v0.65.000

summary: Companion data and code for "Do-it-yourself and benchtop DNA synthesis: a biosecurity assessment and a route-attribution capability" (Didenko, 2026). A co-processed reference atlas of DNA-synthesis error signatures (65 sequencing runs across four synthesis processes), the per-run error tables it is built from, the full analysis pipeline (error calling, feature extraction, atlas build, leakage-aware classification, and likelihood-ratio calibration), and a held-out cross-deposit check on an independent column dataset (Yeom SHIFT). No raw sequencing reads are redistributed; every source dataset is public and identified by accession (Filges PRJNA727098; Masaki DRA013805; Lietard PRJEB43002; Gimpel PRJEB65931), and the atlas rebuilds from the included error tables without network access. See README.md for reproduce steps, scope caveats, and provenance. Release pending institutional infohazard review (IBBIS).

summary: QN-AEI is a curated, simulation-based benchmark for studying quantum noise effects in amplitude-encoded grayscale images. Two hundred images from the BSDS500 training subset were converted to grayscale, resized to 64 x 64 pixels, and encoded as 4096-dimensional normalized amplitude vectors, each corresponding to a 12-qubit quantum state. Every image was then evolved under three completely positive trace-preserving noise channels — amplitude damping, Pauli-Z dephasing, and depolarizing noise — at four channel-parameter values, eta = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, with 200 repeated stochastic realizations per image-channel-noise configuration. The release therefore contains 2,400 image-channel-noise conditions, 480,000 noisy amplitude-encoded realizations, and 1,966,080,000 normalized perturbation samples. Each image-level record stores the preprocessed clean image, the clean amplitude vector, the noisy statevector matrices, raw and pooled perturbation arrays, normalized bounded-domain perturbation values, and structured condition-level metadata including a deterministic per-condition random seed. The release also includes a dataset manifest, source-image provenance linking every record to its BSDS500 original, an automated validation report covering all 200 records, aggregated and condition-level perturbation statistics, and the MATLAB script used to generate and validate the dataset. The original BSDS500 image files are not redistributed. Users should obtain them from the Berkeley Computer Vision Group and comply with the BSDS500 usage terms. The dataset supports reproducible benchmarking of quantum-noise modeling, bounded-domain perturbation modeling, denoising and error-mitigation methods, and uncertainty and reliability analysis using the repeated realizations. Due to the size of the release (12.6 GB) and Zenodo's current infrastructure load, QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip is distributed as 26 sequential parts (QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part001 through QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part026) rather than a single file. Download all 26 parts into the same folder, then reassemble the original archive before extracting. summary: QN-AEI is a curated, simulation-based benchmark for studying quantum noise effects in amplitude-encoded grayscale images. Two hundred images from the BSDS500 training subset were converted to grayscale, resized to 64 x 64 pixels, and encoded as 4096-dimensional normalized amplitude vectors, each corresponding to a 12-qubit quantum state. Every image was then evolved under three completely positive trace-preserving noise channels — amplitude damping, Pauli-Z dephasing, and depolarizing noise — at four channel-parameter values, eta = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, with 200 repeated stochastic realizations per image-channel-noise configuration. The release therefore contains 2,400 image-channel-noise conditions, 480,000 noisy amplitude-encoded realizations, and 1,966,080,000 normalized perturbation samples. Each image-level record stores the preprocessed clean image, the clean amplitude vector, the noisy statevector matrices, raw and pooled perturbation arrays, normalized bounded-domain perturbation values, and structured condition-level metadata including a deterministic per-condition random seed. The release also includes a dataset manifest, source-image provenance linking every record to its BSDS500 original, an automated validation report covering all 200 records, aggregated and condition-level perturbation statistics, and the MATLAB script used to generate and validate the dataset. The original BSDS500 image files are not redistributed. Users should obtain them from the Berkeley Computer Vision Group and comply with the BSDS500 usage terms. The dataset supports reproducible benchmarking of quantum-noise modeling, bounded-domain perturbation modeling, denoising and error-mitigation methods, and uncertainty and reliability analysis using the repeated realizations. Due to the size of the release (12.6 GB) and Zenodo's current infrastructure load, QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip is distributed as 26 sequential parts (QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part001 through QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part026) rather than a single file. Download all 26 parts into the same folder, then reassemble the original archive before extracting. summary: We present a synthesis of the Karimov–Alekberli (KA) Framework into a unified theory of Constitutional Intelligence: the capacity of an adaptive system to make consequential decisions that are simultaneously governed, explainable, accountable, reconstructable, verifiable, and capable of learning without retroactive falsification of the historical record. We formulate six formal results — one per required property — organized into three proof tiers: Tier A (two unconditional geometric results), Tier B (three conditional results valid under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), Tier C (one KA extension under a physical implementation assumption). Results draw on viability theory,information geometry, and thermodynamics. The theorems are organized in three tiers reflecting their current proof status: Tier A (fully proved geometric results), Tier B (conditional theorems under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), and Tier C (KA extensions requiring additional physical or topological conditions). A unifying condition, the Constitutional Integrity Criterion (CIC), is formulated as a representation theorem characterizing systems that satisfy all six properties simultaneously. We derive, under the CIC, that the governance loop Govern → Reason → Act → Remember → Learn → Govern defines a well-defined autonomous map on the constitutional moduli space that preserves the admissible region; fixed-point existence follows as a corollary under compactness. We position the framework within the existing literature on viability theory, formal verification, safe reinforcement learning, AI governance, and constitutional economics. We propose Constitutional Intelligence Science as the emerging discipline that unifies these results.

summary: Adaptability release: the analysis pipeline no longer assumes an NV-scale emitter or a negligible instrument response, and measured data enter through a documented file contract. This release also upgrades the fit physics itself -- two changes that came out of adversarial re-examination rather than feature work. Bring your own emitter and instrument load_hbt_csv / save_hbt_csv : a documented two-column contract ( delay_ns,counts ) with an exact round trip and refusals for wrong headers, field counts, negative counts and non-increasing delay axes. Configurable lifetime windows : t1_bounds / t2_bounds (ns) on analyze_histogram , fit_g2_histogram and profile_likelihood_ci -- validated on entry. The defaults are the NV-scale window used since v0.1. The test suite runs a tau1 = 0.15 ns, tau2 = 5 ns emitter and shows BOTH halves: the default window fails visibly (error > 0.2), the emitter's own window recovers g2(0) to better than 0.05. register_platform (existing) plus a test that a user-defined platform runs the whole pipeline; load_fisequr now takes the dataset directory explicitly instead of defaulting to one machine's path. The fit physics, corrected Physical parameterization. The LM fit and the profile likelihood now fit the dip depth rho^2 multiplying BOTH exponentials (g2(0) = 1 - rho^2), the form g2_measured itself uses. The previous 1 - d e1 + a e2 form capped d at 1 -- which biased g2(0) upward for any emitter with a strong bunching shoulder -- and hid a genuine (d, a) ridge behind that cap. The instrument response is in the model. summary: Doucette rereads Keynes’s 1930 essay “Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren” as a sequencing rule, not a prophecy of mass idleness or automatic leisure. Keynes defined technological unemployment as a pace problem: labor-saving discovery outruns new uses for labor. He called it a temporary maladjustment, while predicting long-run abundance through technical progress and capital accumulation. Doucette applies this framework to the U.S. mid-2020s, focusing on generative AI’s early labor-market effects and the data-center buildout. AI stress appears mainly in junior cognitive work and entry-level hiring, not the national unemployment rate. Data centers are capital-intensive, labor-sparse operations: thousands of construction jobs, few permanent ones, and local conflict over water, power, rates, and consent. They resemble power stations or switching offices more than factories. Northern Virginia illustrates the consent problem. Keynes said little about ownership, so the paper imports distribution: who captures the dividend? It proposes three tests: absorption (rebuild the first rung), cost assignment (large loads pay incremental infrastructure costs), and the dividend (where productivity appears). It considers accelerationist, localist, and leisure-skeptic objections. Limitations include early evidence, mixed data, and one mature cluster. The conclusion separates two clocks: short-run maladjustment and long-run abundance. AI is neither a completed solution nor a surplus of workers; it changes task content and drives physical accumulation. The task is to keep entry paths open, assign costs to the load causing them, and track whether productivity reaches typical pay. Failure would be institutional, not technical.

Abstract La rigida delimitazione imposta dall'atletica classica (World Athletics Technical Rule 6.3.4) contro gli ausili attivi ha storicamente confinato l'indagine sulle massime capacità biomeccaniche umane all'interno di un perimetro biologico intrinseco. summary: Extraction code, full concordance, both coders' independent judgements and the adjudication record for the article "In Our Lands": Region, Language, and Community in Ibn Sīnā's First Person. Every first-person plural in nineteen works of Ibn Sīnā (2,070,759 words) was extracted and classified, together with three control authors — al-Bīrūnī, Abū Bakr al-Rāzī and al-Fārābī — for a total of fifty-nine works and 410 instances. All instances were coded independently by two readers, the second blind to the hypothesis; the 49 disagreements were adjudicated against written criteria. Both readers' original codes are preserved unaltered. Source texts are from the OpenITI corpus, version 2025.1.9 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17767721); the texts themselves are not redistributed here. See README.md in the archive for a file-by-file description, the coding scheme, headline figures and reproduction instructions. Licence note: data/ is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (inherited from OpenITI via ShareAlike); code/ and protocol/ are MIT. See LICENCE-data.txt and LICENCE-code.txt. The second coding pass was carried out independently, and blind to the hypothesis, by a colleague who has asked not to be named; their codes are included in full as data/codes_reader_B.csv, and the adjudication record in data/uzlastirilmis.csv shows where their reading was preferred.

All instances were coded independently by two readers, the second blind to the hypothesis; the 49 disagreements were adjudicated against written criteria. Both readers' original codes are preserved unaltered. Source texts are from the OpenITI corpus, version 2025.1.9 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17767721); the texts themselves are not redistributed here. See README.md in the archive for a file-by-file description, the coding scheme, headline figures and reproduction instructions. Licence note: data/ is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (inherited from OpenITI via ShareAlike); code/ and protocol/ are MIT. See LICENCE-data.txt and LICENCE-code.txt. The second coding pass was carried out independently, and blind to the hypothesis, by a colleague who has asked not to be named; their codes are included in full as data/codes_reader_B.csv, and the adjudication record in data/uzlastirilmis.csv shows where their reading was preferred.
title: Replication data for "In Our Lands": Region, Language, and Community in Ibn Sīnā's First Person

summary: Whether a neural language model can report facts about its own computation is difficult to evaluate because an accurate report may be generated either from the realized runtime state or from a static simulation of the computation conditioned on the input and fixed parameters. We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768). In ESW-1A, a planted directional watermark becomes increasingly decodable as training examples grow relative to representation dimension, reaching 88.4% held-out accuracy at N/d=6.51 (cos θ = 0.9236), while a one-dimensional control reaches 100.0%. In an exploratory Oracle Ladder diagnostic, differential signals peak at Layer 8 before downstream attenuation. In the subsequent multi-seed paired-counterfactual benchmark (ESW-2B), an external nonlinear probe of intermediate runtime differences reaches approximately 0.62–0.63 AUROC, while the tested unperturbed-state baseline remains close to chance (0.507 AUROC) and a sample-label decoupled control remains at 0.546 AUROC. The paired bootstrap difference between the joint and runtime-only models includes zero (ΔAUROC = +0.012, 95% CI [-0.023, +0.047]), demonstrating that adding baseline activations provides no statistically detectable advantage over the runtime perturbation alone.  We interpret the experiments as empirical evidence for runtime-state-dependent decodability under the ESW intervention, not as evidence that GPT-2 possesses autonomous introspection, privileged self-report, consciousness, or subjective self-knowledge.

summary: Experimental-adaptability release: the three inputs a laboratory actually has -- a measured dispersion table, a fixed set of deposited materials, and a reflectance specification -- now enter the yield-aware design loop directly. Added TabulatedMaterial : bring your measured dispersion. An n(lam) table from ellipsometry, a vendor datasheet or a refractiveindex.info tabulation is used directly -- no Sellmeier fit required. Shape-preserving PCHIP interpolation, refusal outside the tabulated range (the same rule as the cited Sellmeier built-ins), and a mandatory reference naming where the table comes from. An optional extinction column serves the absorbing forward solver through .nk() ; .n() refuses an absorbing table rather than silently dropping k, because the design path is lossless. .n(lam) is the same interface as SellmeierMaterial.n , so a tabulated material drops into dispersion_shape , layer_index and everything built on them. Per-layer and frozen design boxes. Every DesignBox bound now accepts a scalar or an (N,) array, and a bound pair with lo == hi freezes that parameter -- so a real multi-material stack, whose indices are deposited materials rather than design variables, runs through the identical engine. DesignBox.thickness_only(N, t_lo, t_hi, n_fixed) builds the common case. A fully frozen box (nothing left to design) is refused. weights_from_reflectance : mirror and high-reflector merits. A reflectance-based linear merit converts to transmittance weights by the exact lossless identity R = 1 - T, so reflectance specifications run through the same hand adjoint, design engine and CVaR robustifier unchanged. The thickness-only metrology path , documented and anchored: a tool that logs thickness but not per-run index sets n_fab = n_recipe in the trace contract; the fitted twin then invents no index errors, and robustification on a frozen-index box uses exactly the information the lab has. Changed FabTwinConfig validates its bounds (strictly increasing scalars): the learned twin's recipe conditioner normalizes by hi - lo, so frozen or per-layer bounds -- a design-space feature of DesignBox -- are refused there with an explanation instead of producing a division by zero. Anchors (asserted in tests/test_experimental_adapt.py , not stated) A table sampled from the cited Malitson Sellmeier is exact at its nodes and agrees with the independent closed form between them; the whole design path (shape, solver, hand adjoint vs central finite differences) runs on a tabulated material end to end. The design engine and the CVaR robustifier return a frozen index profile EXACTLY ( np.array_equal ); per-layer sampling and clipping respect each layer's window. The reflectance-weight identity holds at machine precision on a lossless stack through the solver's exact R + T = 1; on an absorbing stack it fails by exactly w_R . A (asserted as an exact relation), and the quarter-wave (HL)^3 mirror scores its closed-form admittance reflectance through this path. A thickness-only twin's sampled index errors stay below 1e-3 while its thickness errors are preserved, and CVaR ascent on the frozen-index box does not degrade the objective it ascends. Full test suite: 63 passed (Python 3.10-3.13, JAX extra active in CI). See CHANGELOG.md for details.

Every DesignBox bound now accepts a scalar or an (N,) array, and a bound pair with lo == hi freezes that parameter -- so a real multi-material stack, whose indices are deposited materials rather than design variables, runs through the identical engine. Conventions are checked by identities rather than trusted: every conversion round-trips exactly, F scales as sqrt(P), and threshold_power is cross-validated through the package's own flat-state cubic -- at the returned power, homogeneous_steady_states contains the rho = 1 root to machine precision. summary: This repository contains the curated 17-specimen compression summary, source-file checksum manifest, deterministic analysis code, machine-readable statistical outputs, sensitivity analyses, regenerated figures, data dictionary and provenance documentation supporting the manuscript “Failure-Sensitive Manufacturing Heterogeneity in Pultruded Unidirectional Carbon/Vinyl-Ester Composites: A Reproducible Open-Data Reanalysis”. The source experimental data are openly archived at Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18435237) and are not duplicated here. An optional downloader verifies all source files by MD5 before independent header re-extraction. The reanalysis compares three pultruded profiles from the same carbon-fiber/vinyl-ester base material and tests whether profile-level manufacturing heterogeneity is amplified in compression failure quantities relative to longitudinal stiffness.
title: Reproducibility Dataset and Code for Failure-Sensitive Manufacturing Heterogeneity in Pultruded Unidirectional Carbon/Vinyl-Ester Composites
