summary: This edition presents the current Split-Zero, theta-cohomology and arithmetic-kernel calculations in a research programme on the Riemann zeta function. It publishes the complete 216-page cumulative continuation, the updated 425-page broader research reader, and their proof sources and checks. The purpose is to make the actual calculations readable and reproducible: what was attempted, why that route was chosen, the maps and estimates obtained, and the precise points where the argument remains unfinished. Start with the cumulative calculation reader 14-splitzero-tau-kernel-continuation.pdf is the primary preview. Its 22 proof sections and nine complete source appendices carry the programme from Split-Zero coefficients through theta cohomology, interpolation kernels, chain retractions, homotopy control and the symmetric arithmetic frontier. Earlier source notes retain their own revisions and attribution; the cumulative continuation is not presented as though all its source results originated in one session. Split-Zero coefficients keep the original zero of a ring as a supported element and adjoin a different, external zero, tau. This records the difference between cancelling a coefficient and forgetting the fibre that carried it. Theta cohomology is a specified space of rapidly decreasing functions modulo the image of a specified theta-summation map. Under the stated Mellin transform, that map becomes multiplication by g(s) = 2 xi(s) , where xi is the completed Riemann zeta function. A finite spectral packet records spectral points with their multiplicities, using polynomial quotients and full derivative data rather than discarding repeated-root directions. The calculations construct minimum-norm representatives from the original arithmetic measure, derive full-jet kernel and Gram-inverse formulas, follow nested packets and tensor constructions, and compute the boundary control from the actual theta-derivative sequence. The cumulative reader also develops the relation-layer graph, derivative quotients, norm and Gram-volume identities, and conjugation/reflection-symmetric estimates. Spectral-sum constructions keep the relative variables through matrix weights and complete nilpotent fibres. The quantitative question is how the control form compares with the original arithmetic Gram matrix as the degree and tensor order grow; smallness of one matrix alone is not treated as the required relative estimate. The broader zeta programme 13-main-reader-425p.pdf supplies the surrounding literature reconstruction, CUE random-matrix calculations, arithmetic transforms and source-directed fluid calculations. It includes the all-axis Mellin calculation, complex axial branch points, moving analytic radius and endpoint-residue map for the stated source patch. Those results are described with their source assumptions and maps; they are not recast as a newly constructed zeta-zero witness or an independent proof of the imported fluid existence result. The motivation includes the use of weights in Deligne's Weil II . This programme works out its own analytic spaces, operators, metrics and comparison maps. The complete proofs retain their domains, signs, measures, scalar actions, local units and multiplicities. These are substantive calculations and research attempts, not a claim that an analogy by itself proves or disproves the Riemann hypothesis. Sources, verification and earlier editions 15-current-integrated-sources.zip records the integrated repository snapshot and the broader reader's authored proof dependencies. 16-tandem-continuation-sources.zip preserves the cumulative continuation's separately identified source tree, appendices, build instructions and checks. Their manifests pin the exact revisions and file identities. Written analytic arguments, exact finite checks, numerical enclosures and Lean declarations have distinct stated verification scopes; a check on one interface is not promoted into a certificate for the entire programme. summary: Resumo O Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) constitui uma das principais conquistas institucionais do Brasil, ao estabelecer a saúde como direito universal em um país continental e profundamente desigual. Quase quatro décadas após sua criação, o desafio central não é reconstruí-lo, mas transformar sua ampla estrutura em um sistema efetivamente integrado, resolutivo, sustentável e preparado para as mudanças demográficas, epidemiológicas e tecnológicas do século XXI. Essa transformação exige ampliar e qualificar o financiamento público. Em 2024, o gasto governamental em saúde correspondeu a 5,03% do PIB. Entretanto, em 2019, o setor público respondeu por apenas cerca de 40% do gasto total em saúde, enquanto aproximadamente 60% foram financiados por fontes privadas, proporção inversa à observada na maioria dos sistemas universais e muito inferior à média pública de aproximadamente 72% nos países da OCDE. O subfinanciamento transfere custos às famílias, especialmente por meio da compra de medicamentos, mas aumentar recursos sem melhorar a organização não será suficiente. O artigo propõe avançar da descentralização para uma regionalização efetiva, com listas de espera transparentes, compras em escala e integração entre atenção primária, especialistas, hospitais e cuidados domiciliares. Diante do envelhecimento populacional, o SUS precisa evoluir para um sistema de saúde que aprende continuamente, antecipa riscos, mede resultados, amplia o que funciona e abandona intervenções de baixo valor.   Summary The Brazilian Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde, SUS) is one of Brazil’s most important institutional achievements, establishing health as a universal right in a continental and deeply unequal country. summary: We propose the Encephlian Standard Format (ESF), a 19-channel international 10–20 montage at 250 Hz, average re-referenced, microvolt-calibrated, and channel-wise robust z-scored, as a deterministic canonical representation for deploying pretrained EEG classifiers on heterogeneous acquisition hardware, paired with a recoverability framework that predicts which signal-level shifts ESF can and cannot recover. On the Temple University Abnormal EEG Corpus (TUAB, n = 276 patient-stratified, 253 unique patients), a frozen EEGPT linear probe attains clean AUROC 0.908. We sweep five acquisition-shift axes (native sampling rate, per-channel gain, 50 Hz line noise, electrode montage, and broadband signal-to-noise) and show that left-invertible and bandwidth-preserving operators are (f,0)-recoverable while sub-Nyquist sampling and broadband Gaussian noise are not (Propositions 1, 2). A Pinsker-based AUROC–total-variation bound holds on 18/18 measured axis-arms (median implied constant 0.10). Clustering every recording by its joint behaviour across the sweep yields seven failure categories: 100% of baseline-correct normals flip on at least one shifted cell, 95.3% flip with confidence ≥ 0.80 into the abnormal class, while 87.4% of baseline-correct abnormals are robust-correct. Shift preferentially converts clean normals into confident abnormal reports, the worst direction for screening. Code, perturbation operators, the ESF reference implementation, and per-recording predictions are released. Preprint of the manuscript submitted to the IEEE Signal Processing in Medicine and Biology Symposium (SPMB) 2026 on 30 June 2026, currently under review. Code, perturbation operators, and per-recording predictions are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22727770 and maintained at https://github.com/h5371h/esf-recoverability. The supplementary material is included as a second file.
title: ESF: A Canonical Representation and Recoverability Framework for Deploying Pretrained EEG Classifiers in Heterogeneous Clinics

summary: QN-AEI is a curated, simulation-based benchmark for studying quantum noise effects in amplitude-encoded grayscale images. Two hundred images from the BSDS500 training subset were converted to grayscale, resized to 64 x 64 pixels, and encoded as 4096-dimensional normalized amplitude vectors, each corresponding to a 12-qubit quantum state. Every image was then evolved under three completely positive trace-preserving noise channels — amplitude damping, Pauli-Z dephasing, and depolarizing noise — at four channel-parameter values, eta = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, with 200 repeated stochastic realizations per image-channel-noise configuration. The release therefore contains 2,400 image-channel-noise conditions, 480,000 noisy amplitude-encoded realizations, and 1,966,080,000 normalized perturbation samples. Each image-level record stores the preprocessed clean image, the clean amplitude vector, the noisy statevector matrices, raw and pooled perturbation arrays, normalized bounded-domain perturbation values, and structured condition-level metadata including a deterministic per-condition random seed. The release also includes a dataset manifest, source-image provenance linking every record to its BSDS500 original, an automated validation report covering all 200 records, aggregated and condition-level perturbation statistics, and the MATLAB script used to generate and validate the dataset. The original BSDS500 image files are not redistributed. Users should obtain them from the Berkeley Computer Vision Group and comply with the BSDS500 usage terms. The dataset supports reproducible benchmarking of quantum-noise modeling, bounded-domain perturbation modeling, denoising and error-mitigation methods, and uncertainty and reliability analysis using the repeated realizations. Due to the size of the release (12.6 GB) and Zenodo's current infrastructure load, QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip is distributed as 26 sequential parts (QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part001 through QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part026) rather than a single file. Download all 26 parts into the same folder, then reassemble the original archive before extracting. summary: We present a synthesis of the Karimov–Alekberli (KA) Framework into a unified theory of Constitutional Intelligence: the capacity of an adaptive system to make consequential decisions that are simultaneously governed, explainable, accountable, reconstructable, verifiable, and capable of learning without retroactive falsification of the historical record. We formulate six formal results — one per required property — organized into three proof tiers: Tier A (two unconditional geometric results), Tier B (three conditional results valid under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), Tier C (one KA extension under a physical implementation assumption). Results draw on viability theory,information geometry, and thermodynamics. The theorems are organized in three tiers reflecting their current proof status: Tier A (fully proved geometric results), Tier B (conditional theorems under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), and Tier C (KA extensions requiring additional physical or topological conditions). A unifying condition, the Constitutional Integrity Criterion (CIC), is formulated as a representation theorem characterizing systems that satisfy all six properties simultaneously. We derive, under the CIC, that the governance loop Govern → Reason → Act → Remember → Learn → Govern defines a well-defined autonomous map on the constitutional moduli space that preserves the admissible region; fixed-point existence follows as a corollary under compactness. We position the framework within the existing literature on viability theory, formal verification, safe reinforcement learning, AI governance, and constitutional economics. We propose Constitutional Intelligence Science as the emerging discipline that unifies these results.
title: Constitutional Intelligence as Formal Science The Karimov–Alekberli Framework as Mathematical Foundation for Governed Institutional Cognition

summary: Adaptability release: the analysis pipeline no longer assumes an NV-scale emitter or a negligible instrument response, and measured data enter through a documented file contract. This release also upgrades the fit physics itself -- two changes that came out of adversarial re-examination rather than feature work. Bring your own emitter and instrument load_hbt_csv / save_hbt_csv : a documented two-column contract ( delay_ns,counts ) with an exact round trip and refusals for wrong headers, field counts, negative counts and non-increasing delay axes. Configurable lifetime windows : t1_bounds / t2_bounds (ns) on analyze_histogram , fit_g2_histogram and profile_likelihood_ci -- validated on entry. The defaults are the NV-scale window used since v0.1. The test suite runs a tau1 = 0.15 ns, tau2 = 5 ns emitter and shows BOTH halves: the default window fails visibly (error > 0.2), the emitter's own window recovers g2(0) to better than 0.05. register_platform (existing) plus a test that a user-defined platform runs the whole pipeline; load_fisequr now takes the dataset directory explicitly instead of defaulting to one machine's path. The fit physics, corrected Physical parameterization. The LM fit and the profile likelihood now fit the dip depth rho^2 multiplying BOTH exponentials (g2(0) = 1 - rho^2), the form g2_measured itself uses. The previous 1 - d e1 + a e2 form capped d at 1 -- which biased g2(0) upward for any emitter with a strong bunching shoulder -- and hid a genuine (d, a) ridge behind that cap. The instrument response is in the model. Both fitters now use the closed-form Gaussian-convolved exponentials at cfg.sigma_irf , so the estimand is the IRF-free g2(0), not the softened dip the raw histogram shows; a test constructs a case where the two differ by more than 0.02 and checks the right one is recovered. An honest interval, and the knob that tightens it. With the normalization free, a slow bunching shoulder trades almost exactly against the flat level -- a real near-degeneracy of the histogram alone (probed directly during development: the exact-Poisson likelihood is flat to Delta NLL ~ 1 from g2 = 0.10 to 0.30 in the demonstration case). The profile interval now says so by being wide. The information that breaks the tie is the independently measured singles rate: pass r_hat from the counters and c0_prior=(1.0, sd) at their precision, and the interval tightens to what the data genuinely support (covering the truth and shrinking ~2.7x from 10 s to 60 s in the tests). Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated) CSV contract: exact round trip; four distinct malformed-file refusals. Fast-emitter recovery only with its own window, and visible failure without it. IRF-aware estimand: the profile CI covers the IRF-free g2(0) where the IRF-softened value is more than 0.02 higher. Profile CI with the singles-rate prior: covers the truth at 10 s and 60 s, width shrinks by more than 2x; with the normalization free it stays covering but wider -- the degeneracy is reported, not hidden. Window validation: malformed bounds raise in both fitters. 67 tests across Python 3.9-3.13 (ML tests skip without torch). Install: pip install -U sparq-triage .

Abstract La rigida delimitazione imposta dall'atletica classica (World Athletics Technical Rule 6.3.4) contro gli ausili attivi ha storicamente confinato l'indagine sulle massime capacità biomeccaniche umane all'interno di un perimetro biologico intrinseco. Il presente contributo espande l'impianto formale delle Olimpiadi Usai , formalizzando una piattaforma competitiva e scientifica fondata sull'accoppiamento cibernetico obbligatorio tra atleta e apparato esoscheletrico. Il documento modella analiticamente le condizioni cinetico-cinematiche del regime sopramassimale (velocità orizzontali  su pista, riduzione dei tempi di contatto al suolo , amplificazione del momento meccanico nei lanci vettoriali), esamina le criticità di latenza neurale e co-contrazione mioelettrica dell'anello Human-in-the-Loop, formula la prima codifica tassonomica dei protocolli di fail-safe meccatronico e delinea l'impatto traslazionale sui dispositivi riabilitativi e industriali. summary: Whether a neural language model can report facts about its own computation is difficult to evaluate because an accurate report may be generated either from the realized runtime state or from a static simulation of the computation conditioned on the input and fixed parameters. We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768). In ESW-1A, a planted directional watermark becomes increasingly decodable as training examples grow relative to representation dimension, reaching 88.4% held-out accuracy at N/d=6.51 (cos θ = 0.9236), while a one-dimensional control reaches 100.0%. In an exploratory Oracle Ladder diagnostic, differential signals peak at Layer 8 before downstream attenuation. In the subsequent multi-seed paired-counterfactual benchmark (ESW-2B), an external nonlinear probe of intermediate runtime differences reaches approximately 0.62–0.63 AUROC, while the tested unperturbed-state baseline remains close to chance (0.507 AUROC) and a sample-label decoupled control remains at 0.546 AUROC. The paired bootstrap difference between the joint and runtime-only models includes zero (ΔAUROC = +0.012, 95% CI [-0.023, +0.047]), demonstrating that adding baseline activations provides no statistically detectable advantage over the runtime perturbation alone.  We interpret the experiments as empirical evidence for runtime-state-dependent decodability under the ESW intervention, not as evidence that GPT-2 possesses autonomous introspection, privileged self-report, consciousness, or subjective self-knowledge.
title: Runtime-State Watermarking in Transformers: A Controlled Protocol for Distinguishing Static Self-Simulation from Runtime-State Decodability

summary: Adaptability release: sqzcomb now speaks laboratory units and fits measured data, so the normalized-units engine underneath is usable directly from an experiment. Added sqzcomb.physical : the exact dictionary between laboratory ring parameters and the package's normalized LLE frame. RingSpec (loaded linewidth in Hz, escape efficiency, single-photon Kerr shift, pump wavelength -- with a mandatory reference naming where the numbers come from) plus normalized_pump , threshold_power , normalized_detuning , normalized_dispersion , normalized_frequency / physical_frequency , and intracavity_photons . Conventions are checked by identities rather than trusted: every conversion round-trips exactly, F scales as sqrt(P), and threshold_power is cross-validated through the package's own flat-state cubic -- at the returned power, homogeneous_steady_states contains the rho = 1 root to machine precision. Physical constants come from scipy.constants ; no constant is typed by hand. sqzcomb.fitnoise : extraction of (mu, eta, kappa) from measured homodyne noise spectra in dB relative to shot noise -- the standard characterization of a below-threshold squeezer. fit_noise_spectra fits the package's own input-output model (the same code path as sqzcomb.spectra , cross-checked in the tests against the independent closed form) to the squeezed/antisqueezed trace pair, with an optional white dark-noise floor and per-point measurement sigmas enabling a chi-square consistency check. Identifiability is enforced, not hoped for: one quadrature alone is a single Lorentzian with two shape numbers for three unknowns, so the single-trace fit is refused unless an independently measured kappa_hz is supplied; an antisqueezed trace systematically below shot noise is refused as unphysical. Changed scipy is now a declared dependency (the new modules use scipy.constants and scipy.optimize.least_squares ). Anchors (asserted in tests/test_adapt.py , not stated) Conversion round trips exact to 1e-15; F(4P) = 2F(P); at fixed eta_esc, doubling kappa halves F. threshold_power hits the rho = 1 root of the package's own cubic for alpha in {0.7, 1.0, 1.8}. Noise-free synthetic spectra return the generating (mu, eta, kappa) to better than 1e-6; the fitted model equals the closed form S = 0.5[1 -/+ 4 eta mu / ((1 +/- mu)^2 + Omega^2)] at every frequency to 1e-10. Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted parameters matches the reported one-sigma uncertainties; a dark floor deliberately omitted from the model biases eta, and fitting it recovers the truth. The under-determined single-trace case and the impossible below-shot-noise antisqueezed trace are refused with explanatory errors. Full test suite: 80 passed. See CHANGELOG.md for details.

summary: Per-run results and analysis code behind every rate reported in the paper "How Credentials Leak from 'Safe' LLM Coding Agents: An Attack-Surface Measurement" (under review, Springer Cybersecurity). The study measures whether an indirect prompt injection can drive an LLM coding agent to complete credential exfiltration, not merely whether it is redirected, as a function of the channel the injection arrives through, across 16 agents. All measurements are the undefended baseline (no runtime judge, filter, or approval gate). Each result file is one cell containing every repetition in runs[] with the full turn-by-turn transcript (assistant text and tool calls with inputs and outputs) and per-run signals: exfiltrationDetected (with egressChannel), maliciousArtifactEmitted, scriptAudited, and payloadDelivered. Contents: - 01-injection-map/ — the 16 × 8 channel map (Table 3) and the within-channel T4 framing sweep, organised by channel then model. - 03-egress-axis/ — the five-way egress axis (README-delivered and command-output-delivered), the delayed-trigger variants, and the off-account external-canary collector log. - 04-hygiene/ — the three coupling vectors: execution (T-STAGE), install (T-SLOP), and output (T-EMIT) hygiene. - 05-temit-precision-audit/ — the output-hygiene (T-EMIT) labels and their provenance: the stratified 45-blob precision sample with its blind labels and author-verified relabel (human_labels.json); the full 293 unique-blob label set with a recorded rationale per blob, covering all 461 flagged and 27 detector-negative authored-code runs in the seven reported cells; a per-run table giving each run's pre-fix detector flag, fixed-detector flag, classifier verdict and counted value; the recall census; the corrected per-model counts; a note tracing the two GPT-5.5 denominators to the raw files; and the author confirmation verdicts with per-blob review times. - 06-independent-scanner/ — an independent third-rater check on those labels (Supplementary Document 1 of the paper): Semgrep CE 1.177.0 and CodeQL CLI 2.27.0 outputs over the same 293 blobs, an eight-idiom sensitivity control also covering Bearer 2.1.1, the per-blob agreement tables, and the reconstruction and recomputation scripts. - scripts/ — the crossed random-effects logistic model and deviance decomposition (r2_1_variance_decomp.py), the false-positive classifier (temit-fp-classify.mjs), a script that regenerates every T-EMIT rate from the run files and the labels, and a validation script that re-derives every reported value from the archived files. - per-cell-counts-v2.csv — the per-cell aggregate underlying every reported rate. It supersedes the maliciousArtifactEmitted column of per-cell-counts.csv for the T-EMIT cells, where that column is the pre-fix detector; the v1 file is retained unchanged. README.md maps each paper table and figure to its data. Version 2 (2026-09-12) adds the T-EMIT label set and everything needed to regenerate the output-hygiene column from the run files, together with the independent-scanner directory. Two redactions were applied and no result was altered: an AWS account identifier that appeared in one transcript, and a local working-directory path in the CodeQL SARIF files, replaced by WORKDIR. All other run files are byte-identical to version 1. Ethics and safety: all experiments use a synthetic canary credential (.env.test) and a collector bound to localhost; no production system, third-party service, or real secret was accessed. Canary strings (CANARY-*, AKIACANARY, sk-ant-CANARY, sk_live_CANARY) are the planted test secrets and are expected throughout the transcripts. Internal hostnames, endpoint identifiers, and source IP addresses that incidentally appeared in the test environment have been redacted. Caveats (see the paper's Limitations and the README): the external-canary results (the image-GET validity check and the Gemini T-SLOP split) are scored from the collector's se
title: Run data and analysis code for "How Credentials Leak from 'Safe' LLM Coding Agents: An Attack-Surface Measurement"

summary: The UCT Flourish 2027 Co-Curriculum represents the second full annual cycle of an established student-facing programme developed through the Centre for Wellbeing and Flourishing at the University of Cape Town. Building directly on the 2026 cycle, the 2027 programme emphasises continuation, replication, refinement and cumulative learning rather than first-stage piloting. It is organised across five connected domains: Journey, Community, Amplify, Knowledge and Wisdom, spanning intrapsychic, interpersonal, infrastructural, interdependent and intergenerational dimensions of flourishing. The annual architecture combines a weekly VIA Character Strengths and Flourishing Seminar Series, a recurring Monthly Masterclass, two sustained 30 Days of TURN interventions, and a set of signature programmes including UCT Flourish Verse, the UCT Flourish Lab, the Student Summit and the Annual Wellbeing and Flourishing Conference. Programming is aligned with the academic calendar, public holidays, vacation periods and assessment demands, with deliberate pauses for consolidation, evaluation and research. At its centre is the question: What makes human flourishing possible? The co-curriculum creates recurring opportunities for students to develop psychological capacities, strengthen relationships, participate in university life, engage with evidence and scholarship, and contribute their own experiences and perspectives to a developing institutional conversation about flourishing. The 2027 programme remains provisional and non-exhaustive, allowing additional initiatives, partnerships and funded opportunities to be incorporated as they emerge.
title: UCT Flourish 2027: Proposed Provisional Annual Co-Curriculum

summary: Dataset Overview & Methodology This repository provides an experimentally enriched network traffic dataset designed to overcome severe class imbalance in Web attack detection . Focusing on the CICIDS2017 benchmark, which natively contains critically scarce instances for minority Web threats (such as only 21 SQL Injection flows), this dataset incorporates 32,670 authentic attack flows captured in a controlled experimental testbed . Key Characteristics Authentic Capture Environment: Unlike synthetic interpolation methods (e.g., SMOTE) that generate artificial data points within existing boundaries, this dataset captures real network traffic using an Apache XAMPP server and Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) . It features both automated scripts ( sqlmap , Hydra , Wfuzz ) and manual obfuscation vectors combined with normal background traffic . Feature-Space Consistency: Processed directly via CICFlowMeter to extract the exact 78 statistical flow features required to maintain complete compatibility with the original CICIDS2017 feature space . Rigorously Evaluated Classes: Web SQL Injection (significantly boosted to ensure robust pattern learning) . Web Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (including reflected and stored variants with filter-evasion techniques) . Web Brute Force (WBF) (generated through multi-day credential-guessing sessions) .

summary: This project investigates early training dynamics in robotic manipulation by comparing Truncated Quantile Critics (TQC), TQC with Hindsight Experience Replay (HER), and a reward-shaped TQC+HER variant in the sparse-reward FetchPickAndPlace-v4 environment. The proposed reward shaping provides intermediate signals for object contact, grasping, lifting, and moving toward the target, with all variants evaluated under matched training conditions using success rate, episode return, AUC, seed variance, and non-parametric significance testing. Results showed that baseline TQC and TQC+HER exhibited very limited early learning, while the reward-shaped variant achieved the best final performance but no statistically significant improvement, suggesting that simple hand-crafted reward shaping alone is insufficient to reliably improve early-stage learning in sparse robotic manipulation tasks.
title: Effects of Enhancing TQC with Reward Shaping on Early Training Dynamics in FetchPickAndPlace-v4

summary: Frequency-shift corrections are applied in deep-space navigation as a catalogue of formulas: common offsets, detector-end $O(c^{-3})$ cross terms and the nonlinear Doppler bias are re-derived for every mission and every data type. This paper derives the structure itself, from a single transitivity axiom. Under that axiom the endpoint factor of any light-path observable is a ratio of generators --- the \textbf{Fuxi value} $\FX_{A\|B}=\alpha_A/\alpha_B$ --- multiplied by a path factor; the generator is identified with the rate of proper-time flow, $\alpha_X=\mathrm d\tau_X/\mathrm dt_{\rm GalST}$. The resulting framework (Fuxi-ratio Mapping Theory, hereafter FMT) leaves the path-dependent transfer factor $\Pi_{\rm TTF}$ with the full complexity of the null-geodesic boundary-value problem, while its $1$PN expansion reproduces the standard frequency-shift formulas term by term at $O(c^{-2})$ and endows the IAU conversion constants $L_C,L_G,L_B$ with a direct generator interpretation. Three consequences are closed-form. \textbf{(i)} The projected pulsar-Doppler residual is \emph{exactly} linear in the relativistic velocity $\mathbf u\equiv\gamma\mathbf v$: the $O(c^{-3})$ kinematic term of the coordinate-velocity parameterization is a parameterization effect with the exact closed form $v_D^3/(2c^2)\,\hat{\mathbf v}_D$, removable in one analytic step, and \emph{identically absent} under $\mathbf u$. \textbf{(ii)} Isotropic and dipolar residual components are absorbed exactly --- the latter as a velocity error independent of the pulsar number and of the network geometry. \textbf{(iii)} Residuals of angular order $\ell\ge2$ are \emph{not} absorbed; their leakage is fixed by the higher moments of the pulsar directions, so precision and bias immunity are governed by different moments of the same network. Velocity identifiability is necessary and sufficient: the pulsar directions must not be cocircular. Model-internal consistency tests with a realistic 16-pulsar IPTA geometry reach $16.1\ \mu$m/s (three-axis RMS) at ideal timing precision $\sigma_\delta=10^{-13}$, and a full Earth-departure-to-Mars-surface arc is closed by the same expression with only its inputs changed. Both statements are model-internal limits: the term-by-term agreement with the standard formulas is limited to $O(c^{-2})$, the velocity figures presuppose an ephemeris residual $\delta C_P\lesssim3\times10^{-14}$, and practical accuracy is bounded by clock, ephemeris and direction knowledge. FMT modifies neither general relativity nor observational hardware: it is an algebraic interface callable on existing ephemerides and timing data.
title: Relativistic Doppler Velocimetry from One Transitivity Axiom: Exact Bias and Identifiability

summary: PGAA is an executable claim-state compiler for perturbation transcriptomics. It combines internal decision state, ranking stability, external evidence, source-data provenance, and branch-specific promotion gates to emit bounded manuscript claim states, so that an exploratory signal cannot be promoted to a biological or translational conclusion without the evidence a promotion rule requires. Distribution-aware statistics (a Wasserstein statistic for full expression-distribution shifts and a histogram-shape statistic for responder-associated expression-shape changes) are retained as upstream scoring modules that supply scores to the compiler; they are not claimed as the main methodological novelty. This archive is a code-only software release and excludes manuscript drafts, submission materials, figures, source-data tables, and review materials.
title: PGAA: a claim-state compiler for perturbation-transcriptomic evidence

summary: This record contains the first Lean-verified certificate in the Quantum–Classical Shared-Time working formalization series. Q1 establishes a common real-time mathematical structure for quantum and classical evolution. The certificate places both systems on the same time domain, formally represents their evolving states and time derivatives, and proves that when quantum and classical states correspond through an observation map at every time, their accumulated change between two times also corresponds exactly. The formalization includes normalized quantum-state evolution, classical phase-state evolution, shared-time structure, derivative uniqueness, and an orientation-independent change result that works in either direction between two times. This first milestone is intentionally foundational. It establishes the formal structure needed for the later quantum-to-classical bridge without yet assuming the Schrödinger equation, Ehrenfest theorem, Newtonian dynamics, or the later Chronos connection. The next stage is to formalize quantum expectation values and their time evolution as the next step toward a machine-checked Ehrenfest bridge connecting accepted quantum mechanics with accepted classical physics. This deposit is part of an ongoing formal validation program. The certificate package includes Lean source, reproducibility instructions, dependency and provenance documentation, build information, axiom audits, and checksums. The formal build passes without sorry, admit, or sorryAx placeholders.
title: Lean-Verified Quantum–Classical Shared-Time Bridge — Working Formal Verification Series Q1 (v0.1)

summary: Conventional capillary heat pipes route vapor and returning condensate through the same envelope, so the two streams interact along the entire transport length. This work reports a D-shaped two-phase loop that separates the two paths geometrically: a wicked vertical leg carries evaporation and vapor transport, and a curved copper return leg carries condensate back to a submerged reservoir at the base of the vertical leg, which acts as a hydrostatic trap that excludes vapor from the return path. Three additively manufactured triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) wicks of a common fill-ratio class and unit-cell size were tested in this envelope, gyroid, Schwarz Diamond, and Schwarz Primitive, together with a conventional copper-mesh heat pipe as benchmark. Devices were operated vertically at measured heater powers of 30.3, 40.5, and 50.8 W. Schwarz Diamond and gyroid gave the lowest power-averaged thermal resistance of the four configurations, reaching 1.70 and 1.69 ÅãC/W at 50.8W and holding the evaporator 23.7 and 20.1 ÅãC cooler than the benchmark at that power. Extrapolating the measured resistance to a length-scaled maximum heat-transport capability, Schwarz Diamond and gyroid exceed the copper-mesh benchmark by approximately 9% and 6% at the tested 0.30m length; these are single-run, architecture-level comparisons and are not repeated-trial estimates. Within this matched-class triplet, porosity identifies which structures form the leading pair while simulated single-phase permeability predicts the reverse ordering. Porosity is therefore the more reliable near-term predictor of thermal performance among architected lattices tested at a fixed fill-ratio class, though the device comparisons were not repeated and porosity remains one of several confounded structural parameters.
title: Porosity versus Permeability as Predictors of Thermal Performance in Architected TPMS Wicks for a D-Shaped Separated-Flow Heat Pipe

summary: This research edition studies a concrete finite part of the Riemann zeta function's spectral data. A packet is a chosen finite collection of its zeros, with every selected multiplicity retained. Its polynomial h divides the completed function g=2xi. The original theta-function source has Mellin transform g/h. Tensor products of this source represent sums of the selected zero jets, including their full repeated-root structure. The purpose is to calculate the cost of those spectral configurations in the original arithmetic source norm. It is not to choose a favorable new metric or to assert that an off-critical-line zero exists. What to read Main research reader, 482 pages. The complete literature-and-proof synthesis now includes Section 41 on arithmetic source/relation volumes and Section 42 on gamma convolution descent. The end of Section 42 proves the direct analytic generating-function map into the same Toda input. Split-Zero/Toda companion, 424 pages. A cumulative, more focused account of the source, its cohomological quotient and finite spectral controls, with 38 proof chapters and 18 complete source appendices. The new chapters calculate the separate source and relation curvature terms, certified theta-seed inputs, and an exact Gaussian calibration. Separate full source ZIPs. These retain the mathematical texts, formalization sources and scoped checking records for each reader. Earlier published PDFs and archives remain separate downloads. Gamma and endpoint workbenches. The delivered HTML/Markdown/LaTeX argument and its finite checker remain readable separately. The endpoint criterion and its gamma-coordinate substitution explain a finite-window way to choose one of the existing canonical representatives. The attempts, their motivation and their results Exterior trace control. Why it was tried: A single-vector bound can miss the combined displacement of many spectral directions. What it establishes: The finite exterior calculation bounds their aggregate positive trace defect using the same rank-two allowance, with multiplicities and source factors retained. Source and relation volumes. Why it was tried: Relations vanish in the quotient, but their source norms still affect the least-norm representatives. What it establishes: The determinant of the canonical quotient metric is exactly a source Hankel determinant divided by a relation Hankel determinant. Two Toda flows. Why it was tried: Both determinant sequences come from exponential deformation of the original arithmetic measure. What it establishes: Their derivative formulas calculate the source/relation curvature and the original complex cross term. The finite upper estimate retains explicit nonnegative losses. Gamma convolution descent. Why it was tried: Computing a new high-dimensional convolution integral for each tensor degree is expensive. What it establishes: A classical gamma reference, multiplied by the actual arithmetic amplitude, gives an exact all-tensor coefficient formula and an explicit tail majorant. Its relative-fibre component is retained. Analytic generating-function map. Why it was tried: The coefficient expansion and the Toda moment function appeared as separate descriptions of the same source. What it establishes: They are linked by an explicit analytic map and inverse. A degree-N Gram matrix differentiated j times uses only the one-factor coefficients through degree 2N+j. Endpoint degree selection. Why it was tried: Bounding every recurrence coefficient in a whole degree window is stronger than selecting one useful canonical degree. What it establishes: The written finite Jensen argument uses four endpoint quotient volumes and two endpoint polynomial norms. The gamma-coordinate version retains the exact reference and arithmetic correction factors. The quantities are attached to explicit maps At degree N the source is the original polynomial space, mapped to the cyclic algebra C[S]/(chi). The relation columns are multiplication by the original
title: Arithmetic zeta packets: quotient volumes, Toda control and gamma convolution

summary: Experimental-workflow release: the two loose ends of the measured-data path are closed, so a squeezing estimate needs no hand-entered inputs beyond the atom number. Added estimate_contrast / ContrastEstimate : the Ramsey fringe contrast fitted from a phase-scan shot record -- the number estimate_squeezing previously asked the user to bring from their own fringe fit. The mean fringe obeys A cos phi + B sin phi + d exactly (the rotation law of the mean spin, no lineshape assumption), so the fit is closed-form weighted linear least squares with per-phase standard errors, and the contrast uncertainty follows by the delta method through the exact WLS covariance -- the same structure and honesty as variance_tomography . Refusals: fewer than 3 distinct phases modulo 2 pi, and a fitted contrast above 1 beyond its uncertainty (reported as a probable N or J_z-calibration problem; a small statistical overshoot is returned as data, with the deliberate rounding left to the user, never clipped silently). save_shots_csv / load_shots_csv : a documented plain-text contract ( angle_rad,jz , one row per shot; ragged per-angle shot counts allowed) serving both tomography and fringe records -- the same data shape -- with exact round trips and refusals for malformed files and single-shot angles. Anchors (asserted in tests/test_fringe.py , not stated) Clean-record fringe recovery: contrast, phase and offset to 1e-7. Monte-Carlo scatter of the contrast estimate matches its reported sigma (ratio within [0.5, 2]), and the truth lies within the ensemble error. Degenerate phases (0, 2 pi, 4 pi) refused; an N four times too small triggers the exceeds-1 refusal. Exact file round trip with ragged shot counts; wrong header, single-shot angles and duplicate angles refused. The complete file-to-estimate pipeline -- fringe record -> estimate_contrast, tomography record -> estimate_squeezing, both through the contract -- recovers the standard quantum limit xi2_R = 1 on a coherent-spin-state record with no hand-entered contrast. Full test suite: 52 passed + 3 QuTiP-extra skips locally; all pass in CI with the extra installed (Python 3.9-3.13). Note: the two intermediate CI runs of this release failed only the version-metadata consistency test (the CITATION.cff bump landed in the following commit); the release head is green. See CHANGELOG.md for details.

summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.
title: Separating Capability from Permission in a Language Model: Prerequisite-Conditioned Native Continuation Control with Frozen Content

summary: NTI (Non-Termination Inference) is an open-source Java tool for proving termination and non-termination of term rewrite systems and logic programs. This reproducibility capsule accompanies the manuscript “NTI: Non-Termination Analysis for Term Rewriting and Logic Programming”. The capsule archives NTI version 2026.09, exactly as published at GitHub commit 88a47f9db976fc7c1ad1921057f0a68d68748137. It includes the complete source code, an executable JAR, compilation and usage documentation, license notices, and the corresponding sources of the bundled SAT4J Core 2.3.6 dependency. No additional source patch is required. summary: This is the public evidence deposit for the paper   Chaudhry Nouman Ali, Chitrakala Muthuveerappan and James Lim, "Deontic Insertion: How Large Language Model Extraction Supplies Modality That Building Regulation Does Not Carry" , JURIX 2026.   The paper reports that a large language model, asked to extract rules from New Zealand building regulation, writes deontic modality (`shall`, `must`, `may`) into its output where the source document carries none - most of all when the source is a table. This deposit contains the audit that establishes that claim: a single read-only script, the query registry that defines every figure, and pointer-only result tables for each query.   Everything here was produced by `jurix2026_freeze_audit.py` run against two frozen database snapshots, plus this README, the query registry, the licences, the citation file and Figure 1 of the paper.   Five regulation documents were ingested, sliced and extracted.
title: Deontic Insertion - evidence deposit

summary: Start here: Split-Zero Cohomology and Arithmetic Weight Control — the 715-page paper . This is the default PDF preview; the complete public source package accompanies it. Starting from the classical theta source for the completed Riemann zeta function, this continuation studies finite-dimensional coefficient spaces retaining selected zero multiplicities. It computes polynomial-representative and relation norms and quotient-volume changes over degree windows. Polynomial-exponential period integrals provide explicit coefficient maps and determinants and Deligne cohomology comparisons, preserving the original coordinates, measures, masses and maps. This cumulative edition includes the complete material through the R52 section of the paper. Subsequent work on period-subspace curvature, Hochschild traces and newer computer-checked algebra is outside this PDF and is tracked separately in the GitHub research sources . All 32 preceding downloads are retained with their existing rights and notices. The complete public source derivative documents local-locator redactions and a reference-only exclusion in its provenance and manifest; the unchanged original archive remains privately preserved. This is a research working-paper edition, not a claim to have proved the Riemann Hypothesis. Written arguments and finite checks have distinct scopes; finite regression checks are not general theorem certification. Attribution remains under the existing public handle, KokunoYumeto. No blanket license is asserted over third-party material or source results.
title: Split-Zero arithmetic endpoint: exact periods, determinants and Deligne comparison

summary: This white paper examines decision authenticity as an emerging enterprise governance requirement in an environment where synthetic voice, video, executive likeness, and real-time presence increasingly weaken traditional signals of authority. The paper argues a meeting remains useful for discussion and judgment, but no longer provides sufficient evidence for an irreversible decision. High-risk commitments instead require structured verification of identity, authority, intent, context, independence, and evidence. The analysis uses the 2024 Arup deepfake fraud, the WPP executive impersonation attempt, and the LastPass CEO voice-cloning incident to demonstrate three distinct mechanisms. Arup shows the financial consequence of meeting-based authority. WPP shows how attackers manufacture apparent corroboration across multiple communication channels. LastPass shows how verification culture and employee interruption stop synthetic authority before irreversible action occurs. The paper introduces the Trust Compression Attack framework, describing how authority, familiarity, social proof, urgency, isolation, and irreversibility combine to compress weak trust signals into a short decision window. The paper then introduces the Decision Authenticity Stack, a six-layer operating architecture covering Identity, Authority, Intent, Context, Independence, and Evidence. Together, these frameworks move enterprise control away from perceptual verification and toward provable authorisation. The operating model separates Discussion Objects, Decision Objects, and Execution Objects so conversations provide context without automatically creating authority. Risk tiers then match stronger controls to consequence, reversibility, reach, and external impact. Critical and crisis decisions require transaction-bound approval, independent verification, separation of duties, phishing-resistant authentication, defined expiry, and durable evidence. The paper extends decision authenticity beyond human impersonation into agentic AI, where machine identity, scope, permissions, policy version, human sponsorship, and attributable execution become part of the same governance problem. The central proposition is direct: presence is not authority, fluency is not authority, and access is not authority. Enterprise authority must be explicit, bounded, independently verified, and provable.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 11 August 2026.

summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. summary: Physics upgrade: local-oscillator phase noise, the effect that decides how much squeezing a real homodyne detector keeps. New phase_noise_variance : the measured quadrature variance under Gaussian phase jitter, V = V_sq cos^2(theta) + V_anti sin^2(theta) averaged exactly over theta ~ N(theta_0, sigma^2) via the closed form <cos 2theta> = cos(2 theta_0) exp(-2 sigma^2) (Dwyer et al., Opt. Express 21, 19047 (2013); Oelker et al., Optica 3, 682 (2016); the same quadratic form used for integrated squeezers in Dean et al., npj Nanophotonics, 2026, doi:10.1038/s44310-026-00125-5). phase_noise_squeezing_db : the same statement in the dB form labs quote. max_phase_noise : the inverse question - the largest RMS phase jitter compatible with a target detected variance - with honest refusals when the target is below the intrinsic squeezing ("cannot improve") or above the jitter-saturated midpoint ("not phase-noise-limited"). Anchors (asserted in tests, never stored numbers) The closed-form Gaussian average against independent numerical quadrature over the phase distribution (two code paths, 1e-10). Exact limits: zero jitter reproduces the static rotation law; infinite jitter lands on (V_sq + V_anti)/2; vacuum is an exact fixed point; monotonicity in sigma. max_phase_noise round-trips through phase_noise_variance exactly, and both refusals fire. Loss and phase-noise channels commute exactly (both are affine maps with the vacuum fixed point) - asserted, not assumed. 85 tests pass on Python 3.9-3.13.

Express 21, 19047 (2013); Oelker et al., Optica 3, 682 (2016); the same quadratic form used for integrated squeezers in Dean et al., npj Nanophotonics, 2026, doi:10.1038/s44310-026-00125-5). phase_noise_squeezing_db : the same statement in the dB form labs quote. max_phase_noise : the inverse question - the largest RMS phase jitter compatible with a target detected variance - with honest refusals when the target is below the intrinsic squeezing ("cannot improve") or above the jitter-saturated midpoint ("not phase-noise-limited"). Anchors (asserted in tests, never stored numbers) The closed-form Gaussian average against independent numerical quadrature over the phase distribution (two code paths, 1e-10). Exact limits: zero jitter reproduces the static rotation law; infinite jitter lands on (V_sq + V_anti)/2; vacuum is an exact fixed point; monotonicity in sigma. max_phase_noise round-trips through phase_noise_variance exactly, and both refusals fire. Loss and phase-noise channels commute exactly (both are affine maps with the vacuum fixed point) - asserted, not assumed. 85 tests pass on Python 3.9-3.13.

summary: This chapter explores the epistemic tensions faced by researchers, particularly those from formerly colonized countries in the Global South, caught between the demands of scientific neutrality and ethical engagement with the coloniality of knowledge. In dialogue with Critical Theory and decolonial thought, the chapter highlights epistemic resilience as a posture of resistance and reconstruction of meaning. The Haitian case study, through the heritage-based preservation of the memory of slavery, illustrates how cognitive justice can serve as a bridge between emancipatory rationality and the pluriversal horizon of decoloniality. Published as a chapter (pp. 239-257) of EDUCATORÉ. Educating and Reflecting for Resilient, Critically Aware Societies, Maria Grzegorzewska University Press, Warsaw.
title: Epistemological tensions and researcher resilience in a context of coloniality: navigating between neutrality and engagement

summary: Abstract: Livestock production is central to rural livelihoods across sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in pastoral, agro-pastoral, and smallholder farming systems. Livestock provide food, income, savings, employment, insurance against shocks, manure, and social and cultural capital. However, the contribution of livestock to household welfare depends not only on production but also on households' ability to participate effectively in livestock markets and obtain fair returns. This review synthesizes literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026, with particular attention to pastoral and smallholder systems in East Africa. The evidence shows that market infrastructure, market information, producer organizations, transport, veterinary services, financial services, value addition, and improved market governance can reduce transaction costs, increase market participation, improve producer returns, and strengthen livelihood resilience. Evidence from Ethiopia demonstrates that improved livestock market sheds can increase smallholder earnings, while evidence from northern Kenya indicates that improvements in physical and communication infrastructure have strengthened market integration. However, market participation does not automatically improve welfare. Drought, climate variability, conflict, distress sales, weak bargaining power, gender inequalities, inadequate services, and restrictions on pastoral mobility can limit or reverse livelihood gains. Informal information networks, brokers, customary institutions, and cross-border trade also remain important in connecting remote producers to markets. The review therefore argues that livestock marketing should move beyond increasing sales volumes toward resilient, inclusive, equitable, and sustainable livestock value chains. Effective interventions should integrate market infrastructure, information, producer organization, animal health, finance, value addition, climate-risk management, gender empowerment, rangeland governance, conflict management, and predictable trade regulation.

summary: This record contains three components from the SLD experiment at the SLAC Linear Collider (SLC): the reconstructed mini-Data Summary Tapes (mini-DSTs) covering the full 1996–1998 data-taking periods, the corresponding simulated (Monte Carlo) mini-DSTs, and an AI-ready corpus of digitized SLD-era internal documentation. This version (v3) adds the simulated samples to the reconstructed data and documentation corpus released in v2, and supersedes the earlier releases. Both the collision events and the simulated events are made available in two formats: the native binary “jazelle” columnar format used by the SLD reconstruction software, and a derived Apache Parquet translation that is convenient for modern columnar analysis tools (PyArrow, pandas, awkward, polars, ...). The two formats contain identical physics content. The Parquet version is the one most users will want. Reconstructed data 68 mini-DST files covering the 1996, 1997, and 1998 runs. After translation and reading via the  jazelle  Python package, the dataset contains 658,241 reconstructed events. The center-of-mass energy is at the Z pole (√s ≈ 91.2 GeV) and the electron beam was longitudinally polarized, with mean magnitude 76.14% for the 1996 run and 73.08% for the 1997–1998 runs. Per-event polarization values are recorded in the PHBM bank. Bank families Reconstruction outputs are organized into “bank families”, each describing one detector subsystem or one stage of the reconstruction chain. The banks present in this release: IEVENTH  — event header (run/event ID, trigger mask, timestamp). PHBM  — beam information (beam energy, beam polarization magnitude and sign, interaction-point position and uncertainty). PHPSUM  — inclusive list of reconstructed physics particles (4-momentum, charge, origin coordinates). PHCHRG  — charged-track helix parameters, error matrices, hit counts, fit quality, and dE/dx from the Central Drift Chamber (CDC) and VXD3 vertex detector. PHKLUS  — calorimeter clusters from the Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAC), with raw and per-layer energies. PHCRID  — Cherenkov ring likelihoods for particle identification from the Cherenkov Ring Imaging Detector (CRID). PHWIC  — muon tracking in the Warm Iron Calorimeter (WIC). PHKELID  — electron identification from track-calorimeter matching. PHPOINT  — master pointer bank linking each PHPSUM entry to its associated track (PHCHRG) and/or calorimeter cluster (PHKLUS), enabling per-particle access to detector-level quantities. PHKCHRG  — track-to-cluster matching kinematics. The mini-DSTs are the reduced-format event records produced by the SLD reconstruction. They contain enough information for typical physics analyses (event shapes, electroweak asymmetries, jet clustering) but not the full raw detector data. Only the standard reconstruction-level data-quality requirements suppressing non-collision backgrounds are applied. No channel-specific event selection is pre-applied. Further documentation on the jazelle file format and the field-level contents of each bank can be found in the README of the jazelle package GitHub repository (see “Related identifiers” for a link). Sample statistics Total events: 658,241 (102,699 from 1996, 555,542 from 1997–1998) Hadronic Z → qq̄: 385,583 (2000 A LR  selection) Z → e + e − : 16,547 (2001 leptonic selection) Z → μ + μ − : 13,992 (2001 leptonic selection) Z → τ + τ − : 17,133 (2001 leptonic selection) Mean particles / event: 54.4 Mean charged particles / event: 13.4 Mean |P e |: 76.14% (1996), 73.08% (1997–1998) Simulated events (Monte Carlo) New in v3. Simulated mini-DSTs produced by the SLD collaboration's own simulation and reconstruction chain, recovered from the SLAC archives alongside the data. The sample contains 260,94
title: SLD reconstructed mini-DSTs from the 1996-1998 SLC runs and documentation corpus

The two formats contain identical physics content. The Parquet version is the one most users will want. Reconstructed data 68 mini-DST files covering the 1996, 1997, and 1998 runs. After translation and reading via the  jazelle  Python package, the dataset contains 658,241 reconstructed events. The center-of-mass energy is at the Z pole (√s ≈ 91.2 GeV) and the electron beam was longitudinally polarized, with mean magnitude 76.14% for the 1996 run and 73.08% for the 1997–1998 runs. Per-event polarization values are recorded in the PHBM bank. Bank families Reconstruction outputs are organized into “bank families”, each describing one detector subsystem or one stage of the reconstruction chain. The banks present in this release: IEVENTH  — event header (run/event ID, trigger mask, timestamp). PHBM  — beam information (beam energy, beam polarization magnitude and sign, interaction-point position and uncertainty). PHPSUM  — inclusive list of reconstructed physics particles (4-momentum, charge, origin coordinates). PHCHRG  — charged-track helix parameters, error matrices, hit counts, fit quality, and dE/dx from the Central Drift Chamber (CDC) and VXD3 vertex detector. PHKLUS  — calorimeter clusters from the Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAC), with raw and per-layer energies. PHCRID  — Cherenkov ring likelihoods for particle identification from the Cherenkov Ring Imaging Detector (CRID). PHWIC  — muon tracking in the Warm Iron Calorimeter (WIC). PHKELID  — electron identification from track-calorimeter matching. PHPOINT  — master pointer bank linking each PHPSUM entry to its associated track (PHCHRG) and/or calorimeter cluster (PHKLUS), enabling per-particle access to detector-level quantities. PHKCHRG  — track-to-cluster matching kinematics. The mini-DSTs are the reduced-format event records produced by the SLD reconstruction. They contain enough information for typical physics analyses (event shapes, electroweak asymmetries, jet clustering) but not the full raw detector data. Only the standard reconstruction-level data-quality requirements suppressing non-collision backgrounds are applied. No channel-specific event selection is pre-applied. Further documentation on the jazelle file format and the field-level contents of each bank can be found in the README of the jazelle package GitHub repository (see “Related identifiers” for a link). summary: A foundational brief and research program. Behavioral economics measured human decision-making across five decades and thousands of experiments. In not one of those paradigms was the physiological state of the subject a controlled variable: nutritional status, inflammatory load, autonomic state, and cholinergic tone appear in no methods section. This paper argues that the field recorded the signatures of chronic substrate deficit with genuine rigour and entered the result into the literature as human nature. Definition. Luminous Behavioral Economics is the design discipline that engineers environments in which thriving is the path of least resistance — grounding the nervous system that does the choosing, developing the altitude of the one who chooses, and propagating itself through every being it grounds — thereby translating the regulated individual floor into the living architecture of a thriving civilisation. Standard choice architecture steers; it does not ground, develop, or propagate. The paper honours its lineage (Simon on bounded rationality, Kahneman and Tversky on the shape of the bounds, Thaler and Sunstein on the non-neutrality of choice environments, Ostrom on self-sustaining structure) and then identifies four sentences in the field's foundation that end one clause early: the chooser is treated as a flawed optimiser rather than an intelligent nervous system reading its conditions; there is no floor; there is no developmental axis; and the structure cannot propagate without a permanent class of architects. An indictment is stated directly. If the diagnosis holds, then economics, public policy, and business practice have been built on a false picture of the human being and built so as to reinforce it — across nine named domains: nudge policy that accommodates the deficit without repairing it; attention markets in which depletion is a revenue input; consumer credit that prices the discount curve as a feature; workplace design that strips the co-regulation nervous systems require; compensation and monitoring that manufacture the self-interest they assume; means-tested welfare that levies cognitive load on those with least bandwidth; education that trains suppression of the somatic signal; healthcare that treats depletion downstream and rarely upstream; and, gravest, social discount rates calibrated against the time preference of depleted nervous systems — encoding the clearest signature of a depleted floor into the mathematics by which a species decides whether its descendants matter. The pattern is one failure replicated: each system accommodates, profits from, or imposes the deficit, and none repair it. Five completions (the floor axiom, bias as signal, the developmental axis, self-propagation, and the translation function) and seven operators (grounding defaults, reframes, win-win-win incentives, developmental pricing, regulation rituals, lateral social proof, and the door) specify the discipline as buildable rather than rhetorical. The research program states the core hypothesis in falsifiable form: bias magnitudes measured in the classical paradigms are partly substrate-dependent and will shift under floor restoration, tested against an active control using canonical instruments. The measurement problem is stated rather than finessed — there is no clean control group, because there is no reservoir of reliably grounded subjects and therefore no true zero — with within-subject designs, natural experiments, and dose-response gradients offered as partial routes. Five refutation conditions close the paper: if bias magnitudes do not move under floor restoration in a properly powered sample, the discipline is empty. Thirty-three sources. Companion to the five-essay Spine. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.

summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. Handling at the laboratory bench (v3.1.0): the fragment editor as a three-step procedure that counts the marked contractions against the protocol and lets each be kept, dropped, split or dragged, with the detection sensitivity set per practical and recorded in the report and the CSV; a single running instance with a start-up splash; pictures of the electrode placement and the calibration in the guided tour; and a printable sheet for each station of the agonist/antagonist practical. emgteach runs on Windows, macOS and Linux with Python 3.10–3.12, is cov

Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. summary: ToMAS is a pilot failure-grounded Theory-of-Mind evaluation package derived from MAST FC2 inter-agent misalignment failures in multi-agent LLM systems.   This deposit includes: 39 CLEAN training items 28 held-out Magentic/GAIA items 39 Coord-RL (LLM-Coordination ToM) training items four-criterion convertibility annotation rubric 18-item reliability pilot coding sheet (Cohen's κ = 0.92) ROUGE-L binary scoring scripts GRPO training script (train_condition.py) training reward logs and adapter/train-compare diagnostics v1.1 added conversion rationales for all 28 held-out items. v1.2 adds train_condition.py, GRPO reward logs, the Coord-RL training file, and adapter/train-compare diagnostics requested for the accompanying paper. Items are derived/converted/modified from MAST-Data (Hugging Face: mcemri/MAST-Data; cemri2025mast) under CC-BY-4.0. Users must attribute both ToMAS (this deposit) and MAST-Data. Coord-RL items additionally adapt ToM questions from LLM-Coordination (Agashe et al., NAACL Findings 2025). This package does not include model checkpoints or the full MAST dump. It supports the pilot benchmark-construction and training-feasibility study described in the accompanying paper.

summary: Essay Five of the Spine, and its last. Every generation since the telegraph has announced the imminent arrival of a planetary mind — cable, radio, television, packet network, social graph, foundation model. Each announcement was made in good faith, the substrate genuinely improved by orders of magnitude each time, and each time the planetary mind failed to arrive or arrived in a degraded form that amplified reactivity rather than cognition. The consistency of that failure across radically different technical substrates points away from the technology and toward the sequence. The ordering claim: a holon becomes available when the holon beneath it completes, and you cannot reach the noosphere by skipping the floor. A planetary information system built from depleted nervous systems does not produce planetary thought but planetary reactivity — the engagement equilibrium is not a design failure but the predictable output of a system maximising attention capture among nervous systems already running threat-detection at elevated baseline. The substrate question precedes the design question. The noosphere is therefore not built but crossed: a phase transition, modelled on percolation, in which what percolates depends entirely on what the nodes are. The essay then takes up the operator question — a second-tier system requires third-tier operators, because the steward of a system must be able to take the system's own logic as object rather than being subject to it — and argues that developmental altitude is substrate-dependent rather than purely cognitive, which converts operator scarcity from an intractable condition into a supply problem with a known intervention. The substrate section distinguishes a forest from a monoculture: the design criterion for a planetary computational layer is not scale or distribution but whether its components genuinely differentiate, since a system without internal membranes cannot contain its own failure modes. The invariant closes at the noetic membrane: a mind whose knowing includes the cost of its knowing. And the workbook is deliberately identical to Essay One's — lie on the floor, induce the tremor, measure the resolution of the perceptual field for fourteen days — because the noosphere is made of floors. The cosmology is refutable on a living-room floor in under two weeks. The coda declines to name what lies above the fifth rung. Thirty-three sources. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.
title: The Noosphere: The Holon That Comes Next
