summary: This repository contains the code and data used to prepare a manuscript titled "Flow dependence of boundary-layer scheme parameters revealed by stochastic inversion".  Code: The data were produced with two different ideal cases of the Weather Research and Forecasting Model (WRF): (1) WRFlux v1.7.0 in large-eddy simulation (LES) configuration, available at https://github.com/matzegoebel/WRFlux/ and (2) WRF v4.4.2 in single-column model configuration ( https://github.com/wrf-model/WRF/releases/tag/v4.4.2 ).  The LES and SCM simulations represent the evolution of a convective boundary layer in the atmosphere over flat terrain. To reproduce the LES simulation, download WRFlux v1.7.0 from the link above, compile as usual and run it using the namelist file and input sounding provided in LES.zip.  To reproduce the deterministic SCM simulations, a modified version of WRF v4.4.2 is needed. Download WRF v4.4.2 and replace the corresponding files with those provided in this repository under WRF_SCM.zip, then compile as usual. These modifications allow for variable parameters in the YSU planetary boundary layer (PBL) scheme instead of prescribed constant ones. The parameter values are controlled via the namelist: ysu_pfactor ( p ), ysu_bfactor ( b ), and ysu_entrainment_hfx_mag ( Ae ). WRF_SCM.zip also contains the namelist file, input sounding, and surface forcing file (scmflx_bdy) needed to run the simulation. The input sounding and scmflx_bdy files are the same for all SCM runs. To reproduce the ensemble of SCM simulations, the modified version of WRF coupled with a modified version of DART-WRF v2024.2.20 ( https://github.com/lkugler/DART-WRF/releases/tag/v2024.2.20 ) is needed. Here, DART-WRF is used only to generate an ensemble of forecasts. Download DART-WRF v2024.2.20 and copy the files provided in DART-WRF_SCM.zip into the matching paths of the DART-WRF source tree, overwriting the originals. DART-WRF_SCM.zip also contains the parameter perturbation files needed to run the large ensembles (as .txt files). The large ensembles are subject to parameter perturbations only. SINGLE_PARAMETER_PERTURBATION_EXP: contains directories for each parameter with varying parameter values (still deterministic runs), e.g., in Ae_0.0 parameter Ae is set to 0 and the other two parameters remain at their prescribed values. SCM_ensemble.zip: contains all SCM ensemble runs produced with the modified version of WRF via DART-WRF. P_B_AE_C1_ensemble_27000_5min.nc: large ensemble simulation (N=27 000) with parameter perturbations for all three YSU parameters (parameter perturbation files in DART-WRF_SCM.zip), output every 5 minutes. This file is the raw ensemble from which all posterior distributions below are derived. P_C1_ensemble_N10000.nc: large ensemble simulation (N=10 000) with parameter perturbations for parameter  p only. POSTERIOR_MARGINAL_DISTRIBUTIONS: contains time dependent marginal posterior distributions as a function of each parameter (e.g., MARGINAL_Ae.npy) and their respective bins (e.g., MARGINAL_Ae_bins.npy). summary: The Empirical-Axiomatic Framework (EAF) is a broader foundational framework concerned with existence, ontological structure, consistency, logic, information, representation, knowledge, scientific modelling, consciousness, and related philosophical questions. This paper develops the epistemological part of EAF by establishing a conceptual relation between underlying structures, representations, information, self, epistemic architecture, epistemic capacity, and knowledge. The paper distinguishes the Universal Information Space from the Ontological Information Space and defines knowledge as information possessed by a self, where a self is understood as a well-defined system. It further distinguishes generalised knowledge from Traditional Knowledge, with Traditional Knowledge requiring comprehended structural correspondence between a representation and the underlying structure it represents. The paper analyses epistemic activities, knowledge generation, representation changes, generator bases, and the limitations of epistemic systems. It distinguishes incomplete representations from incorrect representations and epistemic limitations from ontological limitations. A computer is examined as a detailed example of a non-biological epistemic system capable of acquiring, storing, processing, transforming, representing, and communicating information without these capacities necessarily implying consciousness or Traditional Knowledge. The framework is then applied to major epistemological and related philosophical problems, including induction, Gödel’s incompleteness problem, material implication, the philosophy of mathematics, Benacerraf’s problem, Gettier’s problem, demarcation, the Münchhausen trilemma, Sorites, and universals. The paper does not claim to provide final solutions to all these problems. Rather, it offers a unified conceptual basis for reframing them through the relations among existence, structure, representation, information, and epistemic systems. The resulting framework provides a foundation for further formal, scientific, and philosophical development within EAF.
title: Epistemology within the Empirical-Axiomatic Framework

summary: Predictive maintenance has become one of the most important approaches for improving reliability, efficiency, and operational continuity in modern industrial enterprises. Unlike corrective maintenance, which is performed after equipment failure, and preventive maintenance, which follows predetermined schedules, predictive maintenance relies on real-time condition monitoring and data analysis to estimate the probability of future faults. The aim of this study was to analyze modern predictive maintenance methods used for industrial machinery and equipment and to evaluate their advantages, limitations, and practical applications. A literature-based analytical approach was used to examine vibration analysis, temperature monitoring, acoustic emission, oil analysis, electrical signature analysis, Internet of Things technologies, machine learning, digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based diagnostic systems. The analysis indicates that combining sensor-based monitoring with intelligent data analytics can identify abnormal equipment behavior before catastrophic failure occurs. Predictive maintenance can reduce unplanned downtime, optimize spare-parts management, extend equipment life, and decrease maintenance costs. However, successful implementation depends on sensor reliability, data quality, appropriate algorithms, integration with industrial control systems, and qualified personnel. Predictive maintenance should therefore be considered a key component of smart manufacturing and modern industrial asset management.
tags: predictive maintenance, industrial machinery, condition monitoring, machine learning, vibration analysis, IoT, digital twin, equipment reliability.

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22734670 . What the paper claims This is an evidence map of 11,628 PubMed-indexed records on generative language models in healthcare, January 2023 to June 2026, built to answer one question: is the clinical literature keeping pace with the systems it evaluates? The central construct is evaluation lag, the number of quarters between the release of the newest model family a study names and that study's own publication quarter. Mean lag widens from 1.33 to 6.08 quarters. Because a discontinued family ages at exactly one quarter per quarter, the authors benchmark that rise against a counterfactual holding 2023 model composition fixed, and find that migration to newer systems offsets 56.2% of the drift (95% CI 49.9-65.2, 2,000 bootstrap resamples). By design, randomised controlled trials evaluate models 4.62 quarters older than other empirical designs (95% CI 3.62-5.63), yet among the records naming a family still receiving releases no design differs from any other; what separates designs is the probability of studying a discontinued family at all, 62.1% for randomised trials against 15.6% for preprints. The framing is right and the execution is unusually careful for a bibliometric paper. Reporting the mechanical ageing rate as the null instead of zero, validating the decomposition by showing that discontinued-only records widen at 1.062 quarters per quarter, and running a pessimistic sensitivity analysis that assumes the earliest release of every named family are all things this literature normally omits. The version-specification result in Section 2 deserves to be read on its own: randomised trials specify the model version in 50.0% of cases, the lowest of any empirical design, which means half of the highest-tier evidence cannot be attributed to a determinate system. My comments below are about three places where the reported precision outruns the design. Does the conclusion hold on the data? 1. Evaluation lag is measured on a differentially selected half of the corpus, and the headline comparison is between designs that differ in exactly that selection. Lag is computable for 5,775 of 11,628 records, and coverage by design runs from 87.0% for comparative evaluations and 69.0% for randomised trials down to 36.2% for preprints and 27.0% for reviews. The paper states this plainly, which is to its credit, but the between-design contrast is its central result and the missingness is both large and design-dependent. The direction is not obvious either: if preprints name a model in the abstract mainly when that model is the novelty on sale, the preprint advantage is inflated; if trials omit the name when the system is an incidental component, the trial penalty may be understated. Two things would settle it. Worst-case bounds in the Manski sense across the plausible range would show whether the ordering survives at all, and a full-text audit of a random sample, a few hundred records stratified by design, would give an empirical estimate of how the non-naming records differ. Without one of those, the contrast rests on an assumption of ignorable missingness that the paper does not state. 2. The abstract quotes the specification that maximises the effect and omits the one that does not survive correction. The median regression gives 4.62 quarters at P = 3.4 x 10^-19; ordinary least squares on the same specification gives an adjusted difference of 1.57 quarters, P = 0.021, and after Holm correction across the seven design contrasts P = 0.084. Median regression is the defensible choice for a strongly right-skewed distribution and the paper says so, so this is not a case of specification shopping. It is a case of a reader meeting one number and not the other. The magnitude differs by a factor of about three between estimators, and the abstract should carry that range, or at minimum state that the estimate

summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. Handling at the laboratory bench (v3.1.0): the fragment editor as a three-step procedure that counts the marked contractions against the protocol and lets each be kept, dropped, split or dragged, with the detection sensitivity set per practical and recorded in the report and the CSV; a single running instance with a start-up splash; pictures of the electrode placement and the calibration in the guided tour; and a printable sheet for each station of the agonist/antagonist practical. Patch 3.1.1: the co-activation of a named window is read on the uncut r
title: emgteach: an open-source teaching platform for surface electromyography

summary: Abstract Fungi are an ecologically diverse and important kingdom of life because of their roles in ecosystems. Current studies show that this kingdom remains underexplored and that much of its diversity is still unknown. Moreover, fungi contribute to several aspects of our well-being. They are used in the food and cosmetic industries as additives; they are found in fermented foods and beverages; and they have been used for ages in traditional Chinese medicine. The most important role is to serve in agriculture as biocontrol agents, nematicides derived from fungi, and drugs such as antibacterials, antimycotics, immunosuppressants, and cardiovascular drugs that are in use or derived from fungi.  Nevertheless, one major problem we face worldwide is the rising number of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria, fungi, and fungus-like organisms. Therefore, there is an urgent need for new drugs with a novel structure and perhaps a new mode of action to address this problem. One way to find new drugs is to explore more natural products, because around 50 percent of the drugs on the market are natural products or are somehow derived from them. Fungi play an interesting role in this because, as mentioned, they are underexplored. For a reason, it is easy to find unexplored biodiversity, together with unexplored chemical diversity. Studying fungi from less exploited taxa, geographic regions, and ecological niches can improve success. Proper identification of fungal species using a modern polyphasic approach will also help study new or interesting, not-so-well-studied taxa. Moreover, insight into biosynthetic gene clusters can provide an overview of an organism's capacity. Several different approaches are needed to activate the BCGs, which are silent under laboratory conditions. The use of different media, co-cultivation, or even genetic manipulation could be helpful. This thesis demonstrates the potential of diverse ecological environments and neglected habitats, such as dung, for identifying new fungi and natural products. Moreover, the thesis provides insight into the heterologous expression of natural products from the basidiomycete Cyclocybe aegerita , to investigate its terpene biosynthesis. Two fungi from different environmental regions: one is from a tree in a forest in Thailand, and the other was isolated from soil in Hong Kong, were investigated for their secondary metabolites. The fungus from Thailand was identified as Resupinatus sp., and the soil-borne fungus is the ascomycete Morinagamyces vermucularis . Both strains yielded several new natural products that showed activity in our in-house test panel. This could give them a potential application within different fields. With the heterologous expression of the Agr2 terpene synthase from Cyclocybe agerita , we could identify a bifunctional terpene synthase that gives rise to both a new diterpene and the known sesquiterpene viridiflorene. This first result can provide knowledge to continue identifying the diverse terpene biosynthesis in Basidiomycota. In the last part of the thesis, coprophilous fungi isolated from herbivorous dung samples collected in northern Germany were isolated and investigated. Our research led to the discovery of a new species of Parascedosporium and a new species of Scytalidium , as well as an updated description of two Collariella species. In conclusion, this study highlights the great capacity still hidden in the fungal kingdom, in both its biodiversity and its secondary metabolites. Moreover, the thesis findings are part of addressing global problems such as biodiversity loss, antibiotic resistance, and antifungal resistance.

Moreover, the thesis findings are part of addressing global problems such as biodiversity loss, antibiotic resistance, and antifungal resistance.

summary: Abstract Fungi are an ecologically diverse and important kingdom of life because of their roles in ecosystems. Current studies show that this kingdom remains underexplored and that much of its diversity is still unknown. Moreover, fungi contribute to several aspects of our well-being. They are used in the food and cosmetic industries as additives; they are found in fermented foods and beverages; and they have been used for ages in traditional Chinese medicine. The most important role is to serve in agriculture as biocontrol agents, nematicides derived from fungi, and drugs such as antibacterials, antimycotics, immunosuppressants, and cardiovascular drugs that are in use or derived from fungi.  Nevertheless, one major problem we face worldwide is the rising number of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria, fungi, and fungus-like organisms. Therefore, there is an urgent need for new drugs with a novel structure and perhaps a new mode of action to address this problem. summary: Abstract Let ρ₅ᴿ be the largest element growth possible in exact Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting on real 5 × 5 matrices, with every legal choice at a pivot tie allowed. We prove ρ₅ᴿ = α = 4.132517078632472854223346853277…, where α is the algebraic lower bound identified by Chen, Edelman, and Urschel, specified by their degree-61 polynomial and a rational isolating interval. Our contribution is the global upper bound. An exact inverse-elimination representation retains all initial and intermediate entry bounds of the same matrix. A constructive contraction preserves the final-pivot height while reducing the problem to two saturated tail geometries. On the negative-diagonal geometry, three feasible paths eliminate six variables and give an attained fibre maximum over seventeen shared parameters. Rational certificates control the remaining domains, while a constrained algebraic maximum argument and feasible transports resolve regions meeting the sharp value. The proof combines these analytic reductions with exact verification of a finite, complete cover. We provide a partial Lean formalization together with publicly available exact certificates and verification code. Files and supporting materials This record contains the 56-page manuscript and its 7-page supplementary index. Both PDFs are archived unchanged from the fixed GitHub release v1.0.1. The supplementary index maps proof responsibilities S1–S8 to the original proof objects and verifier entry points. Source code, exact certificates, verification guides and file manifests are available at GitHub release v1.0.1 . The original certificate assets remain frozen under v1.0.0 and are linked from that release. Formalization scope The recorded first-phase Lean project cold rebuild passed 634 product modules, three additional example/audit modules and 47 named axiom checks, using an explicit dependency-order driver with pinned third-party caches reused and supplemented. The final sharp Lean equality remains conditional on XGlobalSafety and RootEndpointSafety. This is a partial Lean formalization accompanying the computer-assisted proof; neither a complete unconditional Lean proof nor formal verification of the Python/C++ acceptor implementations is claimed. The frozen PDFs retain the publication-status wording at the time of their GitHub release; this Zenodo record supplies their archival deposit.
title: The exact maximum growth factor for complete pivoting on real 5 × 5 matrices

summary: The translation of emotional language in literary discourse involves not only the transfer of lexical meaning but also the reconstruction of emotional intensity, evaluative connotation, psychological stance, and pragmatic effect. The present study investigates lexical-emotional transformations in the Arabic translation of Abdulla Qodiriy’s novel O‘tkan kunlar, published in Arabic as Al-Ayyām al-Khawālī ( الأيام الخوالي ) in 2024. The research is based on a comparative linguopragmatic analysis of emotionally marked units selected from the Uzbek source text and their Arabic correspondences. The examples were examined according to three interrelated parameters: semantic content, emotional intensity, and pragmatic function. The analysis revealed several recurrent patterns, including direct emotional correspondence, grammatical recategorization, semantic-pragmatic attenuation, preservation of emotional intensity, contextual specification, and metaphorical-emotional recreation. The findings demonstrate that lexical-semantic equivalence does not necessarily guarantee an equivalent emotional effect. In some cases, Arabic preserves both the type and intensity of the source emotion; in others, the emotional meaning is attenuated or conceptually reorganized. Conversely, metaphorical emotion may be successfully recreated through a different but functionally corresponding lexical image. The study therefore argues that emotional translation should be assessed beyond lexical equivalence by considering the degree to which the target text reconstructs the emotional and pragmatic potential of the source expression.
tags: literary translation, emotional language, linguopragmatics, Abdulla Qodiriy, O'tkan kunlar, Arabic translation, emotional intensity, pragmatic equivalence, lexical transformation.
title: EMOTIONAL TRANSFORMATIONS IN THE ARABIC TRANSLATION OF ABDULLA QODIRIY'S O'TKAN KUNLAR (BYGONE DAYS): A LINGUOPRAGMATIC ANALYSIS

summary: Patinae v0.5.0 Zawinski's law says that programs keep expanding until they can read email. Patinae started as a molecular viewer. It now has background tasks, Markdown output, and an AI plugin that can connect to MCP servers. We appear to be one mail server away from compliance. The largest change in 0.5.0 is underneath all of that: the task system has been completely rebuilt around one shared lifecycle . Loading a structure, running a script, and asking a plugin to do background work now use the same rules for completion, progress, errors, and cancellation. Those rules extend across the desktop application, native plugins, IPC, Python, and the web viewer. That gives plugins the foundation for longer workflows. A plugin can issue a command, receive its actual result, wait for any background work it starts, and decide what to do next. The new AI plugin puts that into practice: ask for a scene in ordinary language, let the agent operate Patinae, and have it inspect the rendered image before answering. Highlights A task has one lifecycle, wherever it starts Background work now receives a host-assigned task ID and stays under the shared task runner's control. Progress, diagnostics, final outcomes, and cancellation requests belong to that task. The desktop shows active tasks with progress and cancellation controls, and services background work independently of rendering. The distinction between accepting a command and finishing its work is explicit. An immediate command returns its result. A command that starts background work also returns task IDs, which clients can observe, wait for, or cancel. Success means the required scene changes have been applied; it does not promise that the GPU has already presented a frame. Scripts and plugin workflows can create child tasks. A parent stays active until its children finish, and cancellation propagates through the task tree. Cancelling stops further work cooperatively; changes already applied to the scene remain. A wait timeout ends the wait without cancelling the underlying task. Python command methods wait for background work by default, so a script can fetch a structure and then operate on it. Use wait=False to get task IDs immediately and manage them through tasks or a notebook viewer's view.tasks . Browser integrations receive command results and use viewer.tasks.get , list , wait , and cancel to follow the same lifecycle. Plugins can coordinate work and recover from errors Plugins now receive typed replies to the host commands they issue, correlated to the original request and delivered only to the requesting plugin. Replies include success or failure, output messages, and every accepted task ID. A command can fail after starting some work, so those IDs remain available for inspection. For plugin authors, the new contract separates responsibilities clearly: The host owns task identity and state. A plugin submits a task request and starts its worker after the host accepts it and delivers the assigned ID. Workers report progress, output, and completion. Scene mutations go through the host and must be acknowledged before the plugin reports success. Nested commands belong to the parent task. Their completion and cancellation participate in the same lifecycle. Recovery can be deliberate. Child failure fails the parent by default. An executor can opt into deciding the parent outcome after inspecting and handling a failed child. The original failure remains in task history. This matters for an agent that needs to correct a command, or a script that has a fallback when a download fails. The parent can handle the error and continue while preserving the record of what happened. Silent execution also follows the task tree. It suppresses REPL presentation while retaining results, diagnostics, and logs, so a plugin can handle intermediate failures without filling the output panel with messages it intends to recover from. Polling plugins additionally receive named selections and Recent Atoms path

summary: The research paper titled "The Ocean and Spatial Representation in Sangam Literature" by Dr. K. Periya Karuppan examines how the marine ecosystem of the Neithal landscape (ocean and coastal regions) is constructed as a literary and cultural space ( Idanaakkam ) in classical Tamil poetry. Drawing contextual evidence from texts such as Purananuru, Akananuru, Aingurunuru, Natrinai, Paripadal , and the epic Silappathikaram , the study explores the multifaceted thematic functions of the sea. It analyzes the ocean as a metaphorical space for the rising sun, symbolizing a king’s fierce wrath, and as a physical benchmark to measure the profound depth of the hero’s love. The author highlights the realistic environmental depictions of the coast, including the pervasive fishy odor ( Pulal Naatram ) of the waves and drying fish, contrasted with the fragrant Thazhai and Punnai blossoms. Furthermore, the paper looks into the stark demographic contrast between the small, humble coastal hamlets ( Sirugudi ) of the Parathavar community and the immense, vast ocean where their large ships ( Vangam/Thimil ) vanish into the horizon. Lastly, the study maps the sea as a locus for natural phenomenon, like the water cycle, and as a stage for mythological history, notably Murugan's triumph over Surapadman. The paper concludes that Sangam poets seamlessly blended geographic realities with human emotions to transform the physical ocean into a vital psychological space.
tags: Sangam Literature - Marine Ecosystem - Spatial Representation (Idanaakkam) - Neithal Landscape - Allegorical Space - Maritime Trade - Cultural Ecology.
title: The Sea and Maritime Spaces in Sangam Literature

summary: Dorieh is a data engineering platform for population and environmental health research. It turns heterogeneous raw sources, including Medicare and Medicaid claims in fixed-width ResDAC layouts and climate and air-quality data, into documented, queryable warehouses: schema-driven ingestion through a domain-specific language, CWL-orchestrated workflows, data validation and journaling, quality-control aggregates, and column-level provenance. The platform's methodology is described in the monograph "Research Data that Can be Trusted" (Springer, 2026, doi:10.1007/978-3-032-21032-6), which is the preferred citation for the methodology; cite this record for the software itself.

Includes all 40 archived experiment runs across 8 controller/data degree configurations. (2) model-II-three-branch/ — a three-branch clock-controlled generator over GF(3) combined through a quadratic nonlinear ternary function, together with period/design analysis, algebraic/spectral characterization of the combiner, an aggregate statistical pipeline, avalanche diffusion experiments, a matched attack suite, and an exact key-stream-reuse detector. A full SHA-256 manifest (MANIFEST_SHA256.tsv) and verification script (verify_checksums.py) are included to allow integrity checking of every file. See README.md for directory structure, provenance notes, a documented anonymity sanitization log, and instructions to reproduce all reported results. See CORRESPONDENCE.md for a mapping between source files and the tables/figures of the manuscript. Source code (*.py, *.bat) is released under the MIT License. Generated data, results, logs, CSV aggregates, and figures are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).

summary: This edition presents the current Split-Zero, theta-cohomology and arithmetic-kernel calculations in a research programme on the Riemann zeta function. It publishes the complete 216-page cumulative continuation, the updated 425-page broader research reader, and their proof sources and checks. The purpose is to make the actual calculations readable and reproducible: what was attempted, why that route was chosen, the maps and estimates obtained, and the precise points where the argument remains unfinished. Start with the cumulative calculation reader 14-splitzero-tau-kernel-continuation.pdf is the primary preview. Its 22 proof sections and nine complete source appendices carry the programme from Split-Zero coefficients through theta cohomology, interpolation kernels, chain retractions, homotopy control and the symmetric arithmetic frontier. Earlier source notes retain their own revisions and attribution; the cumulative continuation is not presented as though all its source results originated in one session. Split-Zero coefficients keep the original zero of a ring as a supported element and adjoin a different, external zero, tau. This records the difference between cancelling a coefficient and forgetting the fibre that carried it. Theta cohomology is a specified space of rapidly decreasing functions modulo the image of a specified theta-summation map. Under the stated Mellin transform, that map becomes multiplication by g(s) = 2 xi(s) , where xi is the completed Riemann zeta function. A finite spectral packet records spectral points with their multiplicities, using polynomial quotients and full derivative data rather than discarding repeated-root directions. The calculations construct minimum-norm representatives from the original arithmetic measure, derive full-jet kernel and Gram-inverse formulas, follow nested packets and tensor constructions, and compute the boundary control from the actual theta-derivative sequence. The cumulative reader also develops the relation-layer graph, derivative quotients, norm and Gram-volume identities, and conjugation/reflection-symmetric estimates. Spectral-sum constructions keep the relative variables through matrix weights and complete nilpotent fibres. The quantitative question is how the control form compares with the original arithmetic Gram matrix as the degree and tensor order grow; smallness of one matrix alone is not treated as the required relative estimate. The broader zeta programme 13-main-reader-425p.pdf supplies the surrounding literature reconstruction, CUE random-matrix calculations, arithmetic transforms and source-directed fluid calculations. It includes the all-axis Mellin calculation, complex axial branch points, moving analytic radius and endpoint-residue map for the stated source patch. Those results are described with their source assumptions and maps; they are not recast as a newly constructed zeta-zero witness or an independent proof of the imported fluid existence result. The motivation includes the use of weights in Deligne's Weil II . This programme works out its own analytic spaces, operators, metrics and comparison maps. The complete proofs retain their domains, signs, measures, scalar actions, local units and multiplicities. These are substantive calculations and research attempts, not a claim that an analogy by itself proves or disproves the Riemann hypothesis. Sources, verification and earlier editions 15-current-integrated-sources.zip records the integrated repository snapshot and the broader reader's authored proof dependencies. 16-tandem-continuation-sources.zip preserves the cumulative continuation's separately identified source tree, appendices, build instructions and checks. Their manifests pin the exact revisions and file identities. Written analytic arguments, exact finite checks, numerical enclosures and Lean declarations have distinct stated verification scopes; a check on one interface is not promoted into a certificate for the entire programme. By evaluating multi-dimensional wave propagation and self-trapped rotational flow profiles as real geometric deformations of a flexible spatial grid, we replace the abstract, complexified probability landscapes of standard non-linear optics with localized, causal mechanical actions. Modern fluid dynamics and wave mechanics treat the spontaneous reconstruction of broken wave profiles and azimuthal modulation cycles as a consequence of unphysical point-continuum space-time frameworks, necessitating manual phase adjustments and artificial energy subtractions. This investigation provides a non-parametric refinement of these macroscopic structures by showing that long-lived breathers and near-periodic structural revivals are natural hallmarks of a real-valued coordinate network. summary: Resumo O Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) constitui uma das principais conquistas institucionais do Brasil, ao estabelecer a saúde como direito universal em um país continental e profundamente desigual. Quase quatro décadas após sua criação, o desafio central não é reconstruí-lo, mas transformar sua ampla estrutura em um sistema efetivamente integrado, resolutivo, sustentável e preparado para as mudanças demográficas, epidemiológicas e tecnológicas do século XXI. Essa transformação exige ampliar e qualificar o financiamento público. Em 2024, o gasto governamental em saúde correspondeu a 5,03% do PIB. Entretanto, em 2019, o setor público respondeu por apenas cerca de 40% do gasto total em saúde, enquanto aproximadamente 60% foram financiados por fontes privadas, proporção inversa à observada na maioria dos sistemas universais e muito inferior à média pública de aproximadamente 72% nos países da OCDE. O subfinanciamento transfere custos às famílias, especialmente por meio da compra de medicamentos, mas aumentar recursos sem melhorar a organização não será suficiente. O artigo propõe avançar da descentralização para uma regionalização efetiva, com listas de espera transparentes, compras em escala e integração entre atenção primária, especialistas, hospitais e cuidados domiciliares. A extensa rede territorial do SUS deve assumir maior responsabilidade pela saúde de populações definidas, com capacidade diagnóstica, acompanhamento longitudinal e atuação preventiva. Dados interoperáveis devem ser tratados como infraestrutura pública estratégica. Inteligência artificial, genômica, telessaúde, monitoramento remoto e medicina de precisão somente produzirão valor se forem validados na população brasileira, incorporados a fluxos assistenciais funcionais e avaliados quanto a benefício clínico, custo-efetividade, segurança e equidade. Diante do envelhecimento populacional, o SUS precisa evoluir para um sistema de saúde que aprende continuamente, antecipa riscos, mede resultados, amplia o que funciona e abandona intervenções de baixo valor.   Summary The Brazilian Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde, SUS) is one of Brazil’s most important institutional achievements, establishing health as a universal right in a continental and deeply unequal country. Nearly four decades after its creation, the central challenge is not to rebuild the SUS, but to transform its extensive infrastructure into a genuinely integrated, effective, sustainable system prepared for the demographic, epidemiological, and technological changes of the twenty-first century. This transformation requires both increasing and improving public financing. In 2024, government health expenditure corresponded to 5.03% of GDP. However, in 2019, the public sector accounted for only approximately 40% of total health spending, while around 60% came from private sources—the reverse of the pattern observed in most universal health systems and well below the OECD average public share of approximately 72%. Underfunding shifts healthcare costs to households, particularly through medicine purchases, but increasing resources without improving organization will not be sufficient. The article proposes moving from decentralization toward effective regionalization, supported by transparent waiting lists, procurement at scale, and integration among primary care, specialists, hospitals, and home care. summary: We propose the Encephlian Standard Format (ESF), a 19-channel international 10–20 montage at 250 Hz, average re-referenced, microvolt-calibrated, and channel-wise robust z-scored, as a deterministic canonical representation for deploying pretrained EEG classifiers on heterogeneous acquisition hardware, paired with a recoverability framework that predicts which signal-level shifts ESF can and cannot recover. On the Temple University Abnormal EEG Corpus (TUAB, n = 276 patient-stratified, 253 unique patients), a frozen EEGPT linear probe attains clean AUROC 0.908. We sweep five acquisition-shift axes (native sampling rate, per-channel gain, 50 Hz line noise, electrode montage, and broadband signal-to-noise) and show that left-invertible and bandwidth-preserving operators are (f,0)-recoverable while sub-Nyquist sampling and broadband Gaussian noise are not (Propositions 1, 2). A Pinsker-based AUROC–total-variation bound holds on 18/18 measured axis-arms (median implied constant 0.10). Clustering every recording by its joint behaviour across the sweep yields seven failure categories: 100% of baseline-correct normals flip on at least one shifted cell, 95.3% flip with confidence ≥ 0.80 into the abnormal class, while 87.4% of baseline-correct abnormals are robust-correct. Shift preferentially converts clean normals into confident abnormal reports, the worst direction for screening. Code, perturbation operators, the ESF reference implementation, and per-recording predictions are released. Preprint of the manuscript submitted to the IEEE Signal Processing in Medicine and Biology Symposium (SPMB) 2026 on 30 June 2026, currently under review. Code, perturbation operators, and per-recording predictions are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22727770 and maintained at https://github.com/h5371h/esf-recoverability. The supplementary material is included as a second file.
title: ESF: A Canonical Representation and Recoverability Framework for Deploying Pretrained EEG Classifiers in Heterogeneous Clinics

summary: QN-AEI is a curated, simulation-based benchmark for studying quantum noise effects in amplitude-encoded grayscale images. Two hundred images from the BSDS500 training subset were converted to grayscale, resized to 64 x 64 pixels, and encoded as 4096-dimensional normalized amplitude vectors, each corresponding to a 12-qubit quantum state. Every image was then evolved under three completely positive trace-preserving noise channels — amplitude damping, Pauli-Z dephasing, and depolarizing noise — at four channel-parameter values, eta = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, with 200 repeated stochastic realizations per image-channel-noise configuration. The release therefore contains 2,400 image-channel-noise conditions, 480,000 noisy amplitude-encoded realizations, and 1,966,080,000 normalized perturbation samples. Each image-level record stores the preprocessed clean image, the clean amplitude vector, the noisy statevector matrices, raw and pooled perturbation arrays, normalized bounded-domain perturbation values, and structured condition-level metadata including a deterministic per-condition random seed. The release also includes a dataset manifest, source-image provenance linking every record to its BSDS500 original, an automated validation report covering all 200 records, aggregated and condition-level perturbation statistics, and the MATLAB script used to generate and validate the dataset. The original BSDS500 image files are not redistributed. Users should obtain them from the Berkeley Computer Vision Group and comply with the BSDS500 usage terms. The dataset supports reproducible benchmarking of quantum-noise modeling, bounded-domain perturbation modeling, denoising and error-mitigation methods, and uncertainty and reliability analysis using the repeated realizations. Due to the size of the release (12.6 GB) and Zenodo's current infrastructure load, QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip is distributed as 26 sequential parts (QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part001 through QN-AEI-BSD200_v1.0.zip.part026) rather than a single file. Download all 26 parts into the same folder, then reassemble the original archive before extracting. summary: We present a synthesis of the Karimov–Alekberli (KA) Framework into a unified theory of Constitutional Intelligence: the capacity of an adaptive system to make consequential decisions that are simultaneously governed, explainable, accountable, reconstructable, verifiable, and capable of learning without retroactive falsification of the historical record. We formulate six formal results — one per required property — organized into three proof tiers: Tier A (two unconditional geometric results), Tier B (three conditional results valid under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), Tier C (one KA extension under a physical implementation assumption). Results draw on viability theory,information geometry, and thermodynamics. The theorems are organized in three tiers reflecting their current proof status: Tier A (fully proved geometric results), Tier B (conditional theorems under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), and Tier C (KA extensions requiring additional physical or topological conditions). A unifying condition, the Constitutional Integrity Criterion (CIC), is formulated as a representation theorem characterizing systems that satisfy all six properties simultaneously. We derive, under the CIC, that the governance loop Govern → Reason → Act → Remember → Learn → Govern defines a well-defined autonomous map on the constitutional moduli space that preserves the admissible region; fixed-point existence follows as a corollary under compactness. We position the framework within the existing literature on viability theory, formal verification, safe reinforcement learning, AI governance, and constitutional economics. We propose Constitutional Intelligence Science as the emerging discipline that unifies these results.
title: Constitutional Intelligence as Formal Science The Karimov–Alekberli Framework as Mathematical Foundation for Governed Institutional Cognition

summary: Adaptability release: the analysis pipeline no longer assumes an NV-scale emitter or a negligible instrument response, and measured data enter through a documented file contract. This release also upgrades the fit physics itself -- two changes that came out of adversarial re-examination rather than feature work. Bring your own emitter and instrument load_hbt_csv / save_hbt_csv : a documented two-column contract ( delay_ns,counts ) with an exact round trip and refusals for wrong headers, field counts, negative counts and non-increasing delay axes. Configurable lifetime windows : t1_bounds / t2_bounds (ns) on analyze_histogram , fit_g2_histogram and profile_likelihood_ci -- validated on entry. The defaults are the NV-scale window used since v0.1. The test suite runs a tau1 = 0.15 ns, tau2 = 5 ns emitter and shows BOTH halves: the default window fails visibly (error > 0.2), the emitter's own window recovers g2(0) to better than 0.05. register_platform (existing) plus a test that a user-defined platform runs the whole pipeline; load_fisequr now takes the dataset directory explicitly instead of defaulting to one machine's path. The fit physics, corrected Physical parameterization. The LM fit and the profile likelihood now fit the dip depth rho^2 multiplying BOTH exponentials (g2(0) = 1 - rho^2), the form g2_measured itself uses. The previous 1 - d e1 + a e2 form capped d at 1 -- which biased g2(0) upward for any emitter with a strong bunching shoulder -- and hid a genuine (d, a) ridge behind that cap. The instrument response is in the model. Both fitters now use the closed-form Gaussian-convolved exponentials at cfg.sigma_irf , so the estimand is the IRF-free g2(0), not the softened dip the raw histogram shows; a test constructs a case where the two differ by more than 0.02 and checks the right one is recovered. An honest interval, and the knob that tightens it. With the normalization free, a slow bunching shoulder trades almost exactly against the flat level -- a real near-degeneracy of the histogram alone (probed directly during development: the exact-Poisson likelihood is flat to Delta NLL ~ 1 from g2 = 0.10 to 0.30 in the demonstration case). The profile interval now says so by being wide. Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated) CSV contract: exact round trip; four distinct malformed-file refusals. Fast-emitter recovery only with its own window, and visible failure without it. IRF-aware estimand: the profile CI covers the IRF-free g2(0) where the IRF-softened value is more than 0.02 higher. Profile CI with the singles-rate prior: covers the truth at 10 s and 60 s, width shrinks by more than 2x; with the normalization free it stays covering but wider -- the degeneracy is reported, not hidden. summary: Extraction code, full concordance, both coders' independent judgements and the adjudication record for the article "In Our Lands": Region, Language, and Community in Ibn Sīnā's First Person. Every first-person plural in nineteen works of Ibn Sīnā (2,070,759 words) was extracted and classified, together with three control authors — al-Bīrūnī, Abū Bakr al-Rāzī and al-Fārābī — for a total of fifty-nine works and 410 instances. Source texts are from the OpenITI corpus, version 2025.1.9 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17767721); the texts themselves are not redistributed here. See README.md in the archive for a file-by-file description, the coding scheme, headline figures and reproduction instructions. The second coding pass was carried out independently, and blind to the hypothesis, by a colleague who has asked not to be named; their codes are included in full as data/codes_reader_B.csv, and the adjudication record in data/uzlastirilmis.csv shows where their reading was preferred.

summary: Whether a neural language model can report facts about its own computation is difficult to evaluate because an accurate report may be generated either from the realized runtime state or from a static simulation of the computation conditioned on the input and fixed parameters. We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768). In ESW-1A, a planted directional watermark becomes increasingly decodable as training examples grow relative to representation dimension, reaching 88.4% held-out accuracy at N/d=6.51 (cos θ = 0.9236), while a one-dimensional control reaches 100.0%. In an exploratory Oracle Ladder diagnostic, differential signals peak at Layer 8 before downstream attenuation. In the subsequent multi-seed paired-counterfactual benchmark (ESW-2B), an external nonlinear probe of intermediate runtime differences reaches approximately 0.62–0.63 AUROC, while the tested unperturbed-state baseline remains close to chance (0.507 AUROC) and a sample-label decoupled control remains at 0.546 AUROC. The paired bootstrap difference between the joint and runtime-only models includes zero (ΔAUROC = +0.012, 95% CI [-0.023, +0.047]), demonstrating that adding baseline activations provides no statistically detectable advantage over the runtime perturbation alone.  We interpret the experiments as empirical evidence for runtime-state-dependent decodability under the ESW intervention, not as evidence that GPT-2 possesses autonomous introspection, privileged self-report, consciousness, or subjective self-knowledge.
title: Runtime-State Watermarking in Transformers: A Controlled Protocol for Distinguishing Static Self-Simulation from Runtime-State Decodability

summary: Experimental-adaptability release: the three inputs a laboratory actually has -- a measured dispersion table, a fixed set of deposited materials, and a reflectance specification -- now enter the yield-aware design loop directly. Added TabulatedMaterial : bring your measured dispersion. An n(lam) table from ellipsometry, a vendor datasheet or a refractiveindex.info tabulation is used directly -- no Sellmeier fit required. Shape-preserving PCHIP interpolation, refusal outside the tabulated range (the same rule as the cited Sellmeier built-ins), and a mandatory reference naming where the table comes from. An optional extinction column serves the absorbing forward solver through .nk() ; .n() refuses an absorbing table rather than silently dropping k, because the design path is lossless. .n(lam) is the same interface as SellmeierMaterial.n , so a tabulated material drops into dispersion_shape , layer_index and everything built on them. Per-layer and frozen design boxes. Every DesignBox bound now accepts a scalar or an (N,) array, and a bound pair with lo == hi freezes that parameter -- so a real multi-material stack, whose indices are deposited materials rather than design variables, runs through the identical engine. DesignBox.thickness_only(N, t_lo, t_hi, n_fixed) builds the common case. A fully frozen box (nothing left to design) is refused. weights_from_reflectance : mirror and high-reflector merits. A reflectance-based linear merit converts to transmittance weights by the exact lossless identity R = 1 - T, so reflectance specifications run through the same hand adjoint, design engine and CVaR robustifier unchanged. The thickness-only metrology path , documented and anchored: a tool that logs thickness but not per-run index sets n_fab = n_recipe in the trace contract; the fitted twin then invents no index errors, and robustification on a frozen-index box uses exactly the information the lab has. Changed FabTwinConfig validates its bounds (strictly increasing scalars): the learned twin's recipe conditioner normalizes by hi - lo, so frozen or per-layer bounds -- a design-space feature of DesignBox -- are refused there with an explanation instead of producing a division by zero. Anchors (asserted in tests/test_experimental_adapt.py , not stated) A table sampled from the cited Malitson Sellmeier is exact at its nodes and agrees with the independent closed form between them; the whole design path (shape, solver, hand adjoint vs central finite differences) runs on a tabulated material end to end. The design engine and the CVaR robustifier return a frozen index profile EXACTLY ( np.array_equal ); per-layer sampling and clipping respect each layer's window. The reflectance-weight identity holds at machine precision on a lossless stack through the solver's exact R + T = 1; on an absorbing stack it fails by exactly w_R . A (asserted as an exact relation), and the quarter-wave (HL)^3 mirror scores its closed-form admittance reflectance through this path. A thickness-only twin's sampled index errors stay below 1e-3 while its thickness errors are preserved, and CVaR ascent on the frozen-index box does not degrade the objective it ascends. Full test suite: 63 passed (Python 3.10-3.13, JAX extra active in CI). See CHANGELOG.md for details.
title: fabtwin: learned generative process twins for yield-aware inverse design of multilayer optics

summary: Adaptability release: sqzcomb now speaks laboratory units and fits measured data, so the normalized-units engine underneath is usable directly from an experiment. Added sqzcomb.physical : the exact dictionary between laboratory ring parameters and the package's normalized LLE frame. RingSpec (loaded linewidth in Hz, escape efficiency, single-photon Kerr shift, pump wavelength -- with a mandatory reference naming where the numbers come from) plus normalized_pump , threshold_power , normalized_detuning , normalized_dispersion , normalized_frequency / physical_frequency , and intracavity_photons . Conventions are checked by identities rather than trusted: every conversion round-trips exactly, F scales as sqrt(P), and threshold_power is cross-validated through the package's own flat-state cubic -- at the returned power, homogeneous_steady_states contains the rho = 1 root to machine precision. Physical constants come from scipy.constants ; no constant is typed by hand. sqzcomb.fitnoise : extraction of (mu, eta, kappa) from measured homodyne noise spectra in dB relative to shot noise -- the standard characterization of a below-threshold squeezer. fit_noise_spectra fits the package's own input-output model (the same code path as sqzcomb.spectra , cross-checked in the tests against the independent closed form) to the squeezed/antisqueezed trace pair, with an optional white dark-noise floor and per-point measurement sigmas enabling a chi-square consistency check. Identifiability is enforced, not hoped for: one quadrature alone is a single Lorentzian with two shape numbers for three unknowns, so the single-trace fit is refused unless an independently measured kappa_hz is supplied; an antisqueezed trace systematically below shot noise is refused as unphysical. Changed scipy is now a declared dependency (the new modules use scipy.constants and scipy.optimize.least_squares ). Anchors (asserted in tests/test_adapt.py , not stated) Conversion round trips exact to 1e-15; F(4P) = 2F(P); at fixed eta_esc, doubling kappa halves F. threshold_power hits the rho = 1 root of the package's own cubic for alpha in {0.7, 1.0, 1.8}. Noise-free synthetic spectra return the generating (mu, eta, kappa) to better than 1e-6; the fitted model equals the closed form S = 0.5[1 -/+ 4 eta mu / ((1 +/- mu)^2 + Omega^2)] at every frequency to 1e-10. Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted parameters matches the reported one-sigma uncertainties; a dark floor deliberately omitted from the model biases eta, and fitting it recovers the truth. The under-determined single-trace case and the impossible below-shot-noise antisqueezed trace are refused with explanatory errors. Full test suite: 80 passed. See CHANGELOG.md for details.
title: sqzcomb: Lugiato-Lefever steady states and detected squeezing spectra for Kerr microcombs

First, what is BRICS?  B for Brazil, R for Russia, I for India, C for China, S for South Africa, at the time of writing.  While wandering through the streets of Madrid, I talked to caballeros from the street who said those people are heroes. That was a discourse we were not used to in our homeland. We had not the same sources of disseminated information.  Which are usually secondary sources of information, privately owned. And we are not talking about this as a potential conflict of interest, in the benefit-of-the-doubt sense, on those privately owned secondary sources of information for us.  So that was an opening. You see... what is fantastic in sublimation is that an a priori violation of our fundamental rights that would leave from the autumn to so much brightness and summer light in our life, hopefully. In the previous chapter, we started by stressing this mean-means fallacy, that is to say, a bad loop for a five-year-old child.  And the potential conflict of interest of private editors who are, well, editing hard or soft information and communication techniques, and sometimes undermining our mindfulness.  That is to say, less than 20 percent of our potential.  An interrogation:  Would it make sense to use emotion and motion, dance, visual arts, visual recensions, music to acquire as well as express, whether or not that makes sense in the legal, technical, informational, or court space?  So, being able to get out of the box using back-and-forth lateral thinking, thanks to symbolic thinking, using Trinity lecturing in a dis|mis main case, helped us find ways of expression and reconciliation, and opened a highway of recensions, openings such as DDEF, DEFI, like finance, for instance, up to the personal level, oration and recension, using accessible means within this mean-means fallacy. We would now like to extend this to trade and use this BRICS frame, observing our dissonances intrinsically, and revealing and un-revealing fallacies as well in the terms defined by Timothy Kenny's cognitive biases lectures.  --- Why use the BRICS frame? --- One of the main fallacies traced in the previous chapter was, as we mentioned many times, the mean-means fallacy: the widespread use of digital means of expression, as cited by Francisco Villar from the University of Barcelona, where working on ADHD in children, and attention is all we need at the moment.  So we are underusing our mindfulness.  But not only that: there is also a potential risk of conflict of interest from privately owned firms that are editing, whether hard or soft, these information techniques, these texts, especially for the public sector. For us, this is not impartial.  On top of that, the BRICS frame proposes decentralized, complementary approaches. It is a whole philosophy of multipolarising the world, you see.  And we believe that because we are seeking to raise awareness on inner peace, it is complementary to the centralized, usual way of doing things, whether in finance, education, or data governance.  A typical example in data and metadata governance at the UN level is centralization. It is centralized even in the way it is managed, using SQL, NoSQL, sometimes GraphQL but still the database is centralized. This introduces potential lawful and/or unlawful exploits, though not only that;  A typical mis|exploit is trolling, whether hard or soft. History testifies that a privately owned firm might deliberately leave a mis|exploit as a trolling horse so that if there is a problem, they can interfere for good or bad, but that is outside the client’s scope.  Therefore, the theoretical BRICS non-proprietary model would eliminated any sense of violation for us, at least in this Diegetic Wonderland. summary: The UCT Flourish 2027 Co-Curriculum represents the second full annual cycle of an established student-facing programme developed through the Centre for Wellbeing and Flourishing at the University of Cape Town. Building directly on the 2026 cycle, the 2027 programme emphasises continuation, replication, refinement and cumulative learning rather than first-stage piloting. It is organised across five connected domains: Journey, Community, Amplify, Knowledge and Wisdom, spanning intrapsychic, interpersonal, infrastructural, interdependent and intergenerational dimensions of flourishing. The annual architecture combines a weekly VIA Character Strengths and Flourishing Seminar Series, a recurring Monthly Masterclass, two sustained 30 Days of TURN interventions, and a set of signature programmes including UCT Flourish Verse, the UCT Flourish Lab, the Student Summit and the Annual Wellbeing and Flourishing Conference. Programming is aligned with the academic calendar, public holidays, vacation periods and assessment demands, with deliberate pauses for consolidation, evaluation and research. At its centre is the question: What makes human flourishing possible? The co-curriculum creates recurring opportunities for students to develop psychological capacities, strengthen relationships, participate in university life, engage with evidence and scholarship, and contribute their own experiences and perspectives to a developing institutional conversation about flourishing. The 2027 programme remains provisional and non-exhaustive, allowing additional initiatives, partnerships and funded opportunities to be incorporated as they emerge.
title: UCT Flourish 2027: Proposed Provisional Annual Co-Curriculum

summary: Dataset Overview & Methodology This repository provides an experimentally enriched network traffic dataset designed to overcome severe class imbalance in Web attack detection . Focusing on the CICIDS2017 benchmark, which natively contains critically scarce instances for minority Web threats (such as only 21 SQL Injection flows), this dataset incorporates 32,670 authentic attack flows captured in a controlled experimental testbed . Key Characteristics Authentic Capture Environment: Unlike synthetic interpolation methods (e.g., SMOTE) that generate artificial data points within existing boundaries, this dataset captures real network traffic using an Apache XAMPP server and Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) . It features both automated scripts ( sqlmap , Hydra , Wfuzz ) and manual obfuscation vectors combined with normal background traffic . Feature-Space Consistency: Processed directly via CICFlowMeter to extract the exact 78 statistical flow features required to maintain complete compatibility with the original CICIDS2017 feature space . Rigorously Evaluated Classes: Web SQL Injection (significantly boosted to ensure robust pattern learning) . Web Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (including reflected and stored variants with filter-evasion techniques) . Web Brute Force (WBF) (generated through multi-day credential-guessing sessions) .
tags: Intrusion detection; CICIDS2017; Web attacks; Class imbalance; Traffic augmentation; LightGBM; CICFlowMeter; Multiclass classification
title: Enriched CICIDS2017 Web Attacks Dataset for Network Intrusion Detection

summary: This project investigates early training dynamics in robotic manipulation by comparing Truncated Quantile Critics (TQC), TQC with Hindsight Experience Replay (HER), and a reward-shaped TQC+HER variant in the sparse-reward FetchPickAndPlace-v4 environment. The proposed reward shaping provides intermediate signals for object contact, grasping, lifting, and moving toward the target, with all variants evaluated under matched training conditions using success rate, episode return, AUC, seed variance, and non-parametric significance testing. Results showed that baseline TQC and TQC+HER exhibited very limited early learning, while the reward-shaped variant achieved the best final performance but no statistically significant improvement, suggesting that simple hand-crafted reward shaping alone is insufficient to reliably improve early-stage learning in sparse robotic manipulation tasks.
title: Effects of Enhancing TQC with Reward Shaping on Early Training Dynamics in FetchPickAndPlace-v4

summary: Frequency-shift corrections are applied in deep-space navigation as a catalogue of formulas: common offsets, detector-end $O(c^{-3})$ cross terms and the nonlinear Doppler bias are re-derived for every mission and every data type. This paper derives the structure itself, from a single transitivity axiom. Under that axiom the endpoint factor of any light-path observable is a ratio of generators --- the \textbf{Fuxi value} $\FX_{A\|B}=\alpha_A/\alpha_B$ --- multiplied by a path factor; the generator is identified with the rate of proper-time flow, $\alpha_X=\mathrm d\tau_X/\mathrm dt_{\rm GalST}$. The resulting framework (Fuxi-ratio Mapping Theory, hereafter FMT) leaves the path-dependent transfer factor $\Pi_{\rm TTF}$ with the full complexity of the null-geodesic boundary-value problem, while its $1$PN expansion reproduces the standard frequency-shift formulas term by term at $O(c^{-2})$ and endows the IAU conversion constants $L_C,L_G,L_B$ with a direct generator interpretation. Three consequences are closed-form. \textbf{(i)} The projected pulsar-Doppler residual is \emph{exactly} linear in the relativistic velocity $\mathbf u\equiv\gamma\mathbf v$: the $O(c^{-3})$ kinematic term of the coordinate-velocity parameterization is a parameterization effect with the exact closed form $v_D^3/(2c^2)\,\hat{\mathbf v}_D$, removable in one analytic step, and \emph{identically absent} under $\mathbf u$. \textbf{(ii)} Isotropic and dipolar residual components are absorbed exactly --- the latter as a velocity error independent of the pulsar number and of the network geometry. \textbf{(iii)} Residuals of angular order $\ell\ge2$ are \emph{not} absorbed; their leakage is fixed by the higher moments of the pulsar directions, so precision and bias immunity are governed by different moments of the same network. Velocity identifiability is necessary and sufficient: the pulsar directions must not be cocircular. Model-internal consistency tests with a realistic 16-pulsar IPTA geometry reach $16.1\ \mu$m/s (three-axis RMS) at ideal timing precision $\sigma_\delta=10^{-13}$, and a full Earth-departure-to-Mars-surface arc is closed by the same expression with only its inputs changed. Both statements are model-internal limits: the term-by-term agreement with the standard formulas is limited to $O(c^{-2})$, the velocity figures presuppose an ephemeris residual $\delta C_P\lesssim3\times10^{-14}$, and practical accuracy is bounded by clock, ephemeris and direction knowledge. FMT modifies neither general relativity nor observational hardware: it is an algebraic interface callable on existing ephemerides and timing data.
title: Relativistic Doppler Velocimetry from One Transitivity Axiom: Exact Bias and Identifiability

summary: Conventional capillary heat pipes route vapor and returning condensate through the same envelope, so the two streams interact along the entire transport length. This work reports a D-shaped two-phase loop that separates the two paths geometrically: a wicked vertical leg carries evaporation and vapor transport, and a curved copper return leg carries condensate back to a submerged reservoir at the base of the vertical leg, which acts as a hydrostatic trap that excludes vapor from the return path. Three additively manufactured triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) wicks of a common fill-ratio class and unit-cell size were tested in this envelope, gyroid, Schwarz Diamond, and Schwarz Primitive, together with a conventional copper-mesh heat pipe as benchmark. Devices were operated vertically at measured heater powers of 30.3, 40.5, and 50.8 W. Schwarz Diamond and gyroid gave the lowest power-averaged thermal resistance of the four configurations, reaching 1.70 and 1.69 ÅãC/W at 50.8W and holding the evaporator 23.7 and 20.1 ÅãC cooler than the benchmark at that power. Extrapolating the measured resistance to a length-scaled maximum heat-transport capability, Schwarz Diamond and gyroid exceed the copper-mesh benchmark by approximately 9% and 6% at the tested 0.30m length; these are single-run, architecture-level comparisons and are not repeated-trial estimates. Within this matched-class triplet, porosity identifies which structures form the leading pair while simulated single-phase permeability predicts the reverse ordering. Porosity is therefore the more reliable near-term predictor of thermal performance among architected lattices tested at a fixed fill-ratio class, though the device comparisons were not repeated and porosity remains one of several confounded structural parameters.
title: Porosity versus Permeability as Predictors of Thermal Performance in Architected TPMS Wicks for a D-Shaped Separated-Flow Heat Pipe

summary: This record contains the first three Lean-verified certificate packages in the Chronos Gravity G1 working formal verification series.   The work formally connects a defined radial time-field model to standard Newtonian gravity and progressively verifies the structure of that connection in Lean. Across versions v0.1 through v0.3, the certificates establish the time-field gradient, its exact correspondence with Newtonian point-mass gravitational acceleration under the stated calibration, shared real-time motion and accumulated velocity change, the vacuum radial field equation, spherical flux, source calibration, and the full three-dimensional vacuum Laplacian away from the source.   The latest certificate extends the result from a radial calculation to the full three-dimensional field, showing that the same time-field construction satisfies the standard vacuum harmonic structure while reproducing the Newtonian gravitational field.   This deposit is part of an ongoing formal validation program. Future work will continue toward the point-source Poisson identity, extended source distributions, and broader gravitational structure.   Each ZIP contains the Lean source, reproducibility instructions, build information, axiom audits, checksums, and detailed mathematical documentation. The formal builds pass without "sorry", "admit", or "sorryAx" placeholders.
title: Lean-Verified Chronos Gravity: Radial Time-Field to Newtonian Gravity, Vacuum Flux, and Full 3D Laplacian — Working Formal Verification Series G1 (v0.1–v0.3)

summary: This research edition studies a concrete finite part of the Riemann zeta function's spectral data. A packet is a chosen finite collection of its zeros, with every selected multiplicity retained. Its polynomial h divides the completed function g=2xi. The original theta-function source has Mellin transform g/h. Tensor products of this source represent sums of the selected zero jets, including their full repeated-root structure. The purpose is to calculate the cost of those spectral configurations in the original arithmetic source norm. It is not to choose a favorable new metric or to assert that an off-critical-line zero exists. What to read Main research reader, 482 pages. The complete literature-and-proof synthesis now includes Section 41 on arithmetic source/relation volumes and Section 42 on gamma convolution descent. The end of Section 42 proves the direct analytic generating-function map into the same Toda input. Split-Zero/Toda companion, 424 pages. A cumulative, more focused account of the source, its cohomological quotient and finite spectral controls, with 38 proof chapters and 18 complete source appendices. The new chapters calculate the separate source and relation curvature terms, certified theta-seed inputs, and an exact Gaussian calibration. Separate full source ZIPs. These retain the mathematical texts, formalization sources and scoped checking records for each reader. Earlier published PDFs and archives remain separate downloads. Gamma and endpoint workbenches. The delivered HTML/Markdown/LaTeX argument and its finite checker remain readable separately. The endpoint criterion and its gamma-coordinate substitution explain a finite-window way to choose one of the existing canonical representatives. The attempts, their motivation and their results Exterior trace control. Why it was tried: A single-vector bound can miss the combined displacement of many spectral directions. What it establishes: The finite exterior calculation bounds their aggregate positive trace defect using the same rank-two allowance, with multiplicities and source factors retained. Source and relation volumes. Why it was tried: Relations vanish in the quotient, but their source norms still affect the least-norm representatives. What it establishes: The determinant of the canonical quotient metric is exactly a source Hankel determinant divided by a relation Hankel determinant. Two Toda flows. Why it was tried: Both determinant sequences come from exponential deformation of the original arithmetic measure. What it establishes: Their derivative formulas calculate the source/relation curvature and the original complex cross term. The finite upper estimate retains explicit nonnegative losses. Gamma convolution descent. Why it was tried: Computing a new high-dimensional convolution integral for each tensor degree is expensive. What it establishes: A classical gamma reference, multiplied by the actual arithmetic amplitude, gives an exact all-tensor coefficient formula and an explicit tail majorant. Its relative-fibre component is retained. Analytic generating-function map. Why it was tried: The coefficient expansion and the Toda moment function appeared as separate descriptions of the same source. What it establishes: They are linked by an explicit analytic map and inverse. A degree-N Gram matrix differentiated j times uses only the one-factor coefficients through degree 2N+j. Endpoint degree selection. Why it was tried: Bounding every recurrence coefficient in a whole degree window is stronger than selecting one useful canonical degree. What it establishes: The written finite Jensen argument uses four endpoint quotient volumes and two endpoint polynomial norms. The gamma-coordinate version retains the exact reference and arithmetic correction factors. The quantities are attached to explicit maps At degree N the source is the original polynomial space, mapped to the cyclic algebra C[S]/(chi). The relation columns are multiplication by the original
title: Arithmetic zeta packets: quotient volumes, Toda control and gamma convolution

summary: Experimental-workflow release: the two loose ends of the measured-data path are closed, so a squeezing estimate needs no hand-entered inputs beyond the atom number. Added estimate_contrast / ContrastEstimate : the Ramsey fringe contrast fitted from a phase-scan shot record -- the number estimate_squeezing previously asked the user to bring from their own fringe fit. The mean fringe obeys A cos phi + B sin phi + d exactly (the rotation law of the mean spin, no lineshape assumption), so the fit is closed-form weighted linear least squares with per-phase standard errors, and the contrast uncertainty follows by the delta method through the exact WLS covariance -- the same structure and honesty as variance_tomography . Refusals: fewer than 3 distinct phases modulo 2 pi, and a fitted contrast above 1 beyond its uncertainty (reported as a probable N or J_z-calibration problem; a small statistical overshoot is returned as data, with the deliberate rounding left to the user, never clipped silently). save_shots_csv / load_shots_csv : a documented plain-text contract ( angle_rad,jz , one row per shot; ragged per-angle shot counts allowed) serving both tomography and fringe records -- the same data shape -- with exact round trips and refusals for malformed files and single-shot angles. Anchors (asserted in tests/test_fringe.py , not stated) Clean-record fringe recovery: contrast, phase and offset to 1e-7. Monte-Carlo scatter of the contrast estimate matches its reported sigma (ratio within [0.5, 2]), and the truth lies within the ensemble error. Degenerate phases (0, 2 pi, 4 pi) refused; an N four times too small triggers the exceeds-1 refusal. Exact file round trip with ragged shot counts; wrong header, single-shot angles and duplicate angles refused. The complete file-to-estimate pipeline -- fringe record -> estimate_contrast, tomography record -> estimate_squeezing, both through the contract -- recovers the standard quantum limit xi2_R = 1 on a coherent-spin-state record with no hand-entered contrast. Full test suite: 52 passed + 3 QuTiP-extra skips locally; all pass in CI with the extra installed (Python 3.9-3.13). Note: the two intermediate CI runs of this release failed only the version-metadata consistency test (the CITATION.cff bump landed in the following commit); the release head is green. See CHANGELOG.md for details.
