summary: This record contains the frozen computational data and source code supporting the study “Production Capacity Is Not Growth Coupling: Exhaustive Analysis of PHB Strain Designs.” The archive includes the curated iJA1121 M1 model of Priestia megaterium DSM319; complete growth-optimal classifications for the defined 59-reaction, one- to four-knockout space across four aerobic carbon conditions; zero-product certificates; the C1 same-vector epsilon-capacity oracle and Pareto products; the seed-10–29 active-learning replication; the 280,000-record capacity-surrogate and target-specific SHAP re-execution; bounded genome-scale constrained-minimal-cut-set results; configuration files; registration and amendment documents; solver audits; software environments; and SHA-256 manifests. All reported outcomes are in silico properties of the frozen model, bounds, intervention universe, and numerical tolerances.
title: PHB Growth-Coupling Classification and Capacity-Oracle Benchmark for the Curated iJA1121 M1 Model of Priestia megaterium DSM319

summary: The zip file in this record contains code and data to create the figures and tables and to replicate the underlying analysis in the following publication: Waidelich et al. (2026). The impact of financing cost differences on global energy and industry decarbonization. Nature Climate Change (forthcoming), DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-026-02756-0 For more information on the repository's content and how to replicate the paper content, see the README document included in the replication package. Source Data for the main figures in the paper are provided with the publication itself. For more details on how to access the third-party input data used here, see the Data and Code Availability Statements in the publication itself and the README document in this repository. For questions, please contact the corresponding author as indicated in the underlying publication.  Data files for the CoC estimates: If you want to use the cost of capital estimates, country-level and IMAGE region-level files are included in the zip file as  WaidelichEtAl2026_CostOfCapital_ByCountry.csv  and  WaidelichEtAl2026_CostOfCapital_ByIMAGERegion.csv.  Variables included in these files: - country, region and sector identifiers (names and, for countries, ISO codes) -  wacc_aftertax_nominal : our main WACC estimates - wacc_aftertax_nominal_aaa : our main estimates but setting the country risk premium to zero (i.e., assuming that the country is AAA-rated) - wacc_derivative_... : partial derivatives of our main estimates with respect to different input parameters (country risk premium, equity risk premium, beta, debt spread and risk-free rate). These allow users to modify our estimates ceteris paribus (e.g., by changing the risk-free rate assumption) without having to rerun the entire replication package - flag_imputation_corporatetax : indicates countries for which the corporate tax rate is imputed (see Methods and SI of the underlying publication) - gdp_ppp_real_bn and year_of_gdp_value : GDP data that can be used to aggregate country-level estimates to regions - key input variables that vary by country or sector ( crp_debt_defaultspread_average_20162025 , corporate_tax_rate , debt_spread_damodaran_global , relevered_beta ) Note that these files, and the repository more broadly, also cover climate-relevant sectors not included in the paper (e.g., vehicle or heat pump manufacturing), applying the paper's methodology to support modelers interested in other sectors. If you have any questions about these data files and how to use them for your own research, reach out to the corresponding author. Data sources and usage terms: - Damodaran data: Aswath Damodaran, Stern School of Business, New York University ( https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/ ). Use and redistribution permitted subject to Damodaran's usage rules; commercial resale of the data is not permitted. - World Bank data: World Bank,  World Development Indicators , CC BY 4.0. - Individual PwC corporate tax rates: PwC,  Worldwide Tax Summaries ( https://taxsummaries.pwc.com ), © PwC. All rights reserved. - OECD government bond yield data: OECD, Main Economic Indicators , accessed via FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Redistribution permitted subject to OECD attribution requirements.

summary: The present study characterised the environmental status of Tortugas Bay (Casma, Peru) by integrating biological indices with physicochemical variables, drawing on analyses of subtidal macrobenthic assemblages and water-column conditions. Sam-pling was undertaken at six stations spanning a gradient of anthropogenic pressure across three contrasting seasonal periods in 2023; sediments and benthic macrofauna were collected using a Van Veen grab and processed according to standardised pro-tocols. Biodiversity metrics (species richness and abundance, together with Shannon, Simpson, Pielou and Margalef indices) were computed, and multivariate approaches (PCA, nMDS and PERMANOVA) were employed. The results indicated a pronounced spatial gradient of sediment organic enrichment, peaking at station E-01 (5.20 ± 0.32%) and reaching a minimum at E-06 (1.70 ± 0.50%), with an inverse association to water transparency (1.77 ± 0.23 m at E-01 versus 3.10 ± 0.27 m at E-04). Principal component analysis accounted for 57% of the overall environmental variability and identified sediment organic matter as the dominant structuring driver. Stations subject to greater organic enrichment displayed elevated abundances (up to 512 individuals) alongside reduced diversity (H′ = 2.00) and evenness (J′ = 0.67), whereas comparatively open and better-flushed stations supported assemblages that were both more diverse and more evenly distributed (H′ up to 2.50). Collectively, the integrated use of biological indices and multivariate analyses yielded a robust appraisal of the bay’s environmental con-dition and established a sound baseline for long-term monitoring and sustainable management.
title: BIOLOGICAL INDICES TO CHARACTERIZE THE ENVIRONMENTAL STATE OF A MARINE ECOSYSTEM SUBJECTED TO ANTHROPOGENIC PRESSURE

summary: Computational supplement for the preprint: "Relative Ternary Defect Dynamics in the Accelerated Collatz Inverse Relation" This release contains the code and reproducibility material used to audit finite instances of the main constructions in the manuscript, including: inverse-family identities; exact relative-defect recurrence; local lift-defect isometry; finite triangular bijection; countdown and recharge identities; layered-state and finite-horizon closure; precision lower-bound examples; finite-state obstruction examples; randomized and exhaustive counterexample searches. The computations are intended for reproducibility and falsification support. They do not replace the mathematical proofs and do not constitute a proof of the Collatz conjecture. This release corresponds to the code version cited in the manuscript.
title: FontesJVC/collatz-relative-defect-dynamics: Collatz Relative Defect Dynamics

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a Structured PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22737224 . Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes It explains the problem properly, namely the need for reliable methods for miRNA analysis, as RNA-seq methods are not able to account for its specific characteristics. It also points out the gaps in prior benchmarking studies, clearly identifying that a benchmark particularly for normalization and differential expression has not been performed before, especially one incorporating recently developed methods. Lastly, it clearly states its aim and overall approach. Are the methods well-suited for this research? Somewhat appropriate 1. Some methodological details are missing. PCA and heatmap figures (figure 1B and 1C) are presented in Results alone, with no explanation in Methods section. So no information on the input data (raw or normalized or log), if it was scaled, the miRNAs selection criteria, or what clustering methods were applied. Due to this, the reproducibility of the paper is affected. 2. The paper frames as evaluating a broad range of normalization strategies but just tests only two types: within-sample scaling (RPM, RPM_total, MAP) and cross-sample (DESeq2,TMM). Other options such as quantile normalization or compositional data methods were not tested. 3. An uneven comparison in the differential expression benchmark, two different input data types used. Most methods use miRNA-level count matrix whereas miRglmm uses isomiR-level count matrix. Still, the authors do not address whether miRglmm's strong performance is due to the model or input data. 4. The underlying logic for the ground truth is circular. The authors state that DE ground truth is defined by "monotonicity trends derived from RPM values". But RPM is what they recommend for normalization. So ranking other tools against a baseline that uses their preferred method creates a feedback loop that is not validated against any independent benchmark. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported 1. The paper relies almost entirely on monotonicity as the ground-truth signal, across normalization, differential expression and log2FC tissue-specificity direction. While its limitations are acknowledged, its recommendations seem overconfident due to the narrow validation scope and too much reliance on a single criterion. 2. The authors identified pancreatic contamination in Mouse 3, clearly separating on PC2. They state that removing Mouse 3 did not alter the normalization or DE benchmarking results, but it is based only on supplementary figures and not present in the main text. So, it can not be independently verified. 3. In Results, the authors state that rlog-mean had the highest accuracy and precision for mixture proportions and the lowest error for technical replicate variability. But still the paper recommends RPM instead. The justification is that rlog-mean over-corrects the data by flattening variance between random non-replicate sample pairs.. But this relies on supplementary data and lacks quantitative statistical support in the main text. 4. No clear recommendation is made for log2FC estimation. The log2FC accuracy benchmark doesn't have a clear top method. Instead, the results show a sign-dependent split; RPM-FC and edgeR-v2 do better with positive log2FCs, and miRglmm and NBSR do better with negative log2FCs. The authors do not give a default recommendation for users. Are the data presentations, including visualizations, well-suited to represent the data? Highly appropriate and clear The visualizations are well-designed and logical for each analysis goal. These visuals communicate complex data patterns, like normalization trends and differential expression performance, in a clear format. Supplementary figure are a publication norm as well. summary: This dataset contains 44 synthetic event logs designed to benchmark process concept drift detection algorithms against existential-only dependency changes derived from the Activity Relationships Matrix (ARM). The collection is simulated using the Concept Drift Log Generator (CDLG) and custom python scripts, organized into five structural categories: isolated, surrounding activities, gradual, loops, and related conditions.
title: Dataset for Existential-Only Process Concept Drifts

summary: Data, supporting evidence, and scripts behind the quantitative results of the doctoral dissertation  Improving Refactorings in Dynamically-Typed Object-Oriented Languages (University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences). The package contains the 35 aggregate CSV exports of the Refazz evaluation (255,699 refactoring attempts over five Pharo projects), the catalog of 19 confirmed refactoring-engine defects with issue-tracker evidence and checksums, the transformation-reuse client counts for Pharo 11 and Pharo 14, the two jscpd 4.2.5 duplication reports, the table-generation and consistency-check scripts, and a README with provenance and reproduction instructions. The directory artifacts/rope/ holds a git archive of the Python proof of concept in the rope refactoring engine at commit 77b23b4d (upstream base dbc61cbc); rope is LGPL-3.0 and keeps its license. summary: Abstract When does a transformed presentation remain the same for a declared task, what evidence can establish that judgment, and what can a bounded observer safely do with it? This paper separates representation, evidence, control and implementation, giving each an exact mathematical contract. For declared transformations and required observations, contextual indistinguishability determines the greatest observation-preserving congruence. Its quotient is the coarsest lawful representation preserving every demanded observation under every permitted continuation. A reference–current construction applies this result directly to persistence judgments, including breaking outcomes and required provenance. An evidence channel determines the demanded distinctions extensionally exactly when its kernel refines the contextual congruence; failure supplies an indistinguishable pair requiring different answers. For explicitly presented finite systems, the paper provides quotient constructions, separating witnesses, supplementary-information bounds and exact finite-memory criteria. Under declared transition and observation semantics, robust safety is characterized by a greatest fixed point, with checkable winning and losing certificates. Suitable observer quotients preserve the safety computation. Finite controller enumeration and declared sensor catalogues yield exact bounded-memory synthesis and joint resource frontiers; adaptive acquisition is incorporated as action under explicit contracts. The paper also establishes incremental and transport laws, strategic comparison results, and conservative model-to-system safety transfer under stated coverage hypotheses. Representation minimality, safety maximality and bounded implementation attainment remain distinct. Extensional existence does not imply effective discovery or affordability, and mathematical guarantees do not establish physical correspondence. The results characterize what can be preserved, distinguished and safely controlled within declared regimes while exposing the additional assumptions required for implementation and deployment. This public edition updates the previously deposited v19.1 release. It clarifies editorial framing, historical review status and correction lineage while preserving the mathematical content. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.
title: Identity Persistence under Declared Transformations: Contextual Quotients, Evidence Attainment, and the Limits of Bounded Judgment

summary: Start here: Split-Zero Cohomology and Arithmetic Weight Control — the 821-page R62 paper . This is the reading preview; the accompanying public source ZIP is an offline download. The paper studies finite zero packets of the completed Riemann zeta function through the original theta-function source and its least-norm polynomial quotient metric. The R58–R62 continuation explains how periodized observations recover that specified source and how density arguments identify the relevant completed spaces. It then computes finite-circle curvature together with the quotient compensation terms, compares circle and critical-line observations through their explicit maps, and derives the residue-constituent first-derivative and curvature formulas. These calculations track the retained source, multiplicities, full mass, coefficients, constants, signs and orientations; they do not replace the arithmetic metric by a convenient surrogate. The finite identities and comparisons make the remaining growth problem more explicit. The uniform arithmetic growth estimate is still an active unresolved step: this edition is not a closure of the argument, a claimed proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, or a new Lean certification of the analytic estimates. Written proofs and recorded finite checks retain their distinct scopes. The complete proof/dependency hierarchies and 47 source witnesses remain available. This fixed cumulative PDF and public-source selection ends at R62. Later holonomy, TA, AT, AW and original-theta certification work is not included. The GitHub research sources provide editable sources and a separately scoped current-work index. All 36 files from the preceding 765-page edition remain separately downloadable with the same bytes, rights and notices. The public derivative documents historical locator aliases, narrowly identified internal-coordination excisions and the reference-only exclusion; the original owner archive is not a public payload. Public attribution and rights remain those of the preceding edition. Existing per-file notices are retained; no blanket licence over third-party material or source results is asserted.

summary: The IMEB-Exo Synthetic Benchmark Dataset is an open and reproducible dataset developed for the analysis of passive upper-limb exoskeletons, occupational biomechanics, human–exoskeleton interaction, and multicriteria biomechanical decision support. It provides deterministic synthetic time-series data and derived biomechanical indicators designed to support methodological validation, sensitivity analysis, benchmarking, and reproducibility of the IMEB-Exo framework (Multicriteria Biomechanical Exposure Index for Exoskeletons). The dataset represents 24 virtual anthropometric models evaluated under three simulated occupational task scenarios and two experimental conditions: without exoskeleton assistance and with a passive upper-limb exoskeleton. The data structure enables comparisons between assisted and non-assisted conditions across multiple anthropometric profiles, task scenarios, and human–exoskeleton interface regions. The time-series dataset includes normal and tangential human–exoskeleton interface forces, estimated interface pressure when a technically defined contact area is available, shoulder and trunk kinematics, exoskeleton assistance torque, joint reaction variables, muscle activation surrogates, and cumulative biomechanical exposure indicators. Derived variables include peak and mean force, 95th-percentile force, root mean square (RMS) force, force–time integral, loading rate, time above an operational load threshold, peak counts, projected occupational exposure, CRITIC objective weights, TOPSIS results, IMEB-Exo scores, biomechanical criticality classes (CCB-Exo), and rankings of human–exoskeleton interface regions. The repository contains: • deterministic synthetic biomechanical time-series data; • interface-level and scenario-level metrics; • IMEB-Exo scores and regional rankings; • CRITIC objective weights and TOPSIS outputs; • metadata for 24 virtual anthropometric models; • task and scenario definitions; • human–exoskeleton interface definitions and contact-area specifications; • generation parameters; • a structured SQLite database; • CSV and compressed CSV datasets; • Python scripts for dataset generation and IMEB-Exo calculation; • data dictionary and schema documentation; • SHA-256 checksums and file inventory; • representative figures and data excerpts; • reproducibility documentation in English and Portuguese. The dataset is intended for researchers working with occupational biomechanics, passive occupational exoskeletons, wearable robotics, ergonomic risk assessment, musculoskeletal modelling, multicriteria decision analysis (MCDA/MCDM), decision-support systems, synthetic biomechanical datasets, and reproducible computational research. Methodological notice: the dataset is synthetic and deterministic. The generated variables reproduce the expected structure and behaviour of an OpenSim-oriented musculoskeletal simulation workflow but do not constitute experimentally measured human data and must not be interpreted as direct outputs from an executed OpenSim simulation. The dataset should therefore be used as a methodological benchmark for algorithm development, reproducibility testing, sensitivity analysis, multicriteria modelling, and computational workflow validation rather than as experimental evidence of human biomechanical responses. The dataset was developed within the project “Multicriteria Methods for the Analysis of Monitored Data in the Use of Passive Upper-Limb Exoskeletons”, supported by FAEPEX / University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Grant No. 70262-26.
title: IMEB-Exo Synthetic Dataset: Time-Series Biomechanical Data and Multicriteria Indicators for Passive Upper-Limb Exoskeleton Assessment

summary: Clarifying dialogue can supply evidence about another person's interpretation while changing the interpretation being investigated. This paper develops a relational-history account of the resulting inference problem. It separates current coordination, retrospective attribution, and the prospective formation of understanding, while treating relations, histories, interpretive conditions, and response profiles as jointly constrained. A finite model retains paired initial and current candidate states through inquiry-induced transitions. Exact recovery of an earlier target requires constancy across the initial histories compatible with the complete dialogue transcript. A bounded adaptive-inquiry recursion characterizes when an allowed sequence of questions can achieve that recovery, and a constructive example shows how successful explanation can erase the discriminating opportunity while securing present mastery. Further examples distinguish historical ambiguity, response ambiguity, contextual error, and participants' interpretations of an investigator's expectations. The philosophical analysis connects first-person authority, interpersonal understanding, and the formation of shared meaning without identifying predictive success with access to another person's experience. A proposed study separates immediate correct responding, transfer, and retrospective attribution. The results are conditional formal consequences and conceptual distinctions; their psychological adequacy and the comparative merits of the proposed inquiry procedure remain empirical questions.
title: Theory of Mind in Clarifying Dialogue: Inferring Another Person's Interpretation from Relational History

summary: This white paper examines the operational, financial, customer, governance, and leadership consequences arising when customer-facing artificial intelligence makes a commitment the enterprise did not intend to make. The central argument is that a machine-generated promise becomes an enterprise risk when a customer reasonably relies on the output or when organisational systems allow the machine to act on it. The resulting exposure extends beyond hallucination into authority, workflow, customer reliance, execution, redress, and accountability. The paper identifies four escalating customer-AI risk states: Answer, Recommendation, Decision, and Commitment. Exposure increases when generated language moves from information into enterprise obligation. To govern this transition, the paper introduces the Machine Promise Control Architecture, structured around Authoritative Truth, Intent Classification, Authority Envelope, Verification Gate, Escalation and Redress, and Promise Telemetry. Three case studies demonstrate how machine output acquires authority in different operating environments. Cursor shows how generated language became perceived company policy. Rite Aid illustrates machine classification entering customer-facing operational action without adequate safeguards. McDonald’s and IBM demonstrate how conversational interpretation errors propagate into transaction errors, fulfilment problems, rework, and customer impact. Across all three cases, the common failure occurs when machine output acquires credibility, workflow access, decision rights, or customer reliance without corresponding control. The paper further separates AI authority into three distinct permissions: Say, Decide, and Execute. It introduces Promise Surface Area as an executive management model for assessing exposure based on interaction volume, promise-capable intents, authority scope, and consequence. It also applies Six Sigma disciplines through Critical-to-Quality measures, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, and the Cost of Poor Promise Quality, linking customer-AI governance directly to operating economics. The central proposition is that customer-facing AI should be governed as a complete decision system rather than as a conversational interface. Enterprises need explicit controls over what AI says, decides, and executes, alongside governed knowledge, deterministic verification, meaningful human escalation, decision lineage, promise-quality measurement, and structured incident recovery. The objective is controlled autonomy, with machine authority expanding only as quickly as the organisation’s ability to govern the resulting commitments.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 18 August 2026.
title: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 32: When AI Makes the Wrong Promise to Your Customer

summary: Research artifacts supporting the paper “Cybersecurity Investment Optimization Under Budget Constraints: From QUBO Formulation to Quantum Hardware”. This repository contains the source code, derived experimental instances, raw quantum measurement counts, QUBO/Ising models, QAOA execution outputs, transpiled-circuit metadata, backend information, job identifiers, and processed JSON/CSV results used to reproduce the experiments reported in the paper. The experiments implement an end-to-end cybersecurity investment optimization workflow based on a 0/1 Knapsack formulation transformed into QUBO and Ising representations and solved using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). The experimental design includes ideal simulation with Qiskit AerSimulator, architecture-aware noisy emulation using FakeKingston, and execution on the real IBM Quantum ibm_kingston Heron r2 processor. The artifact set covers the 12-qubit reference benchmark, the 20-qubit Safeguard-level stress experiment, and the real-hardware scaling series at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, and 156 logical qubits. For the scaling experiments, the decision variables beyond the original benchmark are explicitly constructed computational replicas used exclusively to evaluate circuit scaling, transpilation overhead, feasibility degradation, and real-QPU behavior; they must not be interpreted as distinct empirical cybersecurity controls. The repository preserves the information necessary to inspect and reproduce the experimental workflow, including optimized and transferred QAOA parameters, shot counts, sampled bitstrings, decoded cybersecurity portfolios, feasibility indicators, QUBO energies, circuit depths, gate counts, two-qubit gate counts, and real-hardware execution metadata. The public-evidence input dataset, CIS_MITRE_QAOA_Public_Evidence, is maintained separately on Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/andersonfpdossantos/cis-mitre-qaoa-public-evidence The dataset and these computational artifacts together provide the reproducibility package for the study. No claim of quantum advantage is made; the artifacts are intended to support independent verification, methodological replication, and further investigation of QAOA-based cybersecurity investment optimization.

summary: Recent advances in AI-assisted mathematical discovery, program search, and formal reasoning motivate a practical design question: how can a long-horizon open problem be reorganized into a broad, falsifiable, and evidence-accountable human–AI search? We present a prospective candidate-engineering framework, grounded in a source-bound retrospective Phase-I design case on arithmetic dynamical structures relevant to the Hilbert–Pólya programme. The paper does not claim a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a completed Hilbert–Pólya realization, or a spectral identification of Riemann zeros. The framework has three layers. In Layer 1, a mathematician fixes a mathematical origin, permitted data, and an admissible transformation class; the present case uses a prime-symbolic origin, whereas a new mathematician-supplied basic idea begins a new Layer-1 record. In Layer 2, mathematician and AI jointly draft and version-freeze an AGENTS.md contract specifying candidate identity, lineage, gates, controls, portfolio policy, and stopping rules. In Layer 3, bounded AI work returns a source-linked evidence handoff for mathematician review. The accompanying roadmap requires a single candidate to establish an endogenous arithmetic source, orbit/repetition ownership, and a same-object zeta or determinant before stronger analytic and operator obligations are considered. The case comprises one early exploration entry and five system-family sessions. Its P1 Wiki retains catalogued provenance records rather than a common score of completed papers, theorems, or Route advances. No source-bound top-level direction documents an integrated same-object A0+A1+A2 chain in one natural candidate. We therefore motivate a broader but lineage-filtered candidate portfolio, screened early for arithmetic, clock, and determinant ownership rather than assembled retrospectively from partial successes. The associated Wiki is a provenance and navigation resource designed to preserve positive local results, controls, scoped failures, and reuse boundaries for subsequent researchers.
title: AI-Guided Exploration of Arithmetic Dynamical Systems: Constraints, Failure Modes, and Search Strategies Toward Hilbert--Pólya Structures

summary: Circular economy is the trend that has emerged as an urgent necessity for manufacturing companies trying to break the linear "take, make, dispose" production cycle. While there is a significant amount of research happening in the circularity domain, the body of knowledge is split and does not necessarily connect with other theories, concepts and with application in different industrial sectors. The aim of this study was to develop an integrated conceptual framework to overcome the existing ambiguities in the field of CE and to facilitate further research while synthesizing the various streams of research on the topic. Methods: The articles were systematically identified from Web of Science and Scopus databases, and then snowballing was performed, in compliance with the PRISMA guidelines, between 2010 and 2025, and resulted in the identification of 100 articles. A tripartite analytical technique based on the use of quantitative bibliometric analysis, qualitative bibliographic content analysis and conceptual mapping was used. Results: The major thematic clusters that emerged were: circular supply chains, design for circularity, industrial symbiosis, Industry 4.0 enablers, policy and governance, performance measurement. The key practices of CE were identified and categorized according to the 4R and 10R frameworks, reverse logistics, industrial symbiosis and digital support for resource recovery at the micro, meso and macro level. The analysis shows that there are organizational, financial, technological and regulatory challenges that remain unaddressed, and that there is a significant lack of empirical evidence on a larger scale. Conclusions: There is a coherent conceptual framework linking CE principles with supply chain operations and Industry 4.0 technologies in this review and it proposes a prioritized future research direction that covers eight critical knowledge gaps. Government, industry and academia receive practical guidance on how to speed circular transitions in manufacturing.

summary: Assistance can make a person's decision possible while leaving the person vulnerable to interpretive substitution and control of the available options. This paper develops a framework for adult disability support when will and preferences admit several warranted interpretations. Decision authorship is distinguished from causal responsiveness, functional performance, legal capacity, the validity of a particular act, and responsibility. A set-valued model separates semantic fidelity from authority over support and menus. Conditional results characterize compatible outcomes under interpretive uncertainty, changes under additional evidence, and the limited relation between menu expansion and compatibility. Counterexamples show that reversing every expressed preference satisfies sensitivity, that a constant outcome can satisfy fidelity, and that accurate selection within a restricted menu can coexist with an objectionable exclusion of alternatives. A temporal extension distinguishes learning about an earlier preference from forming a present preference through support. A finite branchwise result identifies when clarification permits compatible implementation despite an empty initial intersection. The normative discussion confronts CRPD Article 12, the Committee's corrected General Comment No. 1, selected provisions of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, and a prior proposal for interpretive support. A fictional community-participation decision demonstrates the audit, including disagreement, refusal, revision and supporter conflict. The resulting framework makes uncertainty and authority answerable without converting mathematical compatibility into permission to decide for another person. Empirical validation and case-specific legal application remain open.
title: Preserving Decision Authorship under Uncertain Interpretation of Will and Preferences in Adult Disability Support

summary: Overview  This repository contains the dataset, preprocessing pipeline, surrogate model training scripts, NSGA-II multi-objective optimization suite, and raw experimental outputs supporting the manuscript: "A Leakage-Controlled CatBoost–NSGA-II Framework for Concrete Mix Design: Evaluation Protocol and Strength-Floor Sensitivity" Abstract Traditional concrete mix design usually involves lengthy empirical trial-and-error procedures. This study proposes a CatBoost–NSGA-II framework for multi-objective optimisation of concrete mixes, including leakage-controlled evaluation, uncertainty-aware strength feasibility, repeated-run robustness, and strength-floor sensitivity analysis. To evaluate the surrogate models, a source-study-grouped evaluation protocol consisting of ten repeated train–test splits was employed. The compressive strength model obtained only moderate performance (R^2 = 0.654 ± 0.062), whereas the RCPT model exhibited unstable performance (R^2 = -1.01 ± 3.07) and was therefore not included in the optimisation constraints. An uncertainty-aware lower confidence bound was used for strength feasibility, and the buildability constraints were incorporated into NSGA-II. For the 40 MPa case, 20 separate runs resulted in a robust 15-member Pareto front with an 86.7% recurrence rate. The mixture chosen had estimated reductions of 50.0% in embodied carbon and 22.7% in material cost as compared with a baseline that had the same strength. Nevertheless, the benefits decreased as the strength floor was raised and became statistically no different from zero at 70 MPa. Experimental verification based on physical tests is necessary before the approach can be applied in practice. Repository Structure  * 1_data/: Processed concrete mix dataset (processed_dataset_1867_records.csv) and RCPT sub-dataset (rcpt_subset_203.csv).  * 2_code/: Python codebase including data_cleaner.py, train_catboost.py, nsga2_optimization.py, and run_full_pipeline.py.  * models/: Serialized .joblib CatBoost surrogate model binaries and uncertainty parameters.  * results/: Raw Pareto front outputs across 20 independent seed runs (pareto_front_seed_42.csv through seed_61.csv) and consolidated multi-run front metrics.  * Root: reproducibility_manifest.yaml, data_dictionary.csv, exclusion_log.csv, and main entrypoint run_all.py. Instructions for Reproducibility  * Extract concrete_mix_zenoda.zip.  * Install requirements: pip install -r 2_code/requirements.txt.  * Execute python run_all.py to re-run data cleaning, surrogate training, and multi-objective optimization.

title: Data and Code Artifacts for "A Leakage-Controlled CatBoost–NSGA-II Framework for Concrete Mix Design: Evaluation Protocol and Strength-Floor Sensitivity"

summary: This replication package contains the data, R scripts, figures, and documentation used in the study “Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025.” The study examines the temporal structure of naval procurement competition between Turkey and Greece using annual data for 1990–2025. The main empirical series are derived from the SIPRI Arms Transfers Database and SIPRI Transfer Register. Annual Ships Trend Indicator Value (TIV) data are used to measure international naval platform deliveries, while order-year information is used to distinguish procurement decisions from subsequent deliveries. World Bank World Development Indicators are used for the macroeconomic control variable. The analysis tests contemporaneous and 1–3-year lagged relationships between Greek and Turkish naval procurement. summary: Environmental awareness involves understanding the fragility of the environment and the importance of its protection. As population growth, industrialization, and urbanization continue to intensify, natural resources are increasingly threatened, leading to environmental challenges such as pollution, climate change, global warming, acid rain, and ecosystem degradation. This study examined the correlates of students’ beliefs on environmental protection, focusing on awareness, compliance, and selected sociodemographic factors. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed involving 938 students from the different colleges of Cagayan State University–Carig Campus, the largest campus in terms of student population. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), Pearson product-moment correlation, and multiple linear regressions. Results revealed that students exhibited a high level of beliefs regarding environmental issues and concerns, with an overall weighted mean of 3.87. Among the dimensions assessed, environmental concern obtained the highest rating (x̄= 4.26), followed by environmental attitude (x̄= 4.09), green consumption (x̄= 3.95), and economic growth control (x̄= 3.84), while anthropocentric beliefs were rated at a moderate level (x̄= 3.21). Significant differences in environmental beliefs were observed across year level ( p = 0.003), nationalism ( p  < 0.001), religiosity ( p  < 0.001), expectation in life ( p = 0.001), and expectation in the future ( p = 0.041), but not across gender ( p = 0.235) and college affiliation ( p = 0.095). Furthermore, environmental awareness, compliance, nationalism, year level, awareness of environmental management laws, and level of satisfaction significantly predicted students’ beliefs regarding environmental protection. published by the Journal of Biodiversity and Environmental Sciences | JBES
title: Correlates of students' beliefs on environmental protection: Awareness, compliance, and sociodemographic influences

summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.

summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. u) plane as carrying a generic architecture boundary without deriving that boundary from an absorbing-failure model. The present version replaces that claim with an exact first-passage selector and identifies the conditions under which specialist, mixed, generalist, and variance-rescue regimes occur.

summary: Sanitized code and data reproducibility package for a manuscript currently under double-blind review at the Journal of Information Security and Applications. Author identity is withheld pending the outcome of review. The package contains two independently generated archives: (1) model-I-single-branch/ — a single clock-controlled ternary LFSR generator over GF(3) (controller LFSR A + data LFSR B), together with its exact period and design-condition checkers, a statistical analysis suite, a 14-family ternary long-sequence test battery, and a cryptanalytic attack suite (basic correlation, embedding, fast correlation, Berlekamp-Massey reconstruction, and a linear-consistency/clock-control attack). Includes all 40 archived experiment runs across 8 controller/data degree configurations. (2) model-II-three-branch/ — a three-branch clock-controlled generator over GF(3) combined through a quadratic nonlinear ternary function, together with period/design analysis, algebraic/spectral characterization of the combiner, an aggregate statistical pipeline, avalanche diffusion experiments, a matched attack suite, and an exact key-stream-reuse detector. A full SHA-256 manifest (MANIFEST_SHA256.tsv) and verification script (verify_checksums.py) are included to allow integrity checking of every file. See README.md for directory structure, provenance notes, a documented anonymity sanitization log, and instructions to reproduce all reported results. See CORRESPONDENCE.md for a mapping between source files and the tables/figures of the manuscript. Source code (*.py, *.bat) is released under the MIT License. Generated data, results, logs, CSV aggregates, and figures are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).

summary: An interface standard is advisory when nothing checks conformance to it, and normative when an external mechanism does. Python's public-interface convention is advisory: PEP 8 recommends that a library declare which symbols are contractual, but nothing enforces it, unlike Java, C++, or Rust. Every library therefore ships two surfaces at once — the declared surface it intends to support and the reachable surface clients can and do import — yet no prior work has measured how much of a library's surface is declared, how much of what clients consume is undeclared, or whether declaration predicts stability. We formalise a five-tier declaration ladder, computable statically from a distribution artifact, and measure it across 163 widely used libraries (81 AI/ML, 82 general-purpose controls) over up to 12 minor releases, together with a uniform sample of 30,000 PyPI projects yielding 14,213 client wheels and 12,704 clients contributing 419,752 import edges. The declared surface is tiny (only 7.4% of reachable symbols); clients over-select it by 5.9×, yet 56.5% (45.3% after a recall correction) of consumed edges remain undeclared, affecting 80.2% of client packages, though clients respect the underscore convention far more than __all__. Declaration status does predict removal — undeclared symbols disappear 1.5–2.5× as often as declared ones — and the AI/ML stack is not worse at signalling than general-purpose Python, only larger and faster-moving. The result is a repeatable, low-cost measurement that a standardisation process could run every release to check whether its own advisory recommendations are being followed.

summary: Dark Forest arguments commonly reduce interstellar strategy to a bilateral encounter between two persistent civilisations. A galaxy, however, is an open population in which civilisations enter, disappear, form selective relationships and occupy a spatially constrained network. This paper develops a continuous-time Galactic Network Formation Game integrating demographic turnover, endogenous trust links, directed hostile reach, coalition formation, causal delay and extinction cascades. Civilisations arise at vacant sites and disappear through baseline, predatory and coordination hazards. Pairwise-stable trust links possess an exact distance threshold expressed with the Lambert W function. In a homogeneous three-dimensional field, the model derives a critical entry rate for formation of a giant trusted component. Coalition governance is constrained by a causal-diameter bound, which can make several galactic cliques necessary even when a topological giant component exists. A congestion-security payoff yields conditions for a unique locally stable coalition size. Coalition survival under random or targeted extinction is represented by core pruning, with closed mean-field equations for cascade size. Numerical illustrations reveal sparse archipelagos, brittle cliques, resilient cliques and temporally admissible federations. Cosmic silence, cooperation and pre-emption are therefore network-level outcomes rather than universal consequences of uncertainty.
title: From Two Players to a Galactic Network: Entry, Extinction, Coalitions, Cliques and Spatial Topology in Interstellar Strategic Interaction

summary: Reproducibility package supporting an analysis of sustainability transition in Sarawak, Malaysia. The repository contains curated analytical and processed datasets, acquisition and processing notebooks, model outputs, robustness analyses, figures, quality-assurance records, provenance documentation and detailed reproduction guidance. The research examines whether low-carbon development constitutes a sustainability transition when ecological integrity, biodiversity and climate-conditioned environmental vulnerability are considered alongside energy and development outcomes. The package contains 103 scientific files together with repository control documentation. Eleven public-facing scientific files were prepared as portability-safe or publication-safe copies without changing the underlying scientific results. Three RQ5 outputs carry explicit provenance warnings because their original computational specification could not be fully reconstructed; these limitations are transparently documented. Third-party and derived datasets remain governed by their original licensing and attribution terms.

The repository contains curated analytical and processed datasets, acquisition and processing notebooks, model outputs, robustness analyses, figures, quality-assurance records, provenance documentation and detailed reproduction guidance. The research examines whether low-carbon development constitutes a sustainability transition when ecological integrity, biodiversity and climate-conditioned environmental vulnerability are considered alongside energy and development outcomes. The package contains 103 scientific files together with repository control documentation. Eleven public-facing scientific files were prepared as portability-safe or publication-safe copies without changing the underlying scientific results. Three RQ5 outputs carry explicit provenance warnings because their original computational specification could not be fully reconstructed; these limitations are transparently documented. Third-party and derived datasets remain governed by their original licensing and attribution terms.

summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.
title: BanglaVLP-5K: A Curated High-Resolution Image Dataset of Bangladeshi Vehicles and Licence Plates in Real-World Traffic Environments

summary: Sanitized code and data reproducibility package for a manuscript currently under double-blind review at the Journal of Information Security and Applications. Author identity is withheld pending the outcome of review. The package contains two independently generated archives: (1) model-I-single-branch/ — a single clock-controlled ternary LFSR generator over GF(3) (controller LFSR A + data LFSR B), together with its exact period and design-condition checkers, a statistical analysis suite, a 14-family ternary long-sequence test battery, and a cryptanalytic attack suite (basic correlation, embedding, fast correlation, Berlekamp-Massey reconstruction, and a linear-consistency/clock-control attack). Includes all 40 archived experiment runs across 8 controller/data degree configurations. (2) model-II-three-branch/ — a three-branch clock-controlled generator over GF(3) combined through a quadratic nonlinear ternary function, together with period/design analysis, algebraic/spectral characterization of the combiner, an aggregate statistical pipeline, avalanche diffusion experiments, a matched attack suite, and an exact key-stream-reuse detector. A full SHA-256 manifest (MANIFEST_SHA256.tsv) and verification script (verify_checksums.py) are included to allow integrity checking of every file. See README.md for directory structure, provenance notes, a documented anonymity sanitization log, and instructions to reproduce all reported results. See CORRESPONDENCE.md for a mapping between source files and the tables/figures of the manuscript. Source code (*.py, *.bat) is released under the MIT License. Generated data, results, logs, CSV aggregates, and figures are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
title: Reproducibility package for "Clock-Controlled Ternary Sequence Generators over GF(3): Exact Periods, Statistical Structure, and Cryptanalytic Comparison of Single-Branch and Three-Branch Nonlinear Architectures"

summary: An interface standard is advisory when nothing checks conformance to it, and normative when an external mechanism does. Python's public-interface convention is advisory: PEP 8 recommends that a library declare which symbols are contractual, but nothing enforces it, unlike Java, C++, or Rust. Every library therefore ships two surfaces at once — the declared surface it intends to support and the reachable surface clients can and do import — yet no prior work has measured how much of a library's surface is declared, how much of what clients consume is undeclared, or whether declaration predicts stability. We formalise a five-tier declaration ladder, computable statically from a distribution artifact, and measure it across 163 widely used libraries (81 AI/ML, 82 general-purpose controls) over up to 12 minor releases, together with a uniform sample of 30,000 PyPI projects yielding 14,213 client wheels and 12,704 clients contributing 419,752 import edges. The declared surface is tiny (only 7.4% of reachable symbols); clients over-select it by 5.9×, yet 56.5% (45.3% after a recall correction) of consumed edges remain undeclared, affecting 80.2% of client packages, though clients respect the underscore convention far more than __all__. Declaration status does predict removal — undeclared symbols disappear 1.5–2.5× as often as declared ones — and the AI/ML stack is not worse at signalling than general-purpose Python, only larger and faster-moving. The result is a repeatable, low-cost measurement that a standardisation process could run every release to check whether its own advisory recommendations are being followed.
tags: Python, advisory standards, standards conformance, public API, software evolution, empirical software engineering, machine learning.
title: replication package for Measuring Conformance to an Advisory Interface Standard: The Undeclared API Surface of the Python AI/ML Ecosystem

summary: Dark Forest arguments commonly reduce interstellar strategy to a bilateral encounter between two persistent civilisations. A galaxy, however, is an open population in which civilisations enter, disappear, form selective relationships and occupy a spatially constrained network. This paper develops a continuous-time Galactic Network Formation Game integrating demographic turnover, endogenous trust links, directed hostile reach, coalition formation, causal delay and extinction cascades. Civilisations arise at vacant sites and disappear through baseline, predatory and coordination hazards. Pairwise-stable trust links possess an exact distance threshold expressed with the Lambert W function. In a homogeneous three-dimensional field, the model derives a critical entry rate for formation of a giant trusted component. Coalition governance is constrained by a causal-diameter bound, which can make several galactic cliques necessary even when a topological giant component exists. A congestion-security payoff yields conditions for a unique locally stable coalition size. Coalition survival under random or targeted extinction is represented by core pruning, with closed mean-field equations for cascade size. Numerical illustrations reveal sparse archipelagos, brittle cliques, resilient cliques and temporally admissible federations. Cosmic silence, cooperation and pre-emption are therefore network-level outcomes rather than universal consequences of uncertainty.
title: From Two Players to a Galactic Network: Entry, Extinction, Coalitions, Cliques and Spatial Topology in Interstellar Strategic Interaction

summary: This work considers multi-agent coordination with arbitrary information networks among the agents using a game-theoretic approach. A system designer aims to assign local utility functions to the agents to guide their actions toward a desired system objective. The performance of the assigned local utilities is measured by the well known pure price of anarchy (pPoA) metric that equals the ratio of the system objective at the worst pure Nash equilibrium of the corresponding game to the optimal system objective. Our aim is to derive the utility functions which optimize the pPoA-based performance guarantees for any given information network and system objective. We develop a linear program that derives the optimal pPoA for any arbitrary information network and arbitrary system objective. Our work is the first to solve optimal utility design for arbitrary networks; our techniques generalize previous approaches which considered only the full-information setting. For supermodular objective functions, we prove that counterintuitively, a fully communication-denied utility design is optimal irrespective of the original information network. For submodular system objectives, an exhaustive numerical analysis suggests that the optimal utility design is robust to communication failures even for this case. When the system objective is weighted maximum coverage, the marginal contribution utility design provably optimizes the pPoA for a wide variety of information networks of interest.
title: Deriving the Pure Price of Anarchy for Networked Resource Allocation Games

summary: Traditional large language models (LLMs) are scoped to individual user sessions, limiting their knowledge to a single conversation and preventing them from learning user preferences that evolve over time. Existing agentic memory systems address this limitation but generally operate at the individual-user level, restricting the public knowledge that could be shared across users to improve downstream responses. We introduce AIM (Agentic Interoperable Memory), a unified, privacy-aware memory framework that enables multi-agent, multi-user LLM systems to persistently manage private and shared memory. AIM dynamically classifies information as private, scoped to one user and inaccessible to others, or public, accessible to all users. It enforces index-level access controls so that private memories are retrievable only by their owner, protecting sensitive data while allowing beneficial shared knowledge to improve coordination and consistency. We also introduce MUMBench (Multi-User Memory Benchmark), a dataset of multi-user interactions containing private and shareable information across four domains. To our knowledge, MUMBench is the first public dataset designed to evaluate multiple memory operations, including retrieval, creation, update, and deletion, in a multi-user environment. Across three independent runs on MUMBench, AIM achieves 96.0% visibility classification accuracy, 58.8% strict operation accuracy, and 70.5% state-aware operation accuracy.
title: AIM: A Privacy-Aware Interoperable Memory Framework for Multi-Agent Multi-User LLM Systems

summary: Periodic multilayer mirrors for X-rays require a layer period held to about 0.02 nm, set by deposition rates held in the laboratory's own notebook. A large language model agent was given a target multilayer specification and read access to a laboratory archive. Deposition recipes were authored in the native recipe language of a magnetron sputtering system and submitted through a Model Context Protocol bridge of 17 tools in three tiers, with enforcement held in the control application. The target was a 30-bilayer Ru/C multilayer with a period of 6.85 nm, a pair chosen because each period is fitted as two layers. The agent could write only inside a working project of its own, so it could alter neither the calibration it read nor the measurements that scored it. Mirrors were scored against a human-authored reference by X-ray reflectivity, and the 3% acceptance threshold on relative period difference was fixed before deposition. Across four scored agent-authored depositions the relative period difference fell from 20% on the calibration as given to 2.26% after one measured-feedback iteration and 0.79% after a second. Sixteen failure modes of the agent-facing interface were identified. The result is bounded to the period, pair and chamber observed.
title: Agent-authored deposition recipes for X-ray multilayer mirrors: schema-bound LLM control of a magnetron sputtering system with reflectivity-verified outcomes

summary: The paper studies finite-horizon ruin for an insurance company with several lines of business admitting heavy-tailed claims. The claim amount process of the insurance company is modeled as a multivariate increasing Lévy process possibly perturbed with fluctuations. A relevant insolvency event may involve the failure of a single line, of several lines at once, or of groups of lines linked through internal transfers, reinsurance, or a guarantee arrangement. These events have different geometries and need not occur on the same probability scale. Under asymptotic tail independence among claims from different lines, classical regular variation assigns zero limiting probability to a multi-line failure and is therefore unable to identify either the ruin probability or the corresponding solvency capital requirement. Using a multivariate Lévy process to model cumulative claims and regular variation on a nested sequence of subcones of the positive orthant to model dependence across lines, we provide the exact scaling rate of the ruin probability and the limit behavior. Additionally, explicit computations are presented for examples with independent business lines, common arrivals of independent claims, Gaussian copula dependent claims, Marshall-Olkin dependent claims, and bipartite insurance networks. Finally, we use Monte Carlo simulations to support our theoretical findings.
title: Multivariate Ruin in Lévy-driven Insurance Risk Models under Heavy Tails

summary: Question-answering often requires reasoning across multiple connected facts rather than retrieving a single isolated relation. Knowledge graphs (KGs) provide a structured way to represent such facts, but training large language models (LLMs) only on isolated KG head-relation-tail triples may limit their ability to learn the surrounding context needed for multi-hop reasoning. In this work, we propose a context-augmented training framework for multi-hop question-answering. Although generally applicable, we validate the framework in the context of disease-specific KGs, extracted using a reliable KG extraction framework called GraphMERT, for Gastroparesis and Diabetes. For each primary KG triple, we attach supporting triples extracted from the same source text chunk to form a context graph (CG). This creates two supervision settings: KG-grounded supervision, which uses only the target KG triple or path, and CG-grounded supervision, which uses the target KG triple or path together with supporting context triples. We train the Qwen3-14B model using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) under both settings, producing KGModel and CGModel variants. To strengthen the lower-hop factual foundation of the models, we introduce an LLM-judged, history-aware adaptive repair pipeline that identifies unresolved one-hop failures, continually fine-tunes on targeted repair examples, and removes or quarantines problematic noisy triples. This repair stage enables the models to reach 100% accuracy on the cleaned retained one-hop validation sets. Finally, we employ reinforcement learning (RL) using lower-hop question-answer items and evaluate generalization on harder 3-hop, 4-hop, and 5-hop tasks. Across both diseases, context-augmented supervision consistently improves multi-hop performance over KG-only supervision. RL initialized from repaired SFT checkpoints yields larger and more stable gains.
title: Repair Before Reinforce: Context-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Multi-Hop Question Answering

summary: Prompt-policy editing offers a practical way to improve agents that synthesize executable workflows without updating the underlying model. However, persistent prompt editing has two coupled properties. First, edit locality does not imply effect locality: an edit confined to one policy segment can ripple through downstream execution, altering behavior beyond the edited segment. Second, edit effects are composition-sensitive: edits that work in isolation can interfere after composition, causing one or both to lose their benefit or become harmful. Persistent adaptation must therefore support two distinct decisions: identifying where the policy should change from execution feedback, and determining whether the resulting edit remains safe to persist after composition. To address these challenges, we introduce RIPPLE (Replay-Informed Persistent Policy Localization and Editing), which separates where an edit is made from whether it remains safe after composition. It diagnoses failed trajectories, maps each actionable failure to a predefined policy segment, and restricts the correction to that part of the policy. RIPPLE then evaluates candidates against the same iteration-start policy to compare their isolated gains, before replaying promising edits after previously accepted updates to expose downstream effects and interactions. Only edits that remain safe under composition are retained. We evaluate RIPPLE on Flow-HO, a synthetic held-out benchmark for executable workflow synthesis. RIPPLE improves validation success by up to 23.1% and yields positive gains on two additional frozen language-model backbones, while maintaining edit efficiency and low execution cost. Targeted interaction analysis further demonstrates both properties: a segment-local tool-use edit changes downstream resource resolution and validation, while an edit beneficial in isolation becomes harmful after composition.

summary: Agent evaluations can be numerically correct while measuring a different construct from the one implied by their labels. We present a retrospective measurement audit of selected Praxa AI implementation files, historical evaluation artifacts, and operational records. A 139-case offline routing report contains 112 passes and 27 failures despite zero gating failures, because known gaps are explicitly exempted from the gate. An identifier-free export represents 8,843 tool-attempt rows: 8,395 recorded durations and 448 missing values. Of the durations, 121 equal the signed 32-bit maximum and carry abandoned-client labels; inspected database code clamps elapsed lifecycle age. The pooled recorded 99th percentile is 2,147,483,647 ms, versus 38,118.31 ms among server-observed completed calls. This is a stratum contrast, not a treatment effect. In a documented single-trajectory compaction pilot, the reported follow-up input reduction is 94.39%, but the reduction across the trigger and follow-up calls together is 46.54%. We reproduce the descriptive calculations, verify 91 timing statistics through a separate weighted rational-arithmetic implementation, and execute 13 scoring-function and 12 analysis-verifier tests. Finite-completion bounds show how missing durations limit all-row timing statements without imputing values. The contribution is a source-linked case study and reusable verification package for separating gate policy, lifecycle timing, and request-level accounting from broader agent-performance claims. Historical provider runs and the full current pipeline were not independently reproduced; general capability superiority and population-level statistical significance are not established.
title: When Agent Metrics Measure Different Things: An Evidence-Grounded Audit of the Praxa AI Pipeline

summary: From Wave Confinement to Recursive AI Instability: A Propagation-Correction Criticality Law and Successful Prospective Prediction Richard J. Reyes - September 14, 2026 YouTube:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q7Tr7GXvfMI This paper develops a mathematical bridge from Wave Confinement Theory (WCT) stability dynamics to recursive artificial-intelligence instability through a propagation-correction criticality law. Starting from the WCT Lyapunov framework, it derives a local rate-based description in which destabilizing propagation competes with restoring correction and identifies a dimensionless criticality ratio governing whether perturbations decay, remain marginal, or grow. The resulting framework is then applied to a previously frozen WCT/RCA prediction. A prospective stabilization ratio of approximately R_pred = 0.0100, specified before the later 2026 multi-agent incident analyzed here, is compared with an independently reconstructed event value of approximately R_2026 = 0.0104. The two values differ by approximately 4%. Established in the paper Propagation-Correction Criticality: R_u = mu_u / nu_u = tau_prop,u / tau_corr,u with local perturbation exponent lambda_u = nu_u(1 - R_u). Therefore, R_u > 1 <=> lambda_u < 0 R_u = 1 <=> lambda_u = 0 R_u < 1 <=> lambda_u > 0 The corresponding cumulative instability exponent is Lambda(T) = integral_0^T nu(t)[1 - R(t)] dt. Under persistent supercriticality, R(t) < 1, a finite instability boundary is eventually crossed within the stated dynamical assumptions. Successful Prospective Quantitative Prediction R_pred approximately 0.0100 followed by the later event-derived reconstruction R_2026 approximately 0.0104 corresponding to a relative deviation of approximately 4%. Key results The paper derives the RCA propagation-correction criterion directly from the local WCT stability framework rather than treating the two as a qualitative analogy. The stability boundary R = 1 separates restoring-dominated dynamics from propagation-dominated instability under the stated local-mode assumptions. The later 2026 incident exhibits growth of an unauthorized collective mode from a(0) = 1 to a(3 h) = 53, giving a net perturbation exponent of approximately lambda_net = 1.323 h^-1. summary: Proposed framework: A) Large-scale brain dynamics regulate energy balance by coupling ongoing physiological inputs. B) Cognitive performance depends on the alignment between neural metastability and fluctuations in peripheral energy, a relationship conceptualized here as Body Energy Coupling. Within this framework, metabolism is not merely a constraining variable; rather, it reflects a regulated, coordinated interaction between oscillatory processes in the brain and body. Cognition can thus be understood as an emergent property—or rebound—of metabolic homeostasis. If so, energy-constrained oscillatory systems would represent a universal organizing substrate for energy equilibrium. In the specific case of living systems with known cognitive capabilities, cognition would be understood within this framework as an emergent property of this dynamic self-organizing system coupling. From this perspective, vulnerability arises from a disequilibrium between predictive (or active inference) processes and energy homeostasis mechanisms, leading to maladaptive system dynamics. This view is still preliminary and exploratory, as there is currently no empirical evidence supporting this theory; rather, it serves as a proof of concept. Diego Lombardo. Cross-Scale Energy Coordination in Brain–Body Systems Supports Cognitive Function Across the Lifespan, 27 April 2026, PREPRINT (Version 3) available at Research Square [https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-9279633/v3] This repository contains a fully reproducible Python implementation of a generative brain–body–energy dynamical system designed to study how neural dynamics, peripheral physiological signals, and an internal energy variable jointly contribute to synthetic cognitive outcomes. The model uses coupled nonlinear oscillators defined on small-world networks to simulate large-scale neural activity, which is then bidirectionally coupled to a stochastic body signal and an evolving energy process. Within this framework, cognition is operationalized as a non-circular synthetic variable derived from the system’s ability to predict an independent external environment, allowing the separation of predictive neural dynamics, body–brain coupling, and energy regulation. The primary goal of this last V4 script version is to investigate whether meaningful cognitive-like structure can emerge from the interaction between brain–body coherence and energy-mediated neural modulation, while ensuring that any observed relationships are not artefacts of a single configuration or parameter choice. To address this, the model is evaluated under a systematic robustness protocol consisting of three distinct regimes: a baseline condition in which all coupling mechanisms are fully active, a perturbation condition in which stochastic noise is introduced into both physiological and environmental signals as well as coupling strengths, and an ablation condition in which energy–neural coupling is selectively removed. This design allows us to test whether the observed relationships between brain–body dynamics and synthetic cognition remain stable under biologically plausible variability, whether they degrade under increased noise, and whether they persist when key mechanistic pathways are removed. Across these robustness checks, the same core metrics are computed, including brain–body coherence, a forward-modeling predictability measure of neural dynamics, an internal energy state, and a synthetic cognitive proxy based on prediction error relative to an external process. Statistical evaluation is performed using Pearson correlations, mediation analysis to assess whether energy dynamics act as an intermediate mechanism, and permutation-based null models to ensure that indirect effects are not attributable to chance structure in the data.
